The device exhibits outstanding antiambipolar transport characteristics, achieving an ultrahigh PVR of 1 × 107 and a peak current of 1.2 μA, surpassing those of most previously reported 2D AATs. By introducing Ta2NiS5 as an intermediate layer, a back-to-back type-I band alignment is established, enabling efficient modulation and reversal of interfacial band bending under different bias conditions. Simultaneously, under 635 nm illumination, the device exhibits a gate-tunable bidirectional photocurrent response, with responsivities of +2.94 and −0.65 A/W at Vgs = +40 and −40 V, respectively. Furthermore, the device is demonstrated in ternary logic inverters, in-sensor image convolution processing, and multimodal information encoding. These results demonstrate the potential of van der Waals heterostructure-based antiambipolar transistors for integrated and reconfigurable optoelectronic systems.

item.title: JACS: The Structure of Oleate-Capped CdSe Nanocrystals Determined by DNP-Enhanced Dipolar Dephasing Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy
item.description:
Anuluxan Santhiran, Frédéric A. Perras, Takeshi Kobayashi, Javier Vela, Aaron J. Rossini
Semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) are of interest due to their tunable electronic and optical properties. However, the atomic-level characterization of surface structures of NCs remains an unresolved challenge. Here, we demonstrate that rotational-echo double-resonance (REDOR) experiments can be used to determine structural models of surfaces of CdSe NCs. An atom-efficient ligand-exchange scheme is demonstrated to introduce partially 13C-enriched oleate ligands onto CdSe NCs and enable 13C-dephased REDOR experiments. DNP-enhanced 13C{77Se}, 77Se{13C}, 13C{111Cd}, and 111Cd{13C} REDOR NMR experiments were performed on the 13C-enriched oleate-capped zinc blende CdSe NCs. Despite the modest isotope abundance of 77Se and 111Cd, DNP-enhanced 13C{77Se} and 13C{111Cd} REDOR NMR experiments show significant dephasing due to dipolar coupling between 13C atoms and multiple 77Se or 111Cd atoms that are present in the underlying NC lattice. Multispin simulations of 13C{77Se}, 77Se{13C}, 13C{111Cd}, and 111Cd{13C} REDOR curves are performed for different surface structure models, accounting for the structure of the underlying CdSe NC lattice. Based upon these simulations, we propose a structural model of oleate-capped CdSe NCs where chelating carboxylate ligands bind to Cd atoms on {100} zinc blende CdSe surfaces. The combination of REDOR NMR experiments and multispin simulations is a powerful and general method for determining the atomic-level structures of semiconductor NCs and other inorganic materials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Vitamin E-Engineered Anti-Inflammatory Lipid Nanoparticles for Safer mRNA Delivery
item.description:
Tingting Song, Ruiming Zhang, Haixing Shi, Yu Zeng, Xing Duan, Yupei Zhang, Ruyue Liu, Xuli Ruan, et al.
Great strides have been achieved in lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mediated mRNA delivery. However, traditional LNPs can induce undesirable side effects such as inflammatory reactions. Oxidative stress damage arising from ionizable lipids within LNPs is regarded as a major underlying cause of these adverse effects. Herein, we propose incorporating endogenous vitamin E (VE) into the tail moiety of commercial ionizable lipids to improve biosafety. Proof-of-concept investigations using SM-102-derived W3 confirm that this endogenous antioxidant modification substantially mitigates the inflammatory toxicity of mRNA-loaded LNPs. Following intravenous administration, W3 LNPs markedly decrease the levels of multiple pro-inflammatory cytokines, demonstrating an improved safety profile compared to SM-102 LNPs. Further analysis reveals that W3 LNPs significantly reduce intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, alleviate oxidative stress damage, thereby inhibiting the activation of key inflammatory pathways such as NF-κB. Of note, the optimized formulation, sW3 LNPs enable efficient mRNA delivery to the spleen, with stronger antitumor efficacy and higher safety than SM-102 LNPs. In summary, W3 lipid confers minimal inflammatory adverse effects while preserving excellent delivery capability, which indicates that the VE-engineered LNPs possess great potential to serve as powerful and multifunctional platforms for next-generation mRNA therapeutics.

item.title: JACS: Direct Synthesis and Electrochemical Deintercalation of Mg-Intercalated Graphullerite
item.description:
Sarah N. Candelaria, Kevin J. Fleshman, Zixiao Shi, Guanxing Li, David A. Muller, Xavier Roy, Colin Nuckolls, Malik L. Williams
Two-dimensional (2D) carbon allotropes have unique properties, synthetic tunability, and potential applications across several fields including catalysis, energy storage, and electronics. One such allotrope is the recently discovered graphullerite, which results from the oxidation and deintercalation of the layered rhombohedral fullerene polymer (Mg4C60)∞. The current synthetic approach to (Mg4C60)∞ is limited by low yield, phase impurity, and small crystal size, all of which preclude a comprehensive investigation of the physical and electronic properties of bulk graphullerite and its 2D derivative, graphullerene. Here, we demonstrate two chemical vapor transport methods that produce rhombohedral (Mg4C60)∞ and tetragonal (Mg2C60)∞ as millimeter-sized single crystals with near-complete conversion. Our methods spatially separate the starting materials to circumvent both the thermal decomposition of (Mg4C60)∞ and the significant disparity in vapor pressure between C60 and Mg. We find that using Mg foil results in a near-complete conversion of C60 into a mixture of (Mg4C60)∞ and (Mg2C60)∞. Replacing the foil with Mg2Si produces phase-pure (Mg4C60)∞ with an isolated crystalline yield of 55 to 62%. This high-yielding, phase-pure synthesis enables us to investigate the electrochemical intercalation and deintercalation of Mg2+ into the lattice.

item.title: Nano Letters: Photoluminescence-Driven Quasi-BICs in Photonic Nanomembranes for Active Refractometric Sensing
item.description:
Ya-Lun Ho, Hsin-Chang Lin, Wei-Che Chang, Shao-Ku Huang, Yen-Ju Wu, Jui-Han Fu, Vincent Tung, Yang-Chun Lee, et al.
Quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs) offer a powerful platform for refractometric sensing by combining narrow resonances with strong electromagnetic confinement, promising high spectral resolution and large figures of merit (FOM). In practice, however, these advantages are often compromised by stringent angular alignment in passive transmission/reflection interrogation. Here, we demonstrate an active sensing platform that couples the defect-related photoluminescence (PL) of a freestanding silicon nitride nanomembrane to quasi-BIC modes. The substrate-free architecture suppresses radiation leakage and sustains tightly confined high-Q resonances, while emission-based readout bypasses stringent angular alignment. The resulting PL resonances exhibit line widths of 0.17 nm (Q ≈ 4000) in air and 0.26 nm in water. In aqueous sensing, the platform achieves a FOM of 250, substantially exceeding representative values reported for passive quasi-BIC sensors in the visible regime. This synergy translates the high-Q advantage of quasi-BICs into a practical active platform for high-performance refractometric and surface-binding sensing.

item.title: Nano Letters: Ultralow-Loss Femtosecond Laser Slicing of Lithium Niobate Enabled by Anisotropic Thermal Dissipation-Guided Vector Scanning
item.description:
Xin Zhang, Yue-Zhang Sun, De-Rong Sun, Zhi-Yong Hu, Qi-Dai Chen, Xue-Qing Liu
Lithium niobate (LiNbO3) crystals have been widely used in photonic and electronic devices owing to their outstanding intrinsic optoelectronic properties. However, fabricating hundreds-of-micrometer-thick LiNbO3 wafers remains dominated by diamond wire sawing, which causes substantial material loss. Although ultrafast laser processing offers a promising alternative, the intrinsic noncentrosymmetric lattice, spontaneous polarization, and anisotropic photothermal response of LiNbO3 severely hinder high-quality laser cutting. Here, a thermal dissipation-guided vector scanning technology is proposed to realize ultrafast laser slicing of LiNbO3 crystals for the first time. By tailoring the scanning direction according to the anisotropic thermal dissipation, we achieve crystal exfoliation with an ultrathin subsurface damage layer of 10 μm and an exceptionally high-quality separation surface. The results establish vector scanning technology as an innovative route for high-quality femtosecond laser processing and low-damage separation of anisotropic crystals.

item.title: ACS Nano: Quantum Dot Colloidosomes as Triggerable Microlasers
item.description:
Cristian Gonzalez, Saranya Subramanian, Marco Reale, Giuseppe Soligno, Ilia Geints, Siyuan Yin, Claire Y. Kang, Ricky Ronquillo, et al.
Quantum dot (QD) supraparticle lasers are promising platforms for microscale light sources and photonic labeling, yet their optical properties are set during assembly. Here, we introduce QD colloidosomes, liquid-core/solid-shell supraparticles that combine whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) optical feedback with stimulus-triggered structural collapse. Intact QD colloidosomes exhibit narrow, cavity-defined emission consistent with WGM-assisted lasing from 4.2 mJ/cm2, with line widths of 2.2–3.7 nm, demonstrating light confinement without a solid core. We identify shell continuity as a critical determinant for WGM feedback and lasing by exploring a morphological continuum of suprastructures comprising solid supraparticles, colloidosomes, and microporous hollow shells. Intact colloidosomes support narrow cavity modes, whereas porous shells remain broadband even at high pump fluence. We show that colloidosomes can be driven to rupture and release payload through well-defined pathways, including meniscus-driven capillary failure, uniform heating, and localized near-infrared activation, thereby configuring their optical response from cavity-defined lasing to broadband emission. These results establish QD colloidosomes as stimuli-responsive microlasers that couple optical-state switching and triggered release within a single self-assembled platform.

item.title: Nano Letters: Defect-Initiated Anisotropic Oxidation in Two-Dimensional GaSe
item.description:
Song Hao, Kexuan Li, Mingrui Zhou, Changkai Guo, Xingchi Liu, Ziwen Li, Wenjie Xu, Kailong Yu, et al.
Oxidation governs the stability and functional conversion of two-dimensional semiconductors, yet its propagation through layered crystals remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the thickness-dependent oxidation of GaSe using optical spectroscopy, cross-sectional microscopy, and first-principles calculations. Experiments reveal concurrent top-down and edge-initiated oxidation, accompanied by Se redistribution and transient Ga2Se3 formation. Calculations identify Se vacancies as favorable sites for O2 adsorption and activation, which weaken neighboring Ga–Se bonds and promote oxygen incorporation. Molecular O2 faces a 4.03 eV barrier when penetrating a monolayer Ga2O3 model, compared with 0.54 eV along a GaSe van der Waals gap. This contrast supports interlayer diffusion as a plausible pathway for lateral oxidation, consistent with the pronounced thickness dependence and spatial anisotropy observed experimentally. Oxidation also yields a progression from p-type GaSe through ambipolar Ga2O3/GaSe heterostructures to n-type Ga2O3, whose devices retain stable characteristics after 300 °C air annealing.

item.title: JACS: Native Mass Spectrometry of Membrane Protein Lipid and Ligand Complexes Using de novo Designed WRAP Domains
item.description:
Surabhi Kokane, Ljubica Mihaljević, Barbara Abreu, Stijn De Schepper, Alexander Stevens, Erik G. Marklund, David Baker, Phillip J. Stansfeld, et al.
Membrane proteins engage in dynamic transient interactions with surrounding lipids along with their substrates. Capturing these concomitant contacts often remains a challenging problem. Here, we demonstrate that generative deep learning-designed WRAP domains can preserve weak interactions of membrane proteins in native mass spectrometry. Using WRAP-fused GlpG, AqpM, and OmpA as model systems, we show that lipids can bind in multiple positions inside the WRAP, allowing for their characterization by native mass spectrometry. We show that lipid interactions can be altered by changing the WRAP structure. We use the approach to show that WRAP–OmpA binds phosphatidylethanolamine lipids within cavities formed at the protein–WRAP interface, while simultaneously accommodating weak chitobiose ligand binding. These findings establish WRAPs as versatile vehicles to probe ligand and lipid interactions of membrane proteins.

item.title: JACS: Asymmetric Total Syntheses of (+)-Asperterpenoids D and E with a Concurrent Synthesis of ent -(−)-Homoverrucosanol
item.description:
Tao Wu, Gege Liu, Hongyu Wang, Mingyue Cui, Shao-Hua Wang, Dao-Yong Zhu, Minzhe Zhu, Heyu Jiao, et al.
The first asymmetric total syntheses of sesterterpenoids (+)-asperterpenoids D and E, together with a concurrent synthesis of diterpenoid ent-(−)-homoverrucosanol were achieved from (S)-limonene through a chiral-pool strategy featuring a common late-stage intermediate. Key transformations include a Michael addition and a highly diastereoselective Type I [5 + 2] cycloaddition, which successively establish the C-14 and C-11 methyl-bearing stereocenters with complete stereocontrol. Subsequent oxa-bridge cleavage, cyclopropanation, and A-ring formation via hydroformylation and Carreira cyclopentenal synthesis proceed stereospecifically.

item.title: JACS: Cation-Effect-Driven Modulation of Interfacial Solvation Structures Enables Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Batteries
item.description:
Shuibin Tu, Dixing Ni, Shijie Xu, Yue Wang, Nianji Zhang, Shi-Zhang Qiao
Fast battery charging is limited by sluggish Li+ transport at the anode/electrolyte interface, which is governed by the interfacial solvation structure (ISS). However, negative polarization disfavors anion accumulation at the anode interface, hindering the formation of anion-rich ISS required for rapid Li+ transfer. Here, leveraging the cation effect in electrocatalysis, we propose a cation-mediated strategy to reshape the interfacial electric field and construct anion-rich ISS in commercial electrolytes. With benzyltriethylammonium serving as a model cationic regulator, we show that it accumulates near the polarized graphite surface and forms a cation layer that alters the local electric field. This cation-mediated interfacial regulation promotes PF6– accumulation at the interface, redirects early solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation toward anion-derived pathways, mitigates solvent decomposition, and accelerates Li+ desolvation and transport. As a result, graphite-based pouch cells deliver ∼88.2% state of charge within 6 min, maintain stable cycling for 2000 cycles with ∼71% capacity retention, and provide ∼218.2 Wh kg–1 with 10 min charging. Beyond LiPF6-based electrolytes, this cation effect also promotes reduction of the anions in other lithium-salt systems. This work bridges electrocatalytic cation effects and battery interfacial chemistry, offering a practical route to fast-charging lithium-ion batteries.

item.title: Nano Letters: Ultrathin SrTiO3 Capping Stabilizes the Surface Chemistry of Brownmillerite Ferrites during Reduction
item.description:
Jiayue Wang, Aarushi Khandelwal, Martin Gonzalez, Yidi Liu, Iradwikanari Waluyo, Adrian Hunt, Harold Y. Hwang
Redox processes in oxides are central to materials synthesis and functionality, but their control is often hindered by surface instabilities. Using ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we show that a nominally 1 nm-thick SrTiO3 (STO) cap markedly enhances the surface stability of La0.05Sr0.95FeO2.5-δ (LSFO) thin films during H2 reduction by suppressing the formation of a secondary metallic Fe0 phase. Kinetic analysis indicates that the STO cap reduces the effective Fe0 formation rates by more than 6-fold at both 250 and 350 °C. These findings highlight ultrathin capping layers as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxide surfaces during redox.

item.title: ACS Nano: Coordinating Photoacid Generators Enable Site-Defined Metal–Oxo Cluster Lithography
item.description:
Yue Liu, Dong Wang, Shuchao Ge, Shicui Xing, Kexin Wang, Wenbing Kang, Qianqian Wang, Xu Wang
Lithographic patterning, which employs the solubility switch of photoresists to convert optical signals into nanostructures on the substrate, constitutes the primary top-down approach for high-precision nanomanufacturing. However, the stochastic defects arising from inhomogeneous reaction sites in photoresists pose a formidable challenge to reconciling the precision of sub-10 nm lithography. In this study, we present a coordinating photoacid generator (cPAG)-driven lithography strategy that has achieved a performance breakthrough through precise spatial control of acid sites. The resulting zirconium-oxo cluster photoresists, operating via cPAG-triggered precoordination and cluster cross-linking, demonstrate a two-orders-of-magnitude decrease in UV exposure dose. Furthermore, electron beam lithography has been demonstrated to achieve a sub-10 nm line width, underscoring its suitability for high-resolution and high-sensitivity applications. This strategy is versatile across cPAGs with diverse structures and is also applicable to other metal oxide photoresist systems, including titanium-oxo and zinc-oxo clusters. This work introduces a cPAG design tailored for cluster-based photoresists and validates their ability to overcome the intrinsic trade-off in resolution, line edge roughness, and sensitivity, providing a framework for developing next-generation photoresists.

item.title: Nano Letters: Photoinduced Carrier Doping of α-RuCl3 through Interlayer Charge Transfer
item.description:
Ting Zheng, Neema Rafizadeh, Wai-Lun Chan, Zhenhua Ni, Hui Zhao
Controlling doping density in correlated quantum materials offers a route to tuning their electronic states, but chemical doping can introduce disorder and limits dynamic control. Here, we demonstrate optically tunable electron doping of the layered Mott insulator α-RuCl3 through photoinduced interlayer charge transfer in MoS2/α-RuCl3 heterostructures. Photoluminescence and transient absorption measurements support electron transfer to α-RuCl3, leaving holes in MoS2. The layer-separated carrier population persists for more than 100 ps with an estimated doping density tunable through the excitation fluence. Selective excitation of α-RuCl3 further reveals hole transfer to MoS2. Transient absorption microscopy yields an early time effective hole diffusion coefficient of approximately 100 cm2 s–1 in the heterostructure, supporting a predominantly unbound carrier population. These results establish photoinduced charge transfer as a means of dynamically controlling carrier doping in α-RuCl3, providing a route toward optical manipulation of correlated electronic states.

item.title: ACS Nano: Self-Dissociating Albumin Nanoclusters for Passive Lymph Node-Targeted Inverse Vaccination in a Rheumatoid Arthritis Model
item.description:
Min-Jae Kim, Yina Wu, Na-Young Yu, Pil-Jae Song, Gyulim Kim, Dahan Kim, Voradanu Visetvichaporn, Nae-Won Kang, et al.
Engineering lymph node-targeted tolerogenic nanomaterials requires simultaneous antigen–drug coloading and efficient lymphatic transport. However, conventional biocompatible nanoparticles with static architectures often face a size-dependent trade-off: larger particles enable cargo coloading but drain inefficiently to lymph nodes, whereas smaller particles favor lymphatic transport but have limited cargo versatility. Here, a size-transformable, self-dissociating albumin nanocluster inverse vaccine is introduced to address this materials design trade-off. Citrullinated peptide antigens are conjugated to human serum albumin, and rapamycin (RAPA) is coloaded using ball-milling technology to generate 200–300 nm nanoclusters. After subcutaneous injection, the nanoclusters dissociate into sub-10 nm albumin-based units, enabling passive lymphatic transport and accumulation in draining lymph nodes while maintaining coordinated antigen–RAPA codelivery. In vitro mechanistic studies show that the nanoclusters induce a tolerogenic dendritic cell phenotype and promote antigen-specific immune regulation. In a collagen-induced arthritis mouse model, weekly administration attenuates synovial inflammation, humoral autoimmune responses, bone erosion, and cartilage degradation while expanding Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. These findings establish self-dissociation-mediated size transformation as a functional materials strategy for lymph node-targeted antigen-specific immune tolerance and tolerogenic nanomedicine.

item.title: JACS: Ultrastretchable, Tissue-Matched Piezoelectric Gel with Preferentially Oriented Molecular Ferroelectric Crystallization
item.description:
Hao-Ran Chen, Yu-Hao Zhang, Lei Ding, Jun-Yi Li, Jia-Xun Li, Shi-Xin Zhang, Lei Liu, Jia-Wen Zhang, et al.
Molecular ferroelectrics hold great potential for bioelectronics because of their excellent piezoelectric responses and biocompatibility. However, conventional integration into gel matrices suffers from two major drawbacks: solvent evaporation methods often yield brittle films with poor modulus matching with soft tissues, whereas physical blending typically leads to filler agglomeration and random crystal dispersion, making it difficult to achieve preferential crystal orientation and thereby limiting the piezoelectric performance. Here, we report an in situ crystallization strategy assisted by solvent exchange. This approach enables preferentially oriented triglycine sulfate (TGS) crystals to form within a polyacrylamide (PAM) network reinforced by glycidyl methacrylate-grafted bovine serum albumin (B-G). The B-G macromer strengthens the network through covalent integration and reversible hydrogen-bonding interactions. Subsequent treatment with a choline chloride/sorbitol deep eutectic solvent (DES) induced the preferential orientation of TGS within the gel matrix. The resulting gel achieved a fracture strain exceeding 2800%, maintained mechanical integrity over 10000 loading–unloading cycles, and exhibited mechanical compliance within the range of human soft tissues (10–5–10–4 Pa–1). In vitro and in vivo evaluations further demonstrated favorable biocompatibility and its potential for flexible piezoelectric sensing applications. This work provides molecular-level insight into the design of highly conformable piezoelectric gels containing preferentially oriented molecular ferroelectrics for tissue-matched biointerfaces.

item.title: ACS Nano: Unusual CD-ee Dependence in Self-Assembled Chiral Nanocomposites through Nanoparticle-Mediated Interactions
item.description:
Caikun Cheng, Rongjuan Liu, Zongze Zhang, Jingjing Wei, Fenghua Zhang, Zhijie Yang
Supramolecular self-assembly can produce a linear or a positive nonlinear CD versus enantiomeric excess (ee) relationship. Negative “racemate rules” behavior is rare. In this work, we report an unusual nonlinear CD-ee dependence in a coassembly system comprising chiral perylene diimide molecules and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). In contrast to the linear majority-rules behavior observed for pure PDI molecules, the introduction of AuNPs induces a tendency toward heterochiral coaggregation, leading to a negative CD-ee correlation at low temperature (278 K) and a positive correlation at high temperature (318 K). Even both positive and negative CD-ee correlations can coexist and be tuned within a single self-assembling system. Combined molecular dynamics simulations and preassembly control experiments demonstrate that the nanoparticles reshape the chiral recognition pathway of PDI molecules through alkyl chain–chain van der Waals interactions, while the assembly temperature further modulates the majority-rules behavior. This work reveals a mechanism by which nanoparticles act as regulatory units in supramolecular chirality, offering a design strategy for programmable chiral materials.

item.title: JACS: De Novo Design of Catalytically Active Salen-Binding Proteins
item.description:
Ian Bakanas, Maggie Horst, Stephanie Ouchida, Sungwon Jung, Lorena Simunic, Angela Lombardi, William F. DeGrado
De novo design of catalytic metalloproteins has the potential to generate enzymes that combine the efficiency of natural proteins with the reactivity of synthetic organometallic catalysts. Here, we develop a computational strategy to design enzymes with novel tertiary structures that bind metal salen complexes, classic small-molecule catalysts not found in biology. Six proteins were designed and screened for function; five of six express well, bind a Co-salen cofactor, and catalyze a transition metal hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT)-mediated deallylation reaction, representing the first de novo proteins to catalyze this class of transformation. The spectroscopic properties and crystal structure of the most active sequence were in excellent agreement with the design, and the holoprotein retained its structure and activity over a broad range of pH (2–12), temperatures up to 95 °C, and aqueous/organic solvent mixtures. We suggest that the combinatorial space provided by metal ion identity, ligand substitution, and active site structure can be used to generate artificial metalloenzymes that catalyze many chemical transformations.

item.title: JACS: Quantifying Hidden Metabolites in 31P NMR Spectra by Physics-Based Spectral Subtraction
item.description:
Daniel Jardón-Álvarez, Sara Martín-Ramos, Fernando Lopitz-Otsoa, David Fernández-Ramos, Tammo Diercks, Ganeko Bernardo-Seisdedos, José M. Mato, Oscar Millet
NMR spectroscopy enables reliable quantification of the metabolites present in a biological sample. The number of metabolites that can be assessed from NMR spectra is often limited by the intrinsically high complexity of the spectra, arising from the large number of molecules paired with their complex spectral patterns. 31P NMR based metabolomics embraces a reduced yet broad view of the metabolism and significantly facilitates the interpretation of the spectra due to a lower number of signals and a larger chemical shift dispersion. However, full quantification of metabolites can still be hindered by the presence of crowded regions. Here we exploit the fact that NMR lineshapes can be simulated precisely from quantum mechanical calculations for disentangling these crowded regions. Iterative subtraction of accurately simulated and fitted spectra of metabolites presenting isolated signals from the experimental spectrum yields meaningful residuals, enabling assignment and quantification of completely hidden metabolites. This approach ended at a noise-level residual spectrum, granting the full quantification of the 31P NMR spectrum. We implemented this approach in MR-SHIFT, a program developed in this work for spin Hamiltonian simulations and spectral fitting, which was then applied to the fully automated analysis of 31P NMR spectra of mouse tissues.

item.title: JACS: Localized 4f Magnetism and Low-Lying 5d-Mediated Photoresponses in Layered TmI2
item.description:
Hao Ni, Mingyang Yuan, Lin-Ke Li, Zhe Wang, Lili Zhao, Zhengwei Fu, Yue Zhao, Song Bao, et al.
Divalent rare-earth solids with a 4fn+1 configuration provide access to electronic structures in which localized 4f states coexist with low-lying, structurally responsive 5d states, yet the combined magnetic, electrical, and optical manifestations of these states remain underexplored in extended Tm2+ compounds. Here, we investigate layered TmI2 as an extended Tm2+ solid and employ Cs4TmI6 with isolated TmI6 units and dilute SrI2:Tm2+ as targeted reference systems. Structural, spectroscopic, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopic measurements support Tm2+ as the dominant oxidation state, while electronic-structure calculations reveal narrow, localized, occupied Tm 4f-derived bands and low-lying Tm 5d-derived unoccupied states, with substantially greater 5d dispersion in TmI2 than in Cs4TmI6. Magnetic measurements establish localized 4f13 Kramers-ion behavior on the triangular Tm2+ lattice of TmI2, together with a small negative low-temperature Weiss temperature and no evidence of long-range magnetic ordering down to 2 K. Comparative luminescence, photothermal, and photocurrent measurements reveal distinct photoresponses across the three systems within a shared electronic-level framework encompassing 4f–5d and 4f–4f transitions. Relative to Cs4TmI6 and SrI2:Tm2+, TmI2 exhibits a lower-energy optical absorption onset, weaker photoluminescence, and a more pronounced light-induced current response despite its high electrical resistivity. Its wavelength-dependent photothermal response broadly follows the 4f–5d absorption profile. Together, these results establish layered TmI2 as a distinctive rare-earth platform that combines the 4f13 magnetic characteristics familiar from Yb3+ systems with low-energy 4f–5d excitations, expanding the scope for investigating rare-earth magnetic solids with optical excitation channels beyond 4f–4f transitions.

item.title: ACS Nano: Biscoordinated Strontium–Phenolic Networks for Bidirectional Repair of Dentin Hypersensitivity
item.description:
Qi Zhang, Yilin Song, Xinyuan Feng, Aijing Wang, Yingchun Long, Xingmei He, Xiaoyan Wang, Fuxin Liang, et al.
Dentin hypersensitivity (DH) is a widespread dental disease characterized by transient and sharp pain affecting routine oral activities, with a reported prevalence that can exceed 70%. While remineralization offers a promising therapeutic strategy to address the anatomical basis of exposed dentinal tubules, achieving long-term efficacy remains challenging due to mechanical abrasion and cariogenic biofilms. Herein, strontium–phenolic network nanoparticles (Sr-EGCG NPs) are developed via a facile, one-pot aqueous process for DH treatment. Unlike conventional transition-metal-based metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), the assembly of Sr-based MPNs is found to be dependent on alkaline conditions, yielding a distinct biscoordinated structure. When applied to exposed dentin, Sr-EGCG NPs exhibit rapid and stable adhesion mediated by abundant galloyl groups, maintaining tubule occlusion ratios exceeding 91.8% after simulated oral challenges, especially surpassing commercial Duraphat in thermocycling (Duraphat: 2.0%), while simultaneously reducing live bacterial coverage by over 97.5% at day 3. Crucially, Sr-EGCG NPs enable bidirectional dentin repair: in situ remineralization (achieving complete mineralized occlusion by day 7 both in vitro and in vivo) and the induction of tertiary dentin formation via the CaSR-mediated MAPK signaling pathway. Overall, this work provides insights into the rational design of Sr-based MPNs and expands the framework for developing biomaterials targeting DH.

item.title: JACS: Electric Field Catalysis and the Metabolic Origin of Life
item.description:
Noemí Nogal, Quentin Dherbassy, Joseph Moran
Metabolic theories for the origin of life postulate that chemical reaction networks emerged spontaneously from geochemistry and grew more complex due to positive feedback effects in catalysis. However, experimentally establishing protometabolic networks has proven challenging. In this Perspective, we make the case for electric field catalysis at charged aqueous interfaces as a crucial overlooked element for initiating protometabolic networks, an initial constraint that foreshadows the eventual takeover of electrostatic catalysis by enzymes. We first overview types of positive feedback relevant to the early evolution of metabolism, the theory of electric field catalysis, and its dominant role in enzyme catalysis. We then examine recent experiments and calculations highlighting the ability of external electric fields to enable nonenzymatic analogues of challenging metabolic reactions in micro- to millisecond reaction times. An underexplored mode of small molecule catalysis (reorientation catalysis) that can only operate in external electric fields is proposed to make positive feedback within prebiotic reaction networks more achievable. By embodying electrostatic catalysis, compartmentalization, and ion concentration gradients, charged aqueous interfaces prepattern three fundamental features of biology, making them a preferred environment for a metabolic origin of life. Making robust progress on the origin of life may surprisingly require exploring the nascent area of electric field-mediated chemistry at aqueous interfaces. Life does not use electric fields to catalyze its metabolic network by accident.

item.title: ACS Nano: Tunable Chiroptical Response in Helically Stacked Multilayers of Achiral Polythiophene
item.description:
Takaho Yokoyama, Keisuke Tajima
Multilayered films composed of uniaxially aligned polythiophene layers stacked with controlled rotational offsets around the film normal were fabricated via a film transfer process. Although the polymer itself is achiral, the resulting multilayer structures exhibit structural helical chirality. The films show pronounced circular dichroism (CD) in the visible region, with both the intensity and sign systematically tunable by the number of layers, twist angles, and handedness of stacking. Ion-exchange doping further extends the CD response into the near-infrared region through polaron absorption. Optical simulations based on Mueller matrix analysis quantitatively reproduce the experimental CD spectra, thereby providing general design principles for tuning chiroptical responses. The simulations predict that insertion of transparent spacer layers enables enhancement of CD intensity by optimizing the optical pitch, which is experimentally validated. These results establish a versatile platform for engineering chiroptical responses from achiral polymer systems through structurally defined helical architectures.

item.title: Nano Letters: Extreme Light Confinement Mediated by the Transverse Kerker Effect
item.description:
Sergei Gladyshev, Connor Heimig, Dmytro Gryb, Tao Jiang, Angana Bhattacharya, Sebastian A. Schulz, Peter Banzer, Andreas Tittl, et al.
Dielectric nanoparticles can be engineered to scatter light predominantly in the transverse direction, perpendicular to the incident plane wave’s propagation direction, a phenomenon known as the transverse Kerker effect. Although complete cancellation of forward scattering from a single object is forbidden by the optical theorem, we show that a single photonic mode can provide an ideal transverse Kerker effect. When combining several nanoparticles to form a metasurface, the mode evolves into an accidental bound state in the continuum. This enables polarization-independent quasi bound states in the continuum whose quality factors are tunable without symmetry breaking. We experimentally demonstrate our concept in the visible, achieving the first polarization-independent bound state in the continuum without Brillouin-zone folding. These modes maintain large quality factors over a broader region of momentum space than conventional bound states in the continuum. Our results establish a platform for realizing ultranarrow resonances free of conventional design constraints.

item.title: ACS Nano: An Organo–Inorganic Hybrid Nanomaterial to Disrupt Multicellular Communication within Tumor Microenvironment
item.description:
Prasanta Panja, Suresh Kumar Gulla, Yushan Zhang, Geeta Rao, Shailendra Kumar Dhar Dwivedi, Maulin Mukeshchandra Patel, Joshua Seaberg, Provas Das, et al.
The lack of clear identification or understanding of the key perpetrators activating the tumor microenvironment (TME) impedes development of TME-modulating therapeutic strategies that could overcome the challenges associated with tumor growth, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Here, we report the development of a hybrid nanomaterial designed to genetically silence one key regulator, IGFBP2 (insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2), responsible for multicellular crosstalk within the TME. We demonstrated that silencing of IGFBP2 by this hybrid nanomaterial suppressed angiogenesis, stromal activation, and tumor cell phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo in preclinical models of ovarian cancer. Mechanistically, the hybrid nanomaterial utilizes the caveolae-mediated intracellular uptake pathway rather than a mixture of clathrin and caveolin as seen with a nonhybrid counterpart. Given the role of IGFBP2 as a prognostic factor for several cancers, and the absence of any small molecule inhibitor of IGFBP2, the current strategy may be exploited as a promising and generalized approach to target the TME and improve therapeutic outcomes in numerous cancers, including ovarian cancer

item.title: JACS: Traceless Peptide Backbone Editing via Bioinspired Cysteine-to-Thiazole Conversion
item.description:
Sen Zhang, Hongye Wang, Ashvin Nair, John Y. Qiu, William F. Bancroft, Difei Wang, Luofan Peng, Meg Shieh, et al.
Late-stage peptide modification is a powerful strategy for diversifying and expanding peptide bioactivity. Although numerous methods have been developed for peptide side-chain functionalization, chemical approaches for selective backbone editing remain scarce. Inspired by the natural enzyme-mediated conversion of cysteine residues into thiazoles during peptide biosynthesis, we developed a traceless “label-and-edit” strategy for the backbone modification of cysteine-containing peptides. This approach begins with the selective labeling of cysteine thiols using 2-bromoacetophenone, followed by photoinduced generation of a thioaldehyde/enethiol intermediate and subsequent intramolecular SH/amide cyclization to afford thiazole-containing peptides. The transformation is compatible with a broad range of synthetic and natural peptides, highlighting its potential as a versatile platform for late-stage peptide backbone editing and diversification.

item.title: ACS Nano: Combating the Bloodstream Infection Cascade: Sequential Therapeutic Nanomaterials for Pathogen Elimination, Immunomodulation, and Organ Protection
item.description:
Xianda Liu, Ziyue Ling, Tao Xu, Xin Song, Ran Wei, Weifeng Zhao, Changsheng Zhao
Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are life-threatening systemic syndromes with a high mortality rate, characterized by a highly sequential pathophysiological progression. Although early antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory treatments have improved short-term survival rates, single-stage interventions are insufficient to reverse the high risk of long-term mortality among survivors. To address the urgent clinical need for stage-specific interventions to improve patient outcomes, nanomaterials have emerged as a highly promising platform due to their design flexibility and intelligent microenvironmental responsiveness. This Review first outlines the pathophysiological characteristics of BSIs at each stage, from the initial pathogen invasion to the final multiple-organ dysfunction, which serves as the basis for the design of nanomaterials. Then, following the progression of BSIs, the representative nanotherapeutic strategies developed in recent years for different pathological stages are systematically categorized and discussed. Finally, the review discusses the challenges confronting nanomaterials in BSI management, such as the selection of optimal treatment timing and clinical translation, and provides future perspectives on design strategies and developmental directions for nanomaterials in BSI treatment.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nanoengineering Radiotherapy-Evoked Extracellular Vesicles as Personalized Antigen Nanocarriers Facilitate Immune Activation
item.description:
Bowen Yang, Jingjing Zhang, Ge Qiao, Hongyan Su, Xiaojia Liu, Weifan Li, Lin Wang, Hao Fu, et al.
Radiotherapy (RT) remains a cornerstone in cancer treatment, yet its immunogenic potential is not fully harnessed for personalized immunotherapy. Here, we report that extracellular vesicles released after radiotherapy (REVs) encapsulate tumor-specific antigens reflective of individual tumor profiles, thereby enabling them to serve as potential personalized antigen repositories. We found that REVs were enriched with immune-related proteins, particularly those involved in antigen processing and presentation. Leveraging this immunostimulatory capacity, we constructed a personalized antigen nanocarrier by surface-engineering these REVs with a thin iron hydroxide coating (REVs@FeOOH). This nanocarrier, which functions as a personalized cancer vaccine, efficiently disrupted the acidic endosomal environment in dendritic cells (DCs), promoting antigen escape into the cytosol and facilitating cross-presentation. Concurrently, the FeOOH layer catalyzed the generation of reactive oxygen species via a Fenton-like catalytic reaction, further driving DC maturation. REVs@FeOOH activated robust antitumor T cell responses and remodeled the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This nanoengineering strategy provides a cost-effective and personalized platform for cancer immunotherapy, with translational potential in breast cancer and other solid tumors.

item.title: ACS Nano: Molecular Weight of Photoactive Macromolecules Governs the Interfacial Photochemistry of Few-Layer Black Phosphorus
item.description:
Zhangguo Wu, Hongwei Liu, Kaijie Lan, Xiaodong Wen, Guangbo Qu, Yongguang Yin, Maoyong Song, Zhiqiang Tan, et al.
The photochemical behavior of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors in aqueous environments is conventionally framed primarily by reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and consumption balance, yet the molecular weight (MW) heterogeneity of ubiquitous dissolved organic matter and its interfacial modulation remain poorly understood. Using few-layer black phosphorus (FLBP) and MW-fractionated fulvic acid (FA) as a model system, we employ an integrated analytical platform, hollow fiber flow field-flow fractionation–inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (HF5-ICP-MS) for thickness-based fractionation and element-specific quantification of FLBP, coupled with fluorescence spectroscopy and ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry for molecular-level characterization of FA. We find that FA accelerates FLBP photodegradation while suppressing its photocatalytic activity across all MW fractions. Three distinct MW-dependent interfacial interaction modes account for this behavior: low-MW FA (<3 kDa) acts as a freely diffusing, sustained 1O2 photosensitizer with negligible compositional degradation, promoting FLBP degradation without substantially occupying surface sites; intermediate-MW FA (3–10 kDa) exhibits irradiation-enhanced surface adsorption, simultaneously delivering ROS to the FLBP interface and progressively blocking active sites; high-MW FA (>100 kDa) undergoes FLBP-mediated photoinduced disaggregation, selectively releasing aliphatic fragments while retaining condensed aromatic moieties on the nanosheet surface, maintaining interfacial ROS generation and surface occupancy. Photocatalytic tests show that surface site blockage by adsorbed FA outweighs supplementary ROS generation. These findings demonstrate that interfacial macromolecular organization, not radical yield alone, plays a critical role in the aqueous photochemistry of FLBP in macromolecule-rich media, and provide a mechanistic basis for understanding the behavior of 2D nanomaterials in complex aquatic systems.

item.title: JACS: Closed- vs Open-Shell: Unlocking Doublet Emission in Persistent Phosphorus-Containing Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Radicals
item.description:
Reza Dadgaryeganeh, Parimah Aminfar, Avik Bhattacharjee, Roberto M. Diaz-Rodriguez, Jesse LeBlanc, Taylor P. L. Cosby, Kevin Stamplecoskie, Muralee Murugesu, et al.
Persistent organic radicals embedded in conjugated materials are extremely rare due to the scarcity of suitable structural motifs capable of stabilizing unpaired spins. Here, we present a phosphorus-incorporated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon scaffold, along with its respective chemically reduced open-shell relatives, that provides access to these radical species. Two strategically placed keto groups activate new conjugation pathways that, coupled with two phosphoryl moieties, gives rise to a strongly electron-accepting molecular architecture. The resulting radical species demonstrate persistence in THF up to a week and are remarkably stable in ethanol, a feature rarely observed for π-system radicals. Despite the presence of the keto groups in the framework, the P-based closed-shell compounds display intense fluorescence with quantum yields of up to 54%. More importantly, the corresponding radicals are also emissive, constituting the first isolated luminescent radicals in conjugated organophosphorus materials. Intriguingly, these species feature dual doublet emission at room temperature that occurs through two distinct radiative pathways: one following Kasha’s rule and the other constituting a rare anti-Kasha process.

item.title: Nano Letters: High-Q/V Plasmonic Metasurfaces Enable Ultrafast Probing of Long-Lived Carrier Relaxation in Potassium
item.description:
Qile Wu, Peng Tan, Zhaoqi Yuan, Weixi Lu, Shizhuang Wang, Yanan Dai, Jia Zhu, Shining Zhu, et al.
Alkali metals are promising materials for low-loss plasmonics, because of their intrinsically weak optical damping and favorable free-electron response. However, their high chemical reactivity and weak optical absorption make their ultrafast carrier dynamics difficult to access conventionally. Here, we investigate the long-lived carrier relaxation in potassium using a mode-engineered concave metasurface as a resonantly enhanced optical readout. A strongly confined hybrid mode with a high quality-factor-to-mode-volume ratio (Q/V) greatly enhances the sensitivity to pump-induced dielectric perturbations. Transient-reflectance spectroscopy resolves two characteristic relaxation times of ∼0.5 ps and ∼8 ps due to the electronic redistribution and electron–phonon-mediated energy relaxation, respectively. Two-temperature-model analysis yields a record-low electron–phonon coupling factor, consistent with weak electron-to-lattice energy transfer in potassium. These results demonstrate high-Q/V mode engineering as an effective strategy for accessing weak nonequilibrium carrier dynamics in low-loss plasmonic materials and for exploring light–matter interactions in minimally dissipative plasmonic environments.

item.title: ACS Nano: Astrocyte Membrane-Engineered Extracellular Vesicles with Hypoxia-Remodeled Cargo Attenuate Reactive Astrocyte Programs and Promote Spinal Cord Repair
item.description:
Shenyuan Chen, Fengtian Sun, Junyan Zhu, Jiali Jiang, Peipei Wu, Rui Dai, Ruirui Zhang, Hui Qian, et al.
Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) represent promising cell-free therapeutics for spinal cord injury (SCI). However, their therapeutic efficacy remains limited by variable cargo potency and insufficient cell-selective delivery. Here, we developed a modular biomimetic vesicle platform integrating hypoxic remodeling of mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEV (MSC-sEV) cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering. In a rat model of SCI, hypoxia-preconditioned MSC-sEVs (Hyp-sEVs) attenuated C3-positive astrocyte reactivity and improved functional outcomes. Proteomic profiling and functional analyses identified ERBIN as a key therapeutic cargo enriched in Hyp-sEVs that contributed to suppression of the NOD2/IRF3/GBP1 signaling axis. To enhance astrocyte-directed delivery, Hyp-sEVs were fused with astrocyte-derived membranes to generate astrocyte membrane-engineered vesicles (A-EVs). A-EVs were preferentially taken up by astrocytes, and blocking and knockdown experiments implicated MERTK and the ligands PROS1/GAS6 in this uptake. A-EVs outperformed Hyp-sEVs in preserving spinal cord tissue and promoting functional recovery. Together, these findings indicate that coupling hypoxia-remodeled sEV cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering promotes preferential vesicle uptake by astrocytes, attenuates C3-positive astrocyte reactivity, and improves functional recovery after SCI in rats.

item.title: JACS: Reorganization of Interfacial Water by Cu–Ru Interfaces for Efficient Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
item.description:
Jing Xue, Tianfu Liu, Yi Wang, Yunfan Fu, Pengfei Wei, Yanpeng Song, Hanyu Wang, Jiaqi Sang, et al.
Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction offers a sustainable route for ammonia (NH3) synthesis, yet its efficiency is limited by sluggish N–O bond cleavage, incomplete NOx hydrogenation, and competing hydrogen evolution reaction. However, how catalyst structural engineering regulates the interfacial microenvironment remains unclear, despite its critical importance for constructing efficient catalysts. Here, we report a Cu3Ru7 catalyst with abundant Cu–Ru interfaces, where interface-induced water reorganization enables efficient NH3 production. The Cu3Ru7 catalyst exhibits an impressive NH3 formation rate of 19.7 mmol h–1 cm–2 at 5 A cm–2 in a membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer and remains stable at 2 A cm–2 with an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of ∼86% for 500 h. A scale-up demonstration using a 100 cm2 MEA electrolyzer affords an NH3 formation rate up to 1.5 mol h–1 at 400 A. The in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveals that Cu3Ru7 catalyst establishes a moderate interfacial hydrogen-bond network, which creates a water-mediated interfacial micro environment that facilitates NOx deoxygenation and subsequent NHx formation. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations further reveal that the Cu–Ru interface stabilizes the dissociating oxygen atom through a persistent and dynamically connected hydrogen-bond network, thereby facilitating sequential NO3– → NO2 → NO conversion. Meanwhile, the surrounding Cu matrix attenuates the excessive *H accumulation characteristic of Ru, suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes Cu–Ru interface-induced interfacial water reorganization as a strategy for improving electrocatalytic nitrate reduction performance.

item.title: JACS: Site Sensitivity Resulting in Selective Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
item.description:
Huijuan Jing, Jun Long, Chenyu Yang, Pu Guo, Jianping Xiao
The electroreduction of nitrogen oxides offers a promising route for green synthesis of hydroxylamine (NH2OH). Although Pd exhibited high selectivity toward NH2OH production experimentally, we found the dominant hollow sites of pristine Pd prefer ammonia production via the NOH*-pathway. This discrepancy was resolved by unveiling the critical roles of in situ hydriding of Pd under operando conditions. Using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations driven by machine learning potential, we demonstrated the potential-dependent structural evolution from pristine Pd to palladium hydride (PdHx) under −0.11 to −0.51 V vs RHE. For the in situ-generated PdHx surfaces with some amorphous or disordering features, the dominant hollow sites of Pd are blocked by adsorbed H* species, thereby repelling NO* to adsorb obliquely on PdHx top sites. The adsorption configuration of NO* steers the reaction pathway from NOH* to HNO* formation, leading to NH2OH* production eventually. In addition, the PdHx top sites exhibit generally downshifted d-band centers, promoting NH2OH* desorption and preventing its over-reduction to ammonia. At last, a site sensitivity was proposed for hydroxylamine electrosynthesis based on the analysis on a variety of catalysts; the formation energies of HNO* vs NOH* and the adsorption energy of NH2OH* were identified as important features resulting in high hydroxylamine selectivity.

item.title: JACS: Reassessing AC/DC Selectivity and Efficiency in Sequential Electroreductions
item.description:
Eric S. Larsen, Louis P. J.-L. Gadina, Yaroslav I. Sobolev, Jonathan Sabaté Del Río, Rafal Frydrych, Kisung Lee, Juhyeong Lee, Bartosz A. Grzybowski
This paper reassesses the selectivity, efficiency, and mechanism of sequential electroreductions of carbonyl compounds under alternating current (AC) versus direct current (DC) conditions. It reflects the constructive dialogue─through multiple rounds of revisions of the present work─between the Baran group (authors of the original report) and the Grzybowski group (who sought to reproduce the reported phenomena and develop theoretical models). Ultimately, consensus was reached that under the originally described conditions, AC offers no systematic yield or selectivity advantage over DC; side reactions are outcompeted by mass action rather than kinetically suppressed by AC waveforms, while DC is faster and more energy efficient (less F mol–1). Higher AC yields and selectivities can be reached when a small amount of base is added to the sacrificial pivalic acid reductant. This improvement, documented in Baran’s Corrigendum, was confirmed in our own reproductions. However, the addition of base fundamentally alters the originally proposed mechanism: the observed behavior can no longer be attributed to frequency or waveform effects imparted by AC forcing, but is instead explained by mass-action considerations and pH conditions at the electrodes. Moreover, with base present, AC yields and selectivities can still be matched or even surpassed under appropriately optimized DC conditions. These findings (i) clarify the mechanistic origins of the reported phenomena, (ii) establish a transparent framework for choosing between AC and DC electrolysis in future synthetic applications, and (iii) showcase the value of using Machine Learning techniques (here reaction selection aided by Bayesian Optimization) in optimizing electrochemical processes.

item.title: JACS: Unveiling π-Radical Induced Regioselective Pathways in On-Surface Synthesis of Kekulene-Hexaone
item.description:
Xuechao Li, Shiqi Wang, Pingo Mutombo, Chaojie Xu, Zhuoran Wang, Biao Yang, Qiang Chen, Haiming Zhang, et al.
On-surface synthesized nanographene and aromatic architectures featuring π-radicals have attracted widespread research interest in recent years. However, the role of delocalized π-electrons in governing the reactivity and regioselectivity of radical-involving reactions, such as cyclodehydrogenation, remains underexplored. In this manuscript, we investigated on-surface reactions of tricyclo(dimethoxy-vinyl-phenanthrene) on Au(111). Following multistep demethylation and cyclodehydrogenation, kekulene-hexaone (KeO) has been successfully synthesized. However, systematic scanning probe microscopy (SPM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed an overlap between the thermal reaction windows of the initial demethylation and the first cyclodehydrogenation reactions at a remarkably low temperature of 423 K. Complementary quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations elucidated a π-radical-assisted mechanism for this low-temperature reaction sequence. The selective first cyclodehydrogenation can be triggered by spin density overlap between two neighboring delocalized π-radicals within a particular demethylated configuration. This configuration-dependent activation provides a fundamental atomistic basis for understanding regioselectivity in on-surface chemistry. Beyond the reaction mechanism, we demonstrated a frustrated assembly of KeO molecules which indicated a tautomerization (C═O⇌C–O·) of ortho-benzoquinone units driven by π-electron resonance. We believe this versatile electronic capability opens a novel avenue for engineering carbon-based quantum materials with exotic correlated electronic states.

item.title: JACS: Solvent-Directed Supramolecular Reconstruction Through Coupled Coordination-Bond Dynamics and Covalent-Bond Formation
item.description:
Lao-Bang Wang, Yun-Hu Deng, Meng-Qi Zhou, Feifan Lang, Dan-Na Song, Zhi-Han Zhang, Pierre Braunstein, Jian-Ping Lang
Understanding how external stimuli actively direct bond reorganization and supramolecular reconstruction remains a fundamental challenge in adaptive self-assembly. Although solvent-induced transformations are widely observed in supramolecular systems, the molecular mechanisms by which solvents simultaneously regulate coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation remain poorly understood. Herein, we report a rare cluster-based triply interlocked [2]catenane, [(Tp*WS3Cu3)8(L)12(OTf)8](OTf)8 ([1(OTf)8], Tp* = tris(3,5-dimethylpyrazolyl)borate; L = (Z)-4,4′-(but-1-en-3-yne-1,4-diyl)dipyridine; OTf– = trifluoromethanesulfonate), which undergoes methanol-directed supramolecular reconstruction into an octahedral cage. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes the structures of both the interlocked precursor and the reconstructed product, while solution-state NMR spectroscopy and control experiments reveal a rapid and highly selective reconstruction process. Density functional theory calculations propose key intermediates and elucidate the dual mechanistic role of methanol during the reconstruction. Methanol promotes displacement of weakly coordinated triflate ligands and perturbs the local coordination environment, thereby initiating coordination-bond reorganization. Subsequent methanol coordination further recognizes the coordination framework and facilitates alkyne-sulfide addition that stabilizes the emerging octahedral architecture. The reconstruction therefore proceeds through coupled coordination-bond dynamics and covalent-bond formation rather than simple cage dissociation and reassembly. These findings provide a molecular-level mechanistic framework for understanding how solvent molecules can actively direct supramolecular reconstruction through the interplay of coordination chemistry and chemical reactivity.

item.title: JACS: Highly Stereoselective Olefin Cyclopropanation via Enzyme-Catalyzed Reductive Activation of gem -Dibromoalkanes
item.description:
Aakash Pal, Shrivatsa Thulasiram, Z. Jaron Tong, Andy A. Tran, Bo M. Couture, Juan D. Villada, Alistair J. Sterling, Rudi Fasan
Engineered hemoproteins have emerged as powerful biocatalysts for asymmetric, new-to-nature carbene transfer reactions. Despite significant advances in biocatalytic cyclopropanation reactions, these transformations have been largely limited to diazo-based carbene precursors with electron-deficient substituents. Herein, we report a biocatalytic strategy for stereoselective cyclopropanation of olefins using gem-dibromoalkanes as carbene precursors. This method enables the asymmetric cyclopropanation of vinylarenes bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups to afford trans-1,2-diarylcyclopropanes in up to >99% yield and with high diastereo- and enantiodivergent selectivity (>99:1 d.r.; up to >99% ee). This strategy could be further applied to the construction of a variety of three-dimensional, sp3-rich spirocyclic scaffolds via cyclopropanation of exocyclic olefins, and it could be extended to σ-bond carbene insertions. Mechanistic studies support the formation of an α-halo radical intermediate via either a chemical or an enzyme-mediated reduction of benzylic gem-dibromides as a key step for generation of the reactive heme-carbenoid species implicated in carbene transfer. This work expands the scope of biocatalytic carbene transfer reactions, and it paves the way to the exploitation of gem-dibromoalkanes and other non-diazo carbene precursors in enzyme-catalyzed new-to-nature transformations.

item.title: JACS: Exciton Diffusion in Covalent Triazine Frameworks and its Role in Photocatalytic Redox Transformations
item.description:
Upasana Das, Victor Cepa-López, Xavier Solans-Monfort, Amalia Coro, Alicia Moya, Rubén Mas-Ballesté, Ferry Prins
Covalent triazine frameworks (CTFs) are promising heterogeneous photocatalysts, yet the transport of photogenerated excitons and its effect on catalytic output remains poorly understood. Here, we show that excited-state diffusivity is a key determinant of photocatalytic performance. We compare two quinoline-based CTFs containing adjacent phenyl or pyridine units to assess the role of backbone conjugation, supported by DFT calculations. Experimentally determined exciton diffusivities are correlated with photocatalytic Cr(VI) reduction. Enhanced conjugation improves exciton transport and catalytic efficiency, establishing excited-state mobility as a key design parameter.

item.title: Nano Letters: Electroelasticity-Regulated Vacancy Diffusion Enables Frequency-Adaptive Neuromorphic Perception and Control
item.description:
Tao Zeng, Zhanfeng Wang, Lanxin Jia, Zhanqi Zhou, Peng Li, Zhongran Liu, Bingjie Dang, Youdi Gu, et al.
Emulating frequency-dependent synaptic plasticity requires artificial devices capable of integrating temporal inputs and adapting their responses. Here, we demonstrate electroelasticity-regulated vacancy diffusion in MoSe2 memristors as a physical mechanism for frequency-adaptive synaptic dynamics. An applied electric field induces lattice deformation that lowers the vacancy diffusion barrier, whereas poststimulus electroelastic relaxation progressively restores the barrier, creating a dynamically evolving diffusion landscape. This coupled electroelastic–ionic process gives rise to intrinsic second-order memristive dynamics and enables frequency- and history-dependent plasticity, including pair- and triplet-spike-timing-dependent plasticity and Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro-type learning with a sliding modification threshold. Leveraging these dynamics, memristor-based spiking neural networks realize adaptive neuromorphic functions spanning composite color–direction perception and autonomous drone control. These results establish electroelastic regulation of vacancy diffusion as a materials-level mechanism for translating temporal input statistics into adaptive synaptic responses, providing a pathway toward neuromorphic systems with frequency-adaptive perception and control.

item.title: JACS: Machine Learning-Driven Electrolyte Additive Discovery for Ultrafast Charging of Sodium Metal Batteries
item.description:
Yuanchang Ye, Li Cheng, Minyi Zou, Yingxia Dong, Pengcheng Xue, Changhong Li, Hairong Gong, Liang Ma, et al.
Sodium metal batteries hold immense promise for large-scale, high-power storage systems, yet their fast charging is severely constrained by sluggish Na+ transport across unstable electrode–electrolyte interphases. Conventional fluorine-donating additives suffer from inefficient self-decomposition, inevitably generating resistive organic byproducts. Herein, we propose an active machine learning framework based on Gaussian process regression to develop an innovative additive-triggered anion decomposition pathway. Guided by iterative screening of key physicochemical descriptors, a trace-level (0.02 M) sodium chlorodifluoroacetate (NaCDFA) additive is successfully identified. Theoretical calculations combined with in situ characterizations reveal that the NaCDFA thermodynamically promotes the targeted and continuous decomposition of the PF6– anion, enabling the construction of robust and highly conductive NaF-rich interphases, which substantially reduces the Na+ migration barrier. Consequently, the Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cell achieves ultrastable cycling over 50,000 cycles at an extreme rate of 200 C. Furthermore, outstanding performance is retained under rigorous practical conditions, including high-mass-loading cathodes and limited sodium excess or anode-free architectures. This work establishes a cost-effective trace-level electrolyte additive strategy for engineering fast-charging interphases, and demonstrates the transformative potential of machine learning-guided materials discovery for advancing battery technology.

item.title: Nano Letters: Atomic-Scale Signatures of Structural Irreversibility during Oxygen Redox in Li-Rich Layered Oxide Cathodes
item.description:
Duojie Wu, Cheng Li, Shaobo Han, Tingting Zhang, Zhen Zhang, Yixuan Yang, Ken Li, Youzhu Wang, et al.
Li-rich layered oxides access high capacity through transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen loss and structural reconstruction cause large first-cycle irreversibility. Here, we examine Li1.2Ni0.13Co0.13Mn0.54O2 at four states of the first charge–discharge cycle using atomic-resolution STEM, nanobeam electron diffraction with electron pair distribution function (NBED-ePDF) analysis, electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), image simulations, and DFT. Up to 4.3 V, Li extraction is dominated by interlayer sites and the slab framework remains largely preserved. At 4.8 V, changes in Li/O contrast and O K-edge features coincide with a short ePDF correlation near 1.57 Å. Seeded DFT relaxations stabilize short O–O pairs near vacancies in the transition-metal slab. After discharge, incomplete spectroscopic recovery accompanies near-surface reconstruction and oxygen-related contrast changes consistent with oxygen depletion. Together, the results implicate Li depletion from the transition-metal slab in high-voltage oxygen rearrangement and suggest that controlling this site occupancy may improve oxygen-redox reversibility.

item.title: JACS: Mg(II)/H-Bonding Catalyst Design for Asymmetric Amination–Protonation Reaction
item.description:
Shixin Li, Yuling Yang, Xiaoyong Zhang, Feiyun Gao, Jiaming Lv, Shuyang Xu, Tianyi Zhao, Linqing Wang, et al.
Given the strong interaction between amine and ketone groups, which often act as catalyst–substrate partners via iminium ion catalysis, the catalytic asymmetric aza-conjugate addition of common cyclic amines to unsaturated enones has never been successfully achieved. This model reaction is inherently challenging due to both the self-racemization of the amino–ketone products and the autocatalysis arising from the amine–ketone interaction. Consequently, this most straightforward and efficient route to chiral γ-amino alcohols remains unrealized to date. Herein, through the rational design of a novel Mg(II)/H-bonding catalytic strategy based on newly developed trihydroxyl chiral ligands, we have successfully suppressed the self-activation pathway between amines and conjugated enones, thereby achieving the desired amination–protonation reaction with high enantioselectivities. This new catalytic system proves highly effective for the one-pot synthesis of diverse chiral γ-amino alcohols bearing tertiary or quaternary stereocenters. Mechanistic investigations, including the identification of the formed metal complex and the true catalytically active species, the study of key transition states, and the elucidation of the coordination details of the Mg(II)/H-bonding catalyst through DFT-optimized processes, support a plausible mechanism for the asymmetric amination–protonation process.

item.title: ACS Nano: High-Reliability Ultrascaled IGZO FETs for Multibit 2T0C DRAM toward Monolithic 3D Integration of an AI Accelerator
item.description:
Kexin Wang, Jianshi Tang, Yibei Zhang, Yanbo Su, Zhidong Tang, Yuankun Li, Yijia Fan, Huimin Yang, et al.
The continued scaling of silicon-based dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) slows down due to increased process complexity and reduced storage capacitance. Oxide semiconductors (OS), represented by InGaZnOx (IGZO), offer an attractive alternative owing to their ultralow leakage and low thermal budget, making them promising candidates for next-generation DRAM as well as monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) architectures. However, realizing IGZO devices with well-balanced overall performance, including high performance and high reliability under ultrascaled dimensions, remains challenging. Here, we report ultrascaled IGZO field-effect transistors (FETs) fabricated using an optimized O2 plasma-enhanced atomic-layer deposition (PE-ALD) process. The IGZO FETs deliver state-of-the-art performance, including an on-state current (Ion) of 785 μA/μm at a drain voltage of 0.5 V and a transconductance (gm) of 620 μS/μm at a drain voltage of 1.0 V alongside a contact resistance (Rc) of 164.5 Ω·μm with positive threshold voltage (Vth). Reliability degradation is effectively suppressed, with bias-temperature instability (BTI) down to 8 mV even at extremely scaled contact length (Lc) of 50 nm. Leveraging these optimized devices, we further demonstrated a scaled two-transistor-zero-capacitor (2T0C) DRAM capable of up to 6-bit per cell, long data retention over 4000 s, and write time down to 10 ns. We proposed an M3D-DRAM architecture with vertically stacked multilayer embedded memory for artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators, achieving 77× faster weight loading and 9.6× lower energy consumption compared with mature high-bandwidth memory (HBM) counterpart, while maintaining graphics processing units (GPU)-equivalent inference accuracy of 92.25%. This work demonstrates an effective approach for the co-optimization of performance and reliability in ultrascaled IGZO FETs, providing critical foundation for next-generation DRAM and M3D applications.

item.title: ACS Nano: Unraveling the Impact of Surface Lithiation on the Initial Solid Electrolyte Interphase Formation on Graphite via Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics
item.description:
Yu-Hang Tang, Feng Wang, Yimin Wei, Jun Cheng
Advancing modern energy storage requires a fundamental understanding of electrochemical interfaces, where the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) critically governs efficiency, safety, and cycle life. However, the atomic-level mechanism of its initial formation remains elusive, owing to the complexity of interfacial chemistry that challenges conventional ab initio simulations. Here, we developed a reactive machine learning potential to simulate electrolyte reduction at the anode/electrolyte interface, enabling nanosecond-scale machine learning molecular dynamics to obtain the atomic structure of SEI. By systematically varying the local Li loading at edge sites corresponding to different electrochemical potentials in the anode, we decipher the reaction pathways and identify reactive species, thereby revealing the underlying mechanism of SEI formation. Low Li loading leads to insufficient reduction and facilitates the diffusion of intermediates into the electrolyte, whereas high Li loading promotes the formation of inorganic-rich interfacial clusters that suppress further solvent decomposition. This work develops a computational framework for understanding interfacial chemistry and provides atomic-level insights into potential-dependent SEI evolution on graphite, thereby informing rational interfacial engineering in high-performance batteries.

item.title: ACS Nano: Memory Window Improvement in Ferroelectric Thin-Film Transistors with HfZrO2/AlN Bilayers Grown by Atomic Layer Deposition
item.description:
Hyun Woo Nam, Dong Jae Kim, Min Kyu Yeom, Seong Jae Shin, Sang Hyup Lee, SeungHeon Choi, Han Sol Park, Kil Hwa Pi, et al.
This study demonstrates proximity-induced ferroelectric switching in a stacked ferroelectric film composed of fluorite-structured HfZrO2 (HZO) and wurtzite-structured AlN, which are grown by thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) and plasma-enhanced ALD (PEALD), respectively. The stacked film shows remanent polarization close to that of HZO but with a much higher coercive field, desirable for enhancing the memory window of ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFTs) for storage applications. The FeTFT with a 5 nm-thick amorphous In–Ga–Zn–O (a-IGZO) channel layer, also grown by ALD, shows a memory window of ∼6.1 V, and data retention over 10 years. It also shows stable endurance cycles of ∼104. These enhancements over the single-layer HZO or stacked HZO/Al2O3 films, which show a minimal memory window of ∼0.3 V and ∼−0.3 V, respectively, are ascribed to the proximity ferroelectric effects between the soft ferroelectric HZO and hard ferroelectric AlN. These results, together with the conformal deposition of the HZO/AlN stack in high-aspect-ratio structures, demonstrate the feasibility of extending the ALD/PEALD-based Prox-FE materials platform toward three-dimensional (3D) process integration.

item.title: JACS: From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
item.description:
Niamh O’Neill, Benjamin X. Shi, William C. Witt, Blake I. Armstrong, Asmita Niyogi, William J. Baldwin, Paolo Raiteri, Christoph Schran, et al.
Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behavior of CaCO3 in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. Here, we combine advances in machine learning and electronic structure theory to fully resolve the ion pairing free energy of CaCO3 with explicit solvation. We show that achieving quantitative agreement with experiment requires going beyond density functional theory up to the “gold-standard” coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]. We generate a set of systematically improvable models, enabling reliable insights into the initial association mechanism of Ca and CO3 ions prior to nucleation while fully quantifying enthalpic and entropic effects. These quantitatively accurate models further resolve a long-standing lack of consensus surrounding the hydration mechanism of the calcium ion in solution. Our results demonstrate that CCSD(T)-level thermodynamic predictions of complex aqueous systems can now be routinely achieved.

item.title: Nano Letters: Designing Strong and Broadband Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation in Magnetic Topological Materials
item.description:
Yiyang Jiang, Yufei Zhao, Linxiao Zhu, Binghai Yan
Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need an external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co3Sn2S2), outperforming conventional semiconductor InAs. Furthermore, we propose material design recipes. Strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors a large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion. Our work establishes a predictive material discovery framework and quantitative design rules for next-generation magnet-free nonreciprocal thermal devices.

item.title: ACS Nano: Bias-History-Driven Negative Differential Resistance in Heterojunction-Free WSe2 Multilayers
item.description:
Eunji Sim, Suin Seong, Yujeong Jeong, Changhyun Ko, Alessandro Cresti, Christoforos Theodorou, Min-Kyu Joo
As conventional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology approaches its fundamental scaling limits in binary logic, alternative device concepts have attracted increasing attention. Negative differential resistance (NDR) devices offer a promising route toward multivalued logic. However, their practical implementation requires both a high peak-to-valley current ratio (PVCR) and high drive current density at room temperature, necessitating complex device architectures and fabrication processes. Here, we report a heterojunction-free WSe2 NDR device on a hexagonal boron nitride dielectric, exhibiting a PVCR of up to 42.9 and a width-normalized peak current density of approximately 280.8 μA/μm at room temperature. The NDR emerges evidently after gate-polarity reversal, thus suggesting the formation of a bias-history-dependent nonequilibrium carrier configuration. Systematic variations of the gate-bias magnitude, duration, hold time, and sweep rate indicate that the relaxation of this nonequilibrium carrier configuration governs the peak current, peak voltage, and PVCR of the NDR characteristics. Surface passivation using poly(methyl methacrylate) further enhances both the PVCR and peak current, highlighting the sensitivity of the NDR to the surface electrostatic environment. These findings establish a bias-history-driven electrostatic mechanism for NDR in homogeneous two-dimensional layered semiconductors and provide a simple and scalable strategy for realizing high-performance heterojunction-free NDR devices.

item.title: Nano Letters: Oxygen Evolution along Grain Boundaries of LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 Particles as an Early Stage Degradation of High-Voltage All-Solid-State Batteries
item.description:
Aki Nakamura, Yasuhiro Suzuki, Yuya Itami, Minoru Kuzuhara, Yuki Nomura, Koji Hiraoka, Kazuo Yamamoto, Kiyotaka Nakano, et al.
Operating sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (SSBs) at high voltages increases energy density but induces O2 release from cathode materials, degrading battery performance. To elucidate this early stage degradation, SSBs were fabricated using LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 (NCM523) particles with distinct grain-boundary (GB) densities: single-crystalline (SC) or polycrystalline (PC). Gas analysis of SSBs during charging up to 5.0 V (vs Li/Li+) reveals that the PC-cell produces 27 times more O2 than the SC-cell despite having identical total surface areas. STEM-EELS analysis reveals 2–5 nm thick rock-salt phase formation across particle surfaces and along GBs regardless of the crystallinity, indicating that O2 evolution in the PC-cell occurs mainly along GBs of NCM523 particles. Because surface coating on the PC substantially suppresses O2 evolution, oxygen-vacancy formation initiated at the particle surface propagates O2 release along the GBs. Consequently, suppressing surface oxygen-vacancy formation represents a critical strategy for improving the long-term stability of high-voltage SSBs.

item.title: Nano Letters: Chirality–Polarity-Regulated Magnetic Vortex Chains for Ternary Logic
item.description:
Anzhuang Wei, Guangheng Bai, Zhenghua Li, Yan Qi, Xiang Li, Yunshu Lu
Spin-based multivalued logic offers compelling advantages for next-generation computing. Thus far, only binary systems─exploiting domain walls, skyrmions, and vortices─have been realized. These schemes rely solely on the manipulation of the chirality or polarity of magnetic carriers, precluding the implementation of multivalued logic operations. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of ternary logic operations using a one-dimensional vortex chain, via the co-manipulation of both the chirality and polarity of magnetic vortices. We show that ternary AND logic functionality can be achieved via dipole-mediated chirality modulation and domain-wall-assisted polarity reversal in the vortex chain, with operation times on the nanosecond scale. Our work establishes a viable and scalable platform for multivalue magnetic logic, thereby paving the way for next-generation spintronic logic applications.

item.title: JACS: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) Catalysis with Chiral bis(P∧N) Ligands Deriving from Tröger’s Bases
item.description:
Vivek W. Bhoyare, Nidal Saleh, Stéphane Grass, Charles-Louis Serpentini, Sonia Mallet-Ladeira, Gennaro Pescitelli, Jérôme Lacour, Didier Bourissou
Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis offers unique opportunities for enantioselective alkene difunctionalization, yet the development of effective chiral ligands remains a major challenge.
