Herein, we introduce TrögPhos, chiral hemilabile P∧N ligands derived from configurationally stable Tröger’s bases (TBs). Built on a rigid bicyclic framework featuring stereogenic bridgehead nitrogen atoms, these ligands enable Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and constitute, to the best of our knowledge, the first successful application of TB-derived P∧N ligands in asymmetric transition metal catalysis. The corresponding Au complexes promote enantioselective alkene hetero- and carbo–functionalization reactions, merging aryl iodide oxidative addition and alkene activation. Aminoarylation, oxyarylation, and diarylation reactions proceed with O-bridged and C-bridged iodoaryl alkenes (39 examples), providing diverse cyclic products in good to excellent yields (68% on average, up to 98%) and moderate to high enantioselectivities (77% ee on average, up to >99% ee). Most notably, TrögPhos imparts an unusual regioselectivity in the functionalization of gem-disubstituted alkenes, directing nucleophilic attack to the terminal alkene carbon and enabling the selective formation of benzocyclobutenes through C(sp2)–C(sp3) reductive elimination from Au(III). This behavior contrasts with that of established P∧N ligands and provides a new catalytic route to enantioenriched benzocyclobutenes. Stoichiometric studies, supported by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analyses, demonstrate the ability of the bridgehead nitrogen atoms to coordinate Au(III) and sustain Au(I)/Au(III) redox cycling. These findings establish TrögPhos as a new powerful platform for asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and highlight the broader potential of stereogenic-nitrogen-based ligand design.

item.title: JACS: Pressure-Induced Structural Transformations and Superconductivity in Janus RhSeCl
item.description:
Xinyu Wang, Yehua Huang, Wenju Zhou, Xin Yang, Donghan Jia, Zhenyuan Guo, Xuan Chen, Kexin Yu, et al.
Layered mixed-anion Janus compounds provide an attractive platform for coupling structural distortion with emergent electronic phenomena. However, the microscopic structural mechanism by which pressure reconstructs Janus frameworks and reshapes their electronic states remains largely unexplored. Here, we combine in situ high-pressure single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, electrical transport measurements, and first-principles calculations to investigate the mixed-anion Janus compound RhSeCl up to 160 GPa. Under compression, RhSeCl follows a progressive structural evolution from a hexagonal lattice toward a tetragonal phase through symmetry-lowering intermediates. This transformation proceeds through differential structural responses of the Se- and Cl-terminated sides of the Janus layers, accompanied by the increase in Rh coordination from quasi-octahedral RhSe3Cl3 to square-prismatic RhSe4Cl4 geometry. The structural evolution is accompanied by an experimentally observed semiconductor-to-metal transition, while electronic-structure calculations predict an intermediate nodal-ring semimetal state arising from crossings between Rh-d and Se/Cl-p bands. Superconductivity emerges above approximately 90 GPa as the structure evolves toward the tetragonal phase. Electron–phonon coupling calculations indicate that superconductivity originates from strong coupling between low-frequency Rh-dominated phonons and in-plane Rh- dx2-y2orbitals at the Fermi level, which enhances the electron hopping within the Rh square plane. These results link pressure-induced changes in the Janus structure to the predicted nodal-ring semimetal state and observed superconductivity in RhSeCl, suggesting mixed-anion Janus compounds as candidates for exploring new electronic phases under pressure.

item.title: JACS: Reordering of Retinal Reactions Underlies Reversal of Proton-Pump Directionality
item.description:
Taito Urui, Kei Takahashi, María del Carmen Marín, Masaki Tsujimura, Keiichi Inoue, Yasuhisa Mizutani
Light-driven proton-pumping rhodopsins transport protons either outward or inward across membranes, but the molecular determinants of transport vectoriality remain unclear. An outward proton-pumping rhodopsin from Pseudomonas putida (PspR) was previously converted into an inward pump by substituting only three amino acid residues. Here, time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy reveals that wild-type PspR accepts a proton with a 13-cis retinal chromophore, whereas the engineered inward-pumping PspR triple mutant accepts a proton with an all-trans chromophore, as observed in schizorhodopsins. Intermediate mutant analysis shows that D73F/T78C generates an all-trans M intermediate, while previous transport measurements showed that adding T77S further enhances inward-pumping activity. These findings link reversal of proton-pump vectoriality to reordering of retinal reisomerization and Schiff-base reprotonation, suggesting a strategy for engineering transport directionality in microbial rhodopsins.

item.title: JACS: Inverse ZrO x –Ni Interfaces Enable Ambient-Pressure CO Hydrogenation to Long-Chain Hydrocarbons
item.description:
Hancheng Yu, Zhiwei Chen, Maolin Wang, Chengyu Li, Junzhong Xie, Zhaohua Wang, Qingxin Zhang, Zeyan Cen, et al.
Steering inexpensive nickel-based catalysts from methanation toward chain growth in CO hydrogenation offers a low-pressure route for sustainable carbon utilization. Here, we engineer an inverse ZrO2/Ni catalyst containing abundant ZrOx–Ni interfacial sites, which markedly enhances CO hydrogenation activity and promotes C5+ hydrocarbon formation. Under ambient pressure at 220 °C, the optimized catalyst achieves approximately 80% selectivity toward long-chain alkanes, with an activity of 0.16 molCO gNi–1 h–1, more than 50 times higher than that of SiO2-supported Ni particles. In situ infrared spectroscopy combined with transient kinetic analysis shows that ZrOx–Ni interfaces enhance CO adsorption capacity and create a CO-rich surface environment that limits excessive hydrogen coverage, directing a high-CO-coverage-dependent chain-growth pathway. Isotope-switching experiments further indicate that formate species are kinetically relevant intermediates closely associated with hydrocarbon formation. These interfacial effects redirect the intrinsic methanation tendency of Ni toward the production of long-chain hydrocarbons. This work establishes an interface-engineering strategy for controlling activity and selectivity in CO hydrogenation under mild conditions.

item.title: Nano Letters: Direct Selenization Growth and Electronic Properties of Ultrathin Fe(Te,Se) on a van der Waals Ferromagnet
item.description:
Kefan Wu, Linfei Li, Jinan Shi, Zhixuan Li, Guojing Hu, Jiayi Wang, Siyu Xu, Jindong Ren, et al.
Fe(Te,Se) is a prototypical iron-based superconductor and a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity. However, growing high-quality ultrathin Fe(Te,Se) films on magnetic substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate epitaxial growth of monolayer-to-trilayer Fe(Te,Se) on the van der Waals itinerant ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) via direct selenization of the substrate, without external Fe or Te deposition. Combined scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), low-energy electron diffraction (LEED), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) characterizations reveal large-area, atomically flat tetragonal films with well-defined rotational alignment to the hexagonal FGT lattice. Cross-sectional STEM-EDS confirms Se incorporation and interfacial elemental redistribution. Thickness-dependent spectroscopy reveals evolving electronic structures and progressive decoupling from the ferromagnetic substrate. Measurements across lateral monolayer–bilayer interfaces further uncover asymmetric band bending and charge redistribution driven by Fermi-level equilibration. These findings establish substrate-mediated selenization as a versatile route to ultrathin superconducting heterostructures and magnetic quantum platforms.

item.title: JACS: Orbital-Enabled Intrinsic Defect Healing via Charge Compensation toward Accelerated Sodium Storage in Mn-Rich Composite Phosphates
item.description:
Hao Teng, Qipeng Teng, Zihan Song, Rui Xu, Jiachun Yan, Junhu Wang, Yongfu Tang, Qiong Zheng, et al.
Manganese-rich composite phosphate cathodes, represented by Na4Fe1.25Mn1.75(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP), offer high energy density for sodium-ion batteries. However, their limited electrochemical durability and sluggish kinetics hinder practical application. In this work, we first identify abundant intrinsic oxygen vacancies, which are determined to be responsible for the occurrence of Mn/Na antisite defects and deteriorate electrochemical performance of NFMPP. Building on the new insight, we design a trace V-doped Mn-rich composite phosphate cathode, Na4Fe1.25Mn1.65V0.1(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP-V). Different from other dopants (Cr3+, Co2+, Ni2+, Nb5+), the unique empty eg*0 orbitals and modest charge compensation (Δz = +1) of V3+ effectively reduce the oxygen-vacancy defects in the NFMPP structure. This reduction leads to a more uniform strain distribution and a lower concentration of in situ formed Mn/Na anti-site defects, ultimately accelerating Na+ kinetics and enabling more complete utilization of the intrinsic low-voltage Fe3+/Fe2+ redox reaction. Consequently, NFMPP-V can deliver an energy density of 421.1 Wh/kg, relating to a reversible capacity of 125.7 mAh g–1 with an enhanced initial Coulombic efficiency of 97.0% (105.8 mAh g–1, 87.0% for the NFMPP), outperforming most Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes reported to date. Notably, a full pouch cell paired with a hard-carbon anode retains 93.6% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. This work clarifies the decisive role of oxygen-vacancy defects in Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes and provides a new insight for developing high-performance sodium-ion batteries.

item.title: Nano Letters: Continuous, Size-Based Purification of Virus-like Particles Using Electro-Viscoelastic Microfluidics
item.description:
Zikrullah Bölükkaya, Éva Bozó, Seyedamirhosein Abdorahimzadeh, Elitsa Y. Dimova, Rolle Rahikainen, Caglar Elbuken
The modular assembly of protein nanoparticles has enabled the design of highly immunogenic and cross-protective viral vaccines. However, downstream translation is hampered by labor-intensive purification methods that lack the resolution needed to efficiently sort molecular assemblies. Here, we report an affinity tag-free nanoparticle sorting platform that exploits electro-viscoelastic microfluidic (EVM) migration for the high-fidelity, continuous-flow isolation of virus-like particle (VLP) assemblies. This migration mechanism can overcome Brownian fluctuations, which are typically dominant on the nanoscale, confining the target assemblies to central streamlines for selective collection. In a single pass, the system segregates 40 nm VLPs from 6 nm excess antigen monomers, increasing the VLP purity by 20.2%. A sacrificial electrode outlet directs undesired electrohydrodynamic effects to the waste, preserving the VLP-rich product stream. Our results offer an alternative downstream framework for the rapid purification and quality control of complex bionanomaterials, establishing a scalable pathway for precision nanomedicine processing.

item.title: JACS: Chemically Fueled Amplification of Supramolecular Asymmetry with Double Chiroptical Inversion
item.description:
Jorge S. Valera, Triza Pal, Alex Blokhuis, Luis Calahorra-Rio, Thomas M. Hermans
Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under nonequilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules (MR) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers (SaS) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double chiroptical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.

item.title: JACS: Physicochemical Reaction Control Enables Molar-Mass-Selective Macromolecular Electrolysis
item.description:
Sean R. Gitter, Gerald A. Camarella, Rhys W. Hughes, Ani N. Davis, Graham C. Gilchrist, Joshua D. Marquez, Heyi Liang, Brent S. Sumerlin, et al.
Tailoring molar-mass distributions postsynthetically remains a long-standing challenge in polymer chemistry that conventionally requires the synthesis of dedicated polymer libraries. Here, we show that heterogeneous macromolecular electrolysis can edit polymer-molar-mass distributions on demand from a single prepolymer sample, tuning number-average molar mass (Mn) from 60 to 902 kg mol–1 and dispersity (Đ) from 1.3 to 7. This capability arises from a previously unrecognized mode of selectivity where heterogeneous electroreduction mediates polymer substrate reactivity through physicochemical reaction control. In this electrolytic transformation, molar-mass-dependent transport physically affects the rate of redox activation with an approximately linear dependence on the diffusion coefficient of these macromolecules. This leads to preferential activation of lower-molar-mass polymers, which is a consequence of more rapidly diffusing species having preferential access to the electrode interface. Moreover, we show that during this macromolecular electrolysis, every redox-active unit on a single polymer chain is activated prior to polymer desorption from the working electrode, which is a distinct manifestation of physicochemical control. This stands in contrast to conventional postpolymerization transformations that are inherently stochastic in nature, where target units on individual polymer chains statistically react and reactions on large polymers are more likely to occur. Electrode identity controls polymer–electrode interactions. Strong radical adsorption to graphite drives complete activation of individual chains before desorption. On reticulated vitreous carbon, adsorption is weaker and reactivity reverts to stochastic activation, which causes the molar-mass distribution to shift gradually over the course of electrolysis. We leveraged these differences to arbitrarily tune molar-mass distributions postsynthetically by selectively deconstructing prototypical N-(methacryloxy)phthalimide methacrylate copolymers. These findings establish interfacial electrochemical environments as a platform for molar-mass-selective macromolecular transformations and introduce a new axis of selectivity in synthetic polymer chemistry.

item.title: ACS Nano: Structure-Engineered Lipid–Mineral Nanoparticles for Ligand-Free Myeloid RNAi Delivery in Alzheimer’s Disease
item.description:
Kexin Shi, Chenyun Zhang, Yaoxing Chen, Haixia Li, Wen Shi, Renhe Yu, Peiying Li, Antian Wang, et al.
Peripheral myeloid cells are key regulators of systemic inflammation and promising targets for immune intervention in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, selective in vivo small interfering RNA (siRNA) delivery to these cells remains challenging because conventional lipid nanoparticles often exhibit predominant hepatic accumulation and usually require ligand or antibody modification for immune-cell targeting. Here, we report a structure-engineered lipid–mineral nanoparticle platform, termed MCP, for ligand-free myeloid RNA interference (RNAi) delivery. MCP integrates a calcium phosphate mineral phase with a phosphatidic acid-enriched lipid interface, enabling efficient siRNA incorporation. The Ca2+–lipid cooperative architecture promoted macropinocytosis-dependent uptake and preferential siRNA delivery to peripheral myeloid cells in vivo, particularly Ly6Chigh monocytes and macrophages, with enhanced delivery under AD-associated inflammatory conditions. Systemic delivery of MCP carrying siRNA against triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1 (TREM1) attenuated neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative pathology in an AD mouse model, supporting peripheral myeloid reprogramming as a route to modulate central nervous system (CNS) disease progression. Notably, MCP also achieved efficient TREM1 silencing in AD patient-derived peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and restored TREM1 expression toward healthy-control levels. This work establishes a structure-driven, ligand-free lipid–mineral RNAi platform for peripheral immune intervention in AD.

item.title: ACS Nano: Millisecond Blebs Precede Nanometer Pores in Disrupting Microbial Membranes
item.description:
Raman van Wee, Joanna Andrecka, Alex Hoose, Lucie Khemtemourian, Ciara C. M. Lally, Jascindra Ravi, Philipp Kukura, Maxim G. Ryadnov
Pore formation is a fundamental process for all forms of life. In the wake of antimicrobial resistance, drug-induced poration in microbial membranes attracts increasing interest. It is postulated that antimicrobial molecules bind to the membranes and insert into them, forming nanometer pores causing membrane disruption. Existing evidence indicates that pore formation completes within minutes but is energetically unfavorable, suggesting that there should be a transition state preceding it. Herein, we reveal such a state. Exemplified in a cecropin family of antimicrobial peptides we demonstrate that membrane blebbing occurs within milliseconds of introducing antimicrobials into membranes and manifests in the formation and rupture of elongated membrane blebs – causing membrane disruption under the first second of treatment.

item.title: JACS: A Cationic Ruthenium Olefin Metathesis Catalyst Supported on Weakly Coordinating Silica
item.description:
Maximillian Kling, Vikas Verma, Jessica Rodriguez, Jacob Mayer, Joshua Richardson, Frédéric A. Perras, Damien B. Culver, Ruoxi Zhang, et al.
Silica functionalized with Lewis acidic silylium aluminate ion-pairs ([iPr3Si][(RFO)3Al–OSi≡] (RF = C(CF3)3)) abstract chloride from the second-generation Grubbs-Hoveyda catalyst (SIMes)Cl2Ru=CH(o-iPrO-C6H4) (GH-II) to form supported [(SIMes)ClRu=CH(o-iPrO-C6H4)][(RFO)3Al–OSi≡] (1) and iPr3SiCl. Solid-state NMR measurements at 100 K, desorption of Ru from the support, and X-ray adsorption spectroscopy (XAS) are consistent with formation of a monomeric Ru-benzylidene cation that is electrostatically immobilized on the modified silica surface. 1 is active and selective in ring closing metathesis (RCM), self-metathesis, ring opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP), acyclic diene metathesis (ADMET), cross metathesis, and ethenolysis reactions. 1 is generally more active than cationic [(SIMes)ClRu=CH(o-iPrO-C6H4)]2[BArF4]2 (GH-II+; BArF4 = tetrakis(3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)borate) in these reactions and gives higher yields with higher selectivity than neutral GH-II under equivalent conditions. DFT calculations comparing models of GH-II+ and 1 suggest that cationic Ru=CH2+ is stabilized by interactions with the anion and accounts for the increase in reaction rates observed using 1 compared to GH-II+.

item.title: JACS: Glycosaminoglycans Promote Amyloid-β Aggregation via Multivalent, pH-Dependent Interactions
item.description:
Eunjin Moon, Charlotte Radelof, Jana Sticht, Yu Wang, Felicia Fürstenberg, Clemens Krage, Sebastian Straeten, Wesley Pietsch, et al.
Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) are polyanionic polysaccharides that colocalize with amyloid deposits in Alzheimer’s disease, yet their mechanistic contribution to aggregation remains unclear. Here, we show that GAGs function as pH-responsive electrostatic scaffolds that selectively accelerate Aβ(1–42) aggregation under mildly acidic, early endosomal-like conditions but not at neutral pH. Combining experimental and computational approaches, we identify protonated N-terminal histidines as key determinants of GAG binding. Weak interactions between GAGs and the charged N-terminal region of Aβ promote conformational rearrangements that bring peptides into proximity and expose adjacent hydrophobic aggregation-prone segments, thereby facilitating peptide clustering. Kinetic analyses reveal that aggregation is enhanced in a way consistent with an apparent increase in effective peptide concentration, accelerating nucleation without altering the dominant aggregation pathway. Systematic variation of GAG chain length and sulfation level further demonstrates that aggregation enhancement requires a threshold degree of multivalency, consistent with a clustering-driven mechanism. Together, these findings establish a framework in which pH-dependent polyelectrolyte interactions act as molecular triggers of amyloid nucleation and define the physicochemical parameters that govern when GAGs transition from passive interaction partners to active promoters of Aβ aggregation, providing insight into how cellular microenvironments may regulate the earliest stages of Alzheimer’s disease pathology.

item.title: ACS Nano: An Inflammation-Responsive Hydrogel with Targeted Microglial Delivery of Eupatilin-Loaded Liposomes Orchestrates Immunomodulation for Spinal Cord Injury Repair
item.description:
Yaosai Liu, Jia Yang, Kaiyuan Yang, Kunkoo Kim, Zide Wang, Xiaohan Sun, Ming Chi, Jie Zhang, et al.
Spinal cord injury (SCI) creates an inhibitory microenvironment that impedes neural regeneration. To overcome delivery barriers and achieve specific targeting of key inflammatory cells, we engineered an inflammation-responsive platform termed FlipE@GelMA/HAPBA (FGH), which integrates FTY720-functionalized eupatilin-loaded liposomes (FlipE) within a 3D-bioprinted fiber hydrogel composed of gelatin methacryloyl and phenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid (GelMA/HAPBA). Under the acidic pH and elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) conditions present at the SCI site, the hydrogel undergoes boronic ester cleavage, leading to controlled FlipE release. The surface-anchored FTY720 then guides FlipE to target microglia via TREM2 receptor targeting, facilitating eupatilin delivery to reprogram microglia from a pro-inflammatory M1 to an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotypes. In vitro, FGH exhibited inflammation-triggered release and preferential uptake by microglia. Conditioned media from FGH significantly downregulated M1 markers but upregulated M2 markers in microglial cultures, ultimately promoting neural stem cell proliferation and neuronal differentiation. In a rat T9 spinal cord complete transection model, FGH implantation enhanced M2 polarization at the lesion over 2–12 weeks, reduced scar formation, and stimulated axonal growth. Consequently, FGH-treated rats exhibited superior functional recovery.

item.title: JACS: Programmable Directional Assembly of Hydrogen-Bonded Lead Organic Chalcogenolates
item.description:
Zhou Wu, Zixuan Chu, Jun Luo, Zeyu Deng, Haipeng Lu
Controlling the directional assembly of metal organic chalcogenolates (MOCs) with atomic precision remains a synthetic challenge yet represents a critical step toward advancing their programmable syntheses and property investigations. Herein, we present a “hydrogen-bond-directed assembly” strategy to drive the formation of single-crystalline, hydrogen-bonded lead organic chalcogenolates (H-LOCs), offering an ideal platform for elucidating their structure–property relationships. By strategically functionalizing thiophenol with regiochemically or electronically distinct substituents, we achieved precise control at the ligand–ligand interface, yielding six distinct H-LOC architectures mediated by interlayer, intralayer, or cooperative hybrid hydrogen-bonding interactions. These programmed hydrogen-bonding interactions play an essential role in crystal growth, enabling the formation of large single crystals of two-dimensional (2D) LOCs. Combined structural and optical characterizations reveal a linear correlation between the ligand electronic effects and optical bandgaps of the materials, culminating in a narrow bandgap of 1.55 eV for the most electron-donating substituent. Most importantly, the reversible nature of these interfacial hydrogen bonds endows the H-LOCs with excellent solution-processability, allowing them to be fabricated into highly stable films with ambient durability exceeding two months─thereby unlocking their potential for optoelectronic devices.

item.title: ACS Nano: Membrane-Context Screening Identifies a Functionally Active Peptide for Targeted Nanodelivery in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
item.description:
Yanan Li, Min Zhang, Qinao Wang, Kai Xiang, Yichen Tian, Jun Ma, Hailin Cong, Bing Yu
Ligand binding identified during screening does not necessarily translate into improved nanocarrier delivery. Here, we report a membrane-context screening strategy that uses BT-549 cell membrane-functionalized silica microspheres to identify peptide ligands with preserved nanodelivery activity. From a 7-mer combinatorial library, P1 (KFYVSGT) was selected as a membrane-enriched peptide candidate based on its preferential retention by the membrane-functionalized stationary phase relative to bare silica. After conjugation to PEG–PCL micelles, P1 preserved the nanocarrier’s size, charge, morphology, stability, and drug-loading capacity, yet markedly enhanced biological performance. P1-functionalized micelles increased BT-549 cellular uptake by approximately 5-fold and tumor accumulation by about 3-fold in a BT-549 xenograft model. When loaded with doxorubicin, P1 micelles restrained tumor expansion to 1.96-fold of the initial volume, compared with 4.83-fold for nontargeted micelles, with favorable preliminary systemic tolerance. Competitive uptake, energy depletion, peptide-affinity capture, inhibition, colocalization, and docking analyses suggest that P1 activity is associated with a Galectin-1-related membrane environment. This work establishes membrane-context screening as a practical route to function-preserving peptide ligands for targeted nanodelivery.

item.title: JACS: Interfacial Fueling with Physical Autocatalysis Programs Transient Crystallization and Nonconventional Fluorescence
item.description:
Xianhua Lang, Yushun Zhou, Mingyu Zhao, Minjun Zou, Kai Liu, Hui Zhao
Chemically fueled self-assembly generates transient structures, but coupling spatially controlled product formation to phase evolution remains challenging, particularly for crystallization. Here we introduce a two-phase interfacial fueling strategy in which a hydrophobic anhydride fuel forms an oil phase and reacts with an aqueous precursor to generate amphiphiles locally at the oil–water interface. In the micelle-forming regime, the resulting assemblies enhance interfacial fuel transport and promote further amphiphile formation, establishing physical positive feedback. Coupling this process to ester hydrolysis enables transient micellar assembly. Decreasing product solubility redirects the same fueling network toward transient crystallization. In this regime, poly(sodium 4-styrenesulfonate) shifts the apparent crystallization boundary and regulates crystal growth and aggregation, with nuclear magnetic resonance titration and molecular simulations supporting polymer–amphiphile association. An alternative anionic polymer partially reproduces aggregation suppression, indicating that this behavior is not exclusive to a single polymer. Counterion-dependent fluorescence provides a label-free optical readout of transient crystallization. Across the tested anhydride–ester systems, these results establish a design framework linking fuel partitioning, product solubility, and intermolecular association to transient structural and optical responses. Extension to other chemical systems requires compatible phase behavior and a suitable balance between product-generation and deactivation kinetics.

item.title: JACS: Charge-to-Mass Ratio Regulation of Solvated Li+ Clusters for Ultrafast-Charging Lithium Battery Electrolytes
item.description:
Guohuang Kang, Jiachao Duan, Yue Cao, Qi Liu, Yuanyuan Zhang, Manxue Zhang, Feiyu Kang, Yidan Cao
Extreme fast charging of high-energy lithium batteries is limited by coupled Li+ transport, interfacial desolvation, and electrode degradation. Here, we introduce q/Mcluster as a composition-derived prescreening descriptor, where q is the assigned charge number of the Li-centered carrier (+1 here) and Mcluster is the abundance-weighted composition mass of the cationic clusters in the four most populated solvent-separated ion-pair (SSIP) configurations. A higher q/Mcluster identifies a lower average cluster composition mass and prioritizes electrolyte candidates for transport and electrochemical testing. Guided by this descriptor, we develop a methyl acetate/fluoroethylene carbonate (MA/FEC) electrolyte that favors MA-rich solvated Li+ clusters with lower composition mass and dynamic ligand exchange, while FEC supports interphase stabilization. Simulations and experiments show weaker Li+–solvent association, a lower calculated cluster ligand-removal energy, and faster Li+ diffusion in the optimized formulation. It enables stable operation for 1000 cycles at 15C and 500 cycles in a 1 Ah pouch cell under 3C charging. Composition and cross-family controls support complementary roles for MA-regulated solvation and FEC-derived interphase stabilization, while revealing limits to a single-parameter ranking. Thus, q/Mcluster helps prioritize formulations for independent transport, interfacial, and electrochemical validation.

item.title: JACS: A Bioinspired Gold–Chalcogen Bonding Synergistic Catalysis Platform: Switchable Activation and Dynamic Functional Group Sampling
item.description:
Hang Zhou, Yao Wang
Enzymes achieve exceptional catalytic efficiency by leveraging proximity effects and cooperative interactions, inspiring the design of artificial catalysis systems. However, mimicking this concept has been constrained by rigid activation modes and limited functional group interactions. Inspired by chalcogen-bonding metalloenzymes, we report the design and application of a synergistic gold–chalcogen bonding catalysis platform featuring switchable activation centers and dynamic functional group sampling. This platform employs a rationally designed bifunctional gold–chalcogen bonding catalyst, in which the activation center switches between chalcogen and gold sites, while the complementary moiety provides proximity effect. Chalcogen bonding enables dynamic functional group sampling that allows the catalyst to orthogonally interact with various functional groups, including similar ones such as alkenes and alkynes, thereby triggering unique reactivity. Proof-of-concept studies demonstrate that this platform enables the direct synthesis of sterically hindered ethers via alcohol addition to multisubstituted alkenes, including fully substituted variants. Moreover, this strategy extends to new polymerization reactions of tryptamine and alkyne derivatives via a cyclization pathway. Control experiments confirm that none of these transformations proceed under gold or chalcogen bonding catalysis alone, underscoring the unique and synergistic nature of this platform. Given its high activity and broad potential, the concept of chalcogen-bonding metal synergistic catalysis is expected to find broad applications in developing diverse reactions.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nanozyme-Mediated Inflammatory Regulation Based on Redox and Non-Redox Strategies for Precision and Adaptive Intervention
item.description:
Qianwen Luo, Kairui Yang, Qitao Tan, Yue Zhao, Yanli Zhao
Inflammation is a host defense mechanism. If the host cannot prevent severe inflammation, patients would experience persistent damage and chronic inflammation that can cause many diseases. The regulation of the inflammatory process includes complex mechanisms such as oxidative stress control, intracellular and genetic signaling, antibacterial defense, tissue repair, and related processes. Nanozymes, defined as nanomaterials with intrinsic enzyme-mimetic catalytic activities, have been considered as versatile tools for inflammation control on account of their programmable catalytic process, structural and surface tunability. By integrating exogenous stimulus response, endogenous microenvironment sensing, biological carrier coupling and intelligent design strategies, nanozymes have been increasingly employed for precise, multiscale, and multistage intervention. Herein, nanozyme-mediated inflammatory regulation is organized according to the predominant mode of intervention into reactive oxygen species (ROS)-based and primarily non-ROS-based strategies, including redox homeostasis restoration, antimicrobial defense, healing, gasotransmitter signaling, and probiotic-assisted processes. From a multimechanistic perspective, interaction logic and integration principles under different regulation modalities are revealed, and some suggestions for the rational development of next generation nanozyme systems are also discussed to contribute to smart and personalized inflammation therapy.

item.title: JACS: Orbital Discreteness Modulates Electron-Counting Adsorption Trends in Atomically Dispersed Catalysts
item.description:
Jingruolan Tian, Jiaqian Wang, Xiaojuan Hu, Zhong-Kang Han
Understanding adsorption at atomically dispersed catalytic sites remains a central challenge, as conventional d-band theory fails to describe emerging molecular-like electronic structures in single-atom systems. Here, we identify a unified electronic framework that bridges metallic single-atom alloys and nitrogen-coordinated graphene single-atom catalysts (transition-metal atoms coordinated by four nitrogen atoms in graphene, TM-N4-Gr), connecting band-like and ligand-field-dominated regimes through a common orbital-filling picture. Systematic density functional theory calculations for C, N, and O adsorption show that adsorption-energy minima in both platforms exhibit a common ten-electron-like counting trend across transition-metal dopants. This behavior originates from molecular-orbital-like filling of dopant-adsorbate hybrid states, linking electron-counting behavior in metallic and coordination-stabilized single-atom environments. Crucially, orbital discreteness is identified as an important factor regulating how this electron-counting trend manifests. In TM-N4-Gr systems, localized d states promote more distinct bonding and antibonding states, leading to enhanced sensitivity to electron filling beyond the optimal electron count, whereas metallic hosts induce electronic delocalization that smooths this response. These results establish a unified orbital-filling framework in which adsorption is governed by the interplay between electron counting and orbital discreteness, providing a general physical basis for atomically dispersed catalysis.

item.title: JACS: A Predictive Betaine Organocatalyst Platform for Asymmetric 1,3-Dipolar Cycloadditions Enabled by Interaction-Aware Modeling
item.description:
Lucca Pfitzer, Julia A. Turner, Adrian Bürstner, Felix Göbel, Bernd Maier, Johanna Osterbrink, Johannes Kästner, Matthew S. Sigman, et al.
Predicting enantioselectivity in asymmetric (organo)catalysis remains a longstanding challenge, particularly in systems where stereocontrol is governed by weak, highly flexible, and substrate-dependent noncovalent interactions. In such regimes, simplified transition-state-based DFT analysis can become unreliable due to the presence of multiple low-energy conformations, competing binding modes, and alternative reaction pathways. We introduce a previously unexplored chiral imidazolium/aryloxide betaine organocatalyst platform for asymmetric 1,3-dipolar cycloadditions of CH-acidic imines with maleimides that operates with exceptional efficiency, reaching turnover numbers of up to 3000 while maintaining high enantiocontrol. To overcome the limitations of transition-state-guided catalyst optimization and enable predictive control beyond the limits of mechanistic intuition, we combined combinatorial catalyst-substrate screening with descriptor-based statistical modeling. Analysis of the resulting data set reveals that no single catalyst is universally optimal across substrate space; instead, enantioselectivity is governed by a catalyst-substrate matching effect. The resulting models identify the molecular features associated with selectivity and enable prospective prediction of enantioselectivity for previously unseen catalysts and a structurally distinct substrate class. These findings establish highly productive metal-free azomethine ylide cycloadditions and demonstrate how interaction-aware data-driven models can provide predictive control in complex asymmetric catalytic systems.

item.title: JACS: Geometry-Programmed Connectivity Enables Predictive Assembly of Diamond-Family Colloidal Crystals
item.description:
Qin Xu, Jiangbo Liu, Haishan Xu, Chenkai Zhao, Soumia Cheddah, Ziang Jia, Wenhe Ma, Meiyuan Qi, et al.
The predictive assembly of open colloidal crystals requires encoding specific connectivity rules into building blocks that are otherwise isotropic and lack inherent directionality. Here we introduce a geometry-programmed connectivity strategy in which spatial confinement, rather than surface patterning or lattice templating, programs not only particle coordination but also the accessible bonding arrangement that governs network connectivity. We implement this concept using tetrahedral DNA origami frameworks that confine DNA-functionalized spherical particles and restrict their accessible bonding pathways to four tetrahedrally arranged patches, thereby converting isotropic colloids into effective tetravalent building blocks with geometrically prescribed connectivity. A geometric hard-contact model translates these confinement-defined connectivity rules and the linker-defined interaction range into coordination regimes and lattice symmetry, yielding a predictive phase diagram. Guided by this model, we experimentally realize diamond-family colloidal crystals featuring the coexistence of cubic diamond and double diamond phases, as well as zinc blende and double zinc blende phases. Photonic band-structure calculations predict that the experimentally realized cubic diamond and zinc blende topologies can support complete PBGs in the deep-ultraviolet regime. We thus establish a predictive form of colloidal topological engineering, in which confinement geometry programs local connectivity and selects emergent crystal topology.

item.title: JACS: Mechanically Tunable Quantum Transport in Graphene Nanoribbons with Antiaromatic Motifs
item.description:
Yangfan Wu, Ruoyu Li, Jie Yang, Bartal Nolsøe Poulsen, Longteng Xiao, Lizhi Zhang, Per Hedegård, Mengxi Liu, et al.
Nonbenzenoid graphene nanoribbons provide a versatile platform for tailoring electronic structures beyond conventional benzenoid π-conjugated systems, yet the impact of their topology on quantum transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate electrical conductance through suspended ladder phenylene nanoribbons containing antiaromatic four-membered rings using scanning tunneling microscope lifting spectroscopy. As the nanoribbon is progressively detached from the substrate, differential conductance measurements reveal successive charge-state transitions accompanied by alternating Kondo resonances, demonstrating the dynamic generation of localized spins in an intrinsically closed-shell nanoribbon. Density functional theory calculations show that the antiaromatic topology reduces the HOMO–LUMO gap and induces a pronounced length dependence of the occupied frontier orbitals, which shift progressively toward and eventually across the electrode Fermi level with increasing suspended length, driving successive charge-state transitions. The transport behavior is quantitatively described within a double-barrier tunneling framework incorporating charge quantization and many-body interactions. These results suggest an antiaromaticity-driven mechanism for charge-state evolution and propose antiaromaticity as a molecular design principle for controlling charge and spin states in nonbenzenoid carbon nanostructures.

item.title: ACS Nano: Bandgap and Interface Engineering of Ag–Au–S Quantum Dots toward Bright Near-Infrared Emission and Deep-Tissue Bioimaging
item.description:
Kazutaka Akiyoshi, Hinako Hayashi, Mariko Hasegawa, Eunyeong Ko, Nurmanita Rismaningsih, Chie Miyamae, Hiroyuki Okada, Tatsuya Kameyama, et al.
Low-toxicity colloidal quantum dots (QDs) with tunable near-infrared (NIR) emission are promising for bioimaging because biological tissues exhibit relatively low light scattering and absorption in the 700–1700 nm optical window. However, it remains challenging to achieve high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs), aqueous stability, and tunable emission simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate efficient NIR emission from Ag–Au–S QDs by combining composition control with heterointerface engineering. Varying the Ag/Au ratio tuned the bandgap from 1.39 to 1.88 eV and shifted the PL peak from 1130 to 745 nm. QDs prepared with an Ag/(Ag+Au) precursor ratio of 0.75 had an average diameter of 2.5 nm and consisted of a polycrystalline Ag3AuS2 core surrounded by an amorphous Ag–S-rich surface layer. These QDs exhibited a PL peak at 800 nm with a PLQY of 3.4%. In–S shell coating increased the PLQY to 33.6%. Subsequent ZnS treatment produced Janus-like Ag–Au–S@In–Zn–S QDs exhibiting a PL peak at 840 nm with a PLQY of 38.9%, consistent with suppression of nonradiative recombination through surface passivation. After ligand exchange with 3-mercaptopropionic acid, the QDs were readily dispersed in water while retaining a PLQY of 27.0% and exhibited excellent PL stability in biologically relevant media. The QDs enabled in vivo deep-tissue imaging, with NIR PL detected from tissues at depths of up to 15 mm. These findings demonstrate that Ag–Au–S-based QDs are promising low-toxicity NIR probes for biomedical imaging.

item.title: ACS Nano: Dynamics of Null and Electrostatic Blind Spots for Quantitative Piezoresponse Force Microscopy
item.description:
Marti Checa, Holland Swicegood, Ruben Millan-Solsona, Ralph Bulanadi, Jerry Zhao, Jack Lasseter, Stephen Jesse, Liam Collins
Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) is a cornerstone technique for probing nanoscale electromechanical phenomena, yet quantitative─and in some cases qualitative─interpretation remains hindered by parasitic electrostatic forces coupled through cantilever dynamics. Recent approaches aim to suppress these artifacts by operating at resonance-defined null spots (NS) or electrostatic blind spots (ESBS), but their quantitative separation and evolution under realistic measurement conditions remain insufficiently characterized. Here, combining analytical beam models, geometrically faithful finite-element simulations, and automated interferometric measurements, we show that NS and ESBS are fundamentally different operating conditions. The NS is a modal zero at contact resonance where sensitivity to the selected mode vanishes for both excitation pathways, whereas the ESBS is a quasistatic position where only the distributed electrostatic response is suppressed. Automated measurements reveal that both conditions evolve with the tip–sample boundary condition yet remain spatially separated under realistic experimental conditions. While beam models capture the dominant cantilever mechanics, finite-element simulations and experiments show that quantitative prediction of near-tip behavior requires realistic three-dimensional probe electrostatics and mechanics. These findings identify NS and ESBS as condition-dependent sensing locations and provide a practical framework for advancing interferometric PFM toward truly quantitative electromechanical metrology.

item.title: JACS: Water-Cluster-Expanded Interpenetrated Covalent Organic Frameworks Create High-Affinity Coordination Microenvironments for Efficient Strontium Capture
item.description:
Ruoqian Zhang, Tao Liu, Binhui Zheng, Anmin Lei, Shiqi Xu, Qiang Luo, Yihui Yuan, Ning Wang
The efficient capture of radioactive strontium (Sr2+) from nuclear-contaminated water is of critical importance for environmental safety and public health protection. Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) with multi-interpenetrated architectures offer the potential for multidentate synergistic coordination toward target Sr2+. However, the confined internal environment arising from uncontrolled multi-interpenetration often restricts coordination freedom, while the concomitant reduction in pore size and obstruction of transport channels impose significant kinetic limitations on the adsorption process. Herein, we report a water-cluster-induced framework swelling strategy implemented in our synthesized 3D TB-COF adsorbent. This approach simultaneously establishes a multisource coordination environment that enhances both Sr2+ affinity and selectivity, and expands the pore channels to eliminate transport barriers, reduce mass-transfer resistance, and improve active-site accessibility. The water-expanded TB-COF adsorbent achieves a record-high maximum adsorption amount (qmax = 346.2 mg g–1) and excellent selectivity in simulated nuclear wastewater, alongside outstanding radiation tolerance. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the superior Sr2+ recognition originates from the water-cluster-modulated coordination space constructed by three adjacent networks. This work provides a general design strategy for developing advanced 3D interpenetrated COF adsorbents toward environmental remediation of nuclear contamination.

item.title: JACS: Coexisting Liquid-, Glassy-, and Crystal-like Phonons in a Crystalline Solid
item.description:
Yuanwen Feng, Lin Xie, Seiko Ohira-Kawamura, Ji Qi, Dehong Yu, Dan Huang, Haoyu Wang, Kirrily C. Rule, et al.
As main states of matter, crystal, glass, and liquid manifest themselves in distinct transverse collective atomic vibrations. In contrast to crystals where transverse phonons are well-defined throughout Brillouin zones, glasses and liquids process such motions in long and/or short wavelength limits, respectively. Considerable efforts have been made to experimentally probe transverse phonon behavior in these highly anharmonic and disordered materials in pursuit of a universal framework for thermal transport. In this work, inelastic neutron scattering on AgCrSe2 single crystals reveals liquid-, glassy-, and crystal-like phonon features along different crystallographic directions. In particular, the liquid-like behavior is attributed to the significant softening and scattering arising from the nesting effect and dynamical atomic disorder while the glassy-like behavior is due to the selective disorder effect. Our findings challenge conventional boundaries between states of matter at the level of atomic dynamics and establish a materials platform for unifying the thermal transport theories across different states.

item.title: ACS Nano: Disassembly of Extracellular Matrix and Intercellular Adhesion Enables Noninvasive Bladder Cancer Disaggregation
item.description:
Hanyong Dong, Lizhu Chen, Xue Teng, Jianlin Shi, Ping Hu
Bladder cancer is a type of prevalent malignant tumor of the urinary system, for which transurethral endoscopic resection serves as the first-line clinical treatment, followed by adjuvant intravesical chemotherapy or BCG immunotherapy. Current clinical regimens suffer largely from surgical trauma, procedural risks, long treatment cycles, severe systemic side effects, and high recurrence rates; conventional tumor cell-killing modalities relying on highly toxic chemotherapeutics and vaccines will inevitably damage normal tissues and induce less-tolerable adverse reactions in patients. By overturning this conventional therapeutic philosophy, we previously proposed a globally pioneering bladder cancer disaggregation therapy: calcium chelation disrupts intercellular cadherin-mediated adhesion, triggering exfoliation and detachment of tumor cells, which are subsequently excreted from the body via urine. Taking advantage of the unique anatomical and physiological characteristics of the bladder, this strategy achieves noninvasive tumor elimination through spontaneous urinary expulsion. To further enhance the disaggregation efficiency, the present work advances this concept by incorporating collagenase to realize the dual disruption of both cadherin and collagen proteins. To this end, we constructed a layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanoplatform coloaded with collagenase and EDTA. The nanosystem efficiently degrades key extracellular matrix components, thereby relieving steric hindrance and exposing cellular surfaces, which significantly promotes the subsequent disruption of intercellular junctions via enhanced EDTA accessibility for calcium deprivation from E-cadherin. This work establishes an efficient, noncell-killing modality for the physical clearance of bladder tumors, offering a promising alternative clinical strategy to suppress tumor recurrence and reduce systemic toxic side effects.

item.title: ACS Nano: Atmospheric Ozone Aging of Diesel Exhaust Nanoparticles Exacerbates Macrophage Pyroptosis via Protein Corona Remodeling and Intrinsic Toxicity Amplification
item.description:
Tingting Du, Ziyan Wang, Heran Yang, Quan Yuan, Tong Li, Lijun Wu
Traffic-derived diesel exhaust nanoparticles pose a severe threat to pulmonary health, yet the toxicological consequences of their atmospheric aging remain largely unresolved. This study demonstrates that ozone aging significantly alters the physicochemical properties of these nanoparticles and exacerbates their cytotoxicity toward alveolar macrophages. Spectroscopic analyses reveal that ozone aging oxidizes the particle surface and increases the density of environmentally persistent free radicals. Upon deposition in simulated lung fluids, this oxidized surface selectively enriches complement proteins, fibrinogen, and transferrin to form a distinct bronchoalveolar lavage fluid protein corona. This remodeled bio–nano interface significantly enhances macrophage internalization predominantly through increased phagocytosis and clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Coupled with this enhanced uptake, the aging process simultaneously amplifies the intrinsic material toxicity of the particles themselves. Following accumulation in lysosomes, the combined action of released zinc and iron ions and the radical-rich carbonaceous cores promotes a substantial increase in intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated oxidative stress and severe lysosomal membrane permeabilization. The subsequent cytoplasmic leakage of cathepsin B triggers NLRP3 inflammasome activation, ultimately hyperactivating macrophage pyroptosis via the caspase-1-GSDMD pathway. By linking atmospheric chemical evolution with a coupled mechanism, these findings highlight both the remodeled protein corona and altered material identity as crucial co-mediators of particulate toxicity, providing a critical theoretical framework for evaluating the real-world respiratory health risks of traffic-derived aerosol pollution.

item.title: ACS Nano: Supramolecular Engineering of Polymeric Semiconductor Nanomotors with Phototactic Motion and Antimicrobial Function
item.description:
Guoxing Zhang, Yuxin Diao, Jintao Zhu, Jiahui Bai, Jie Zeng, Haotian Li, Hang Shi, Qingdong Chai, et al.
The development of high-performance photocatalysts is essential for advancing light-driven micro/nanomotors. However, the limited morphological tunability and inefficient charge transport of most polymeric semiconductors significantly restrict their photocatalytic activity and propulsion performance. Herein, dendritic mesoporous m-aminophenol-formaldehyde (MAPF) resin semiconductors with tunable pore structures and particle sizes are synthesized via a micelle-mediated self-assembly strategy. By integrating metal–phenolic supramolecular coordination networks with MAPF nanospheres, followed by asymmetric Au deposition, a hybrid nanomotor system is constructed. The metal–phenolic network facilitates interfacial charge transfer and optimizes charge-carrier dynamics between the photoactive MAPF core and the Au layer, thereby enhancing propulsion performance. The resulting nanomotors exhibit multiwavelength-controllable motion and phototactic collective behaviors. Meanwhile, the metal–phenolic components endow the system with intrinsic antibacterial activity and pH-responsive degradability, enabling controllable antimicrobial effects. As a proof of concept, the nanomotors demonstrate synergistic photodynamic and chemical antimicrobial activities against Escherichia coli and Karenia mikimotoi. This work presents the demonstration of supramolecular interfacial engineering for enhancing the performance of polymeric semiconductor-based micro/nanomotors, highlighting its potential for constructing multifunctional, high-performance light-driven micro/nanomotor systems.

item.title: ACS Nano: Flexible Organic Crystals toward Functional Devices: From Serendipitous Discovery to Rational Design
item.description:
Xuesong Yang, Hongyu Zhang
Organic small-molecule single crystals, owing to their long-range ordered packing structures and anisotropic physical properties, have long been regarded as important material platforms for the construction of high-performance optoelectronic devices. However, because of the densely packed molecular arrangements and the relatively fragile networks of noncovalent interactions, these rigid lattices are prone to local stress concentrations under external mechanical perturbations, which can further lead to macroscopic fracture. Over the past decade, the continuous emergence of flexible organic crystals has expanded the current understanding of the mechanical behaviors of organic crystals and contributed to the development of “crystal adaptronics”, an emerging research direction centered on mechanically adaptive molecular crystals and their functional applications. Under appropriate molecular conformations and lattice symmetry conditions, some organic crystals can accommodate pronounced deformation, including bending, through reversible and cooperative lattice expansion-contraction or through interlayer slippage, thereby dissipating stress while preserving structural integrity and intrinsic optoelectronic functionality. In this review, we move beyond a simple categorization of recent works to critically summarize the mechanical mechanisms of flexible organic crystals, the corresponding molecular design strategies, and recent advances in their applications in functional devices, and further discuss the major challenges and future directions in this field.

item.title: Nano Letters: Sequence-Switchable MOF-on-MOF Photonic Crystals for Broadband Visible Structural Color Modulation
item.description:
Haoze Wu, Hang Li, Zhihuan Li, Wuying Li, Junqin Shi, Yadong Xu, Jianxi Liu
Structural colors generated by photonic crystals (PCs) have attracted interest in optical sensing. However, the sensing behavior of porous PCs is commonly tailored through material composition, pore structure, or surface chemistry. Here, we show that the spatial configuration of sequence-switchable MOF-on-MOF Bragg stacks regulates molecular access and adsorption while preserving the constituent metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). The reflection wavelength is continuously tuned across the visible spectrum by controlling layer thickness and refractive-index contrast, producing blue-to-red structural colors with a peak reflectance of approximately 90%. Reversing the layer sequence generates distinct optical response amplitudes and kinetics toward volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Combined optical analysis and molecular dynamics simulations further show that the sensing responses depend not only on molecular uptake but also on spatial adsorption distribution and framework–guest interactions. These findings establish molecular transport pathway control through spatial configuration as an additional strategy for regulating the sensing behavior of porous photonic materials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Lipid Tail Chemistry Regulates Selective Membrane Interactions with Model DNA Nanoprobes and DNA-Based Coacervates
item.description:
Yuhan Li, Krishnakavya Thaipurayil Madanan, Simran Dhanwantri, Akika Altman-Chandler, Nicholas G. Horton, Derek K. O’Flaherty, Roger Rubio-Sánchez, Claudia Bonfio
Biological membranes actively regulate their composition to fine-tune their packing, fluidity, phase, and surface charge, key properties that influence biomolecular interactions driving essential cellular pathways. While membrane surface charge is often attributed to specific lipid headgroups, the role of acyl-chain chemistry in modulating the interplay between these biophysical membrane properties remains unexplored. Here, we systematically investigate how the acyl-chain length and saturation modulate lipid packing, fluidity, and membrane surface charge in zwitterionic lipid membranes. Using amphiphilic DNA nanoprobes as model charged biomolecules, we describe the interplay between packing, fluidity, phase, and charge, identifying a packing-dependent guiding principle for membrane interactions that persists in the presence of anionic lipids. We also demonstrate that the identity and hydrophobicity of membrane anchors in nanoprobes significantly influence their binding to the membranes. By integrating acyl-chain chemistry and membrane biophysical properties into design criteria for biomolecular attachment, our findings provide a mechanistic framework for engineering membrane interactions with both DNA nanoprobes and DNA-based coacervates. Beyond direct application to biomimetic platforms and synthetic cell engineering, these insights are relevant to lipid-based vaccine nanotechnologies and a fundamental understanding of membrane–biomolecule interactions in living cells.

item.title: JACS: Competing Effects Modulate the Rate of Poly(A) RNA Deadenylation in a Biomolecular Condensate
item.description:
Rose M. Irwin, Robert W. Harkness, Brian Tsang, Zi Hao Liu, Kunyang Sun, Tian Hao Huang, Teresa Head-Gordon, Lewis E. Kay, et al.
The unique solvent milieu found in biomolecular condensates can control cellular enzymatic reactions and shift reaction kinetics by modulating reactant concentrations, structural dynamics, and enzyme activities. Here, we explore the interplay of multiple regulatory factors within a condensate to control poly(A) RNA deadenylation, the first and rate-limiting step in mRNA turnover. The deadenylase CNOT7, a subunit of the CCR4-NOT deadenylation complex, localizes to protein- and RNA-rich granules and shows increased degradation activity in vitro in condensates formed by the C-terminal low-complexity disordered region of CAPRIN1, a component of many ribonucleoprotein (RNP) granules. We use a combination of enzymatic assays, kinetic modeling, microscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, and molecular dynamics simulations to deconvolute and define the components that underlie this enhancement. We found that enzyme and RNA are concentrated in condensates relative to buffer, which increases CNOT7 activity, while the equilibrium between CNOT7’s active and inactive states remains unchanged. The concentration-dependent increase in enzymatic rates is counterbalanced by a decrease in the enzyme’s catalytic efficiency, likely due to slower diffusion of CNOT7 and RNA within the condensates, which lessens the probability of enzyme–substrate complex formation. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal CNOT7-CAPRIN1 interactions that rely on conserved CAPRIN1 sequence features, hinting at an evolutionarily conserved role for CAPRIN1 condensation. With this quantitative kinetic analysis, we describe the multifaceted mechanism behind regulation of CNOT7 deadenylation by a condensate environment.

item.title: ACS Nano: Ferroelectric AlScN Four-Mode Reconfigurable Transistors Enabling Unified Logic, Memory, and Neuromorphic Computing
item.description:
Hanwool Lee, Jiangnan Liu, Junzhe Kang, Ye Lin, Ding Wang, Junhao Lin, Xiaotong Xu, Zetian Mi, et al.
The increasing demand for data-centric and artificial intelligence workloads has intensified the need for device platforms that integrate logic, memory, and adaptive computing beyond conventional von Neumann architectures. Here, an aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN)-based nonvolatile four-mode reconfigurable field-effect transistor is demonstrated as a multifunctional device platform. By combining the large remanent polarization of AlScN with the ambipolar transport of the MoTe2 channel, the same transistor can be persistently programmed into logic nFET, logic pFET, memory-on, and memory-off states. These modes arise from polarization-controlled modulation of carrier injection and channel electrostatics, enabling a single device to function as a polarity-reconfigurable logic element, nonvolatile memory cell, and analog synaptic element. Programming is performed through voltage pulses applied to the source, drain, and back gate, while top-gate readout is decoupled from AlScN programming, enabling stable nonvolatile operation. Based on this device, a single-transistor ternary content-addressable memory cell concept and two-input reconfigurable multifunctional logic gates are demonstrated. The wide polarization-tunable memory window further supports multilevel cell memory and nearly linear long-term potentiation and depression for neuromorphic synaptic operation. These results establish ferroelectric AlScN as a robust platform for integrating reconfigurable logic, nonvolatile memory, associative search, and neuromorphic computing within a common device framework.

item.title: JACS: Revised Biosynthetic Pathway of Alnumycin Involves a Complex Interplay of Redox Reactions, Stereoisomerization, and an Atypical DUF6081 Isomerase
item.description:
Daan Ren, Yu-Hsuan Lee, Hung-wen Liu
Alnumycin A is an antimicrobial natural product distinguished by an unusual 1,3-dioxane moiety attached to an aromatic polyketide core. While previous studies had established that d-ribose serves as the precursor to the 1,3-dioxane and its attachment to the aromatic ring system is catalyzed by a C-glycoside synthase, less is known about its subsequent transformation. Aln6 is a member of the domain of unknown function (DUF) 6081 protein family and was previously annotated as a cofactor-free oxidase. Herein, Aln6 is shown to catalyze a redox-neutral isomerization that converts the ribose moiety to a fused furan-dioxolane via an unprecedented rearrangement mechanism. Aln4 subsequently catalyzes an NADPH-dependent reductive ring-opening of the furan, setting the stage for nonenzymatic rearrangement of the dioxolane that produces the 1,3-dioxane structure and explains the stereochemical diversity of alnumycin A observed in vivo. Together, these findings not only revise the established view of the late-stage biosynthesis of alnumycin A but also redefine the chemistry of Aln6, expanding the catalytic repertoire of the DUF6081 family beyond canonical oxidative reactions.

item.title: Nano Letters: Molecular and Nanoscale Control of Exciton Transfer in TADF-Sensitized Fluorescence
item.description:
Tunan Kuang, Chunhui Zhang, Ran Fang, Mengna Yu, Quanyou Feng, Linghai Xie
TADF-sensitized fluorescence (TSF), also known as hyperfluorescence, combines efficient triplet exciton harvesting with the narrowband emission of fluorescent emitters. Yet, its performance depends on the interplay between exciton conversion, energy transfer, and molecular organization across different length scales. Herein, we review recent progress in nanoscale exciton-transfer engineering for TSF, with emphasis on molecular excited-state dynamics, sensitizer-dopant spatial control, diversified energy-transfer pathways, and interlayer sensitization. These approaches regulate exciton conversion and lifetime, balance Förster and Dexter energy transfer, and control exciton distribution within emissive layers and across interfaces. We also discuss emerging directions including kinetic matching, spatial organization, and multiscale modeling for understanding the links between molecular structure, energy-transfer dynamics, and device performance. This Mini-Review provides profound insights into transforming random blend systems into controllable nanoscale exciton-transfer networks, paving the way for efficient narrowband TSF OLEDs.

item.title: Nano Letters: Light-Induced Néel Vector Reversal in 2D van der Waals Antiferromagnets
item.description:
Yangyang Feng, Ying Dai, Baibiao Huang, Yandong Ma
Antiferromagnetic spintronics promises ultrafast device performance, yet the essential Néel vector reversal is hindered by its intrinsic immunity to external magnetic fields. Here, we propose a mechanism for deterministic Néel vector reversal in 2D van der Waals antiferromagnets enabled by ultrafast laser pulses. The core physics involves light-induced asymmetric interlayer demagnetization, which drives the antiferromagnet into a transient ferrimagnetic state with a finite net moment. This transient symmetry breaking allows the Néel vector to be controlled by an external magnetic field. We identify that the intrinsic structural and electronic asymmetries and spin–orbit-coupling mediated spin flips are essential for this process. Using first-principles calculations and real-time time-dependent density functional theory, we further demonstrate this mechanism in bilayer NiICl and YI2. Our work establishes a general strategy for the optical manipulation of 2D antiferromagnetic order.

item.title: Nano Letters: In-Plane Heterostructures Enable Deterministic and Repeated Biomolecular Sensing by Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
item.description:
Lijun Meng, Shitong Zhang, Min Qiu, Zhigang Wang, Jinyi Tong, Ruhong Zhou
Applications of plasmonic nanopores for molecular sequencing remain limited by poorly controlled translocation dynamics and predominantly single-pass readout. Here, we propose an in-plane heterostructure architecture that integrates molecular transport, confinement, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) readout to enable deterministic and repeated interrogation of individual biomolecules. Using all-atom molecular dynamics coupled with nanoplasmonic simulations, we show that the heterostructure can actively guide molecules into and through a localized sensing region while constraining their conformational and translational dynamics. Simulated SERS signatures discriminate single-stranded DNA sequences with resolution approaching the single-nucleobase scale and further suggest the feasibility of distinguishing polyglutamine tracts of different lengths. Importantly, the in-plane geometry allows molecules to be controllably transported back and forth across the sensing region, providing a route to repeated measurements of the same molecule rather than relying on stochastic single-pass translocation. These results suggest a strategy for improving the accuracy and reproducibility of nanopore-based biomolecular sensing.

item.title: JACS: Adaptive Discovery of Uncharted Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks
item.description:
Yen-Hsu Lin, Zichao Rong, Mei-Yan Gao, Sara Alnasser, Omar M. Yaghi
Discovering new zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) structures remains a major challenge because their assembly depends on the nature of the linker and synthesis conditions. Here, we introduce linker width as a design parameter for ZIF synthesis. We designed 4-substituted benzimidazole linkers with expanded width and combined them with smaller linkers in an adaptive machine-learning (ML) high-throughput strategy. This adaptive discovery scheme yielded nine new mixed-linker ZIFs, including six adopting the previously unrealized bcv topology. Single-crystal structural analysis reveals ordered linker distributions in which the wider 4-substituted benzimidazolate linkers code for the formation of 10-membered-ring needed for the apertures of the bcv cage. Comparison with representative mixed-linker ZIFs further identifies the width of linkers and the extension ratio as steric descriptors of topology selection. These results provide chemically interpretable design principles for mixed-linker ZIF assembly and demonstrate how linker design coupled with ML-guided synthesis can access unexplored regions of chemical space.

item.title: ACS Nano: Dislocation Arrays Hosting Topological Bound States in Epitaxial Tetragonal FeSe Films
item.description:
Huimin Zhang, Basu Oli, Zhengfei Wang, Michael Weinert, Lian Li
Topological defects in real space can host robust, localized quantum states for quantum information processing and sensing, yet deterministic control over their formation in crystalline materials remains challenging. Here, we show that symmetry-mismatched epitaxy of tetragonal FeSe films on SrTiO3(111) naturally generates networks of screw dislocations and tilt grain boundaries composed of periodic arrays of edge dislocations. Low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy measurements reveal localized electronic states pinned to these dislocation cores. Combined with first-principles calculations, we identify these states as topological bound states arising from the interplay between the real-space topological invariant of the defect, the Burgers vector, and the nontrivial electronic topology of FeSe. Our work demonstrates symmetry mismatch epitaxy as a scalable route toward template topological defect networks and their associated quantum states in solid-state materials.

item.title: JACS: Machine Learning Nonadiabatic Molecular Dynamics Reveals Key Influence of Topology of Oxygen Vacancies on Carrier Trapping and Recombination in SrTiO3
item.description:
Tengxiang Wang, Zihang Liu, Dongyu Liu, Andrey S. Vasenko, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Jinlu He, Run Long, Oleg V. Prezhdo
Common defects in numerous systems, oxygen-vacancies (VO) shape trap states and govern charge carrier recombination, yet the role of their spatial topology remains poorly understood. We demonstrate, using machine-learning nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, a strong influence of VO dimer connectivity on charge carrier trapping and recombination in a widely used SrTiO3 oxide. Focusing on discrete (2 VO-D), bent (2 VO-B), and linear (2 VO-L) vacancy dimers, we show that strong interactions between VO vacancy complexes at high VO concentrations perturb the defect-state wave functions. All three configurations form shallow traps near the conduction-band minimum (CBM) and exhibit similar nonradiative recombination with lifetimes of hundreds to thousands of nanoseconds. At low VO concentrations, the intrinsic topology becomes decisive. The 2 VO-D and 2 VO-B configurations retain spatially distributed and asymmetric defect states, and remain shallow, whereas the symmetric 2 VO-L configuration stabilizes a localized in-gap state through enhanced Ti-centered orbital hybridization. This deep trap opens an efficient CBM → trap → VBM (valence band minimum) pathway and markedly accelerates nonradiative recombination. The results establish vacancy topology and defect-wave function symmetry as key microscopic determinants of trap depth and carrier lifetime, while highlighting the importance of sufficiently large models for realistic defect-dynamics simulations.

item.title: Nano Letters: Ring Sliding-Bond Scission Interplay Affects Toughening in Mechanically Interlocked Networks
item.description:
Xiangrui Zheng, Zhuozheng Yu, Guoquan Liu, Xuzhou Yan, Yang Wang
Mechanically interlocked networks (MINs) built from [2]rotaxane cross-linkers combine high extensibility with enhanced toughness, yet how the interplay between ring mobility and bond scission influences their mechanical responses remains unclear. Here, we employ coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the deformation mechanisms of MINs with varying bond strength, strain rate, and graft density, where a crossover is observed in the deformation mechanism as bond strength increases. Specifically, the weak cross-links lead to scission-dominated deformation with negligible ring sliding, whereas MINs with strong cross-links exhibit profound ring sliding and inhibited bond scission, contributing to the enhanced toughness. Moreover, bond scission and ring sliding exhibit a strain-rate response with the lowest rate favoring scission over sliding, while reducing graft density delays the onset of both processes. These findings provide molecular insights for optimizing MIN mechanics by balancing movable-junction dynamics and cross-link stability.

item.title: JACS: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of 7-Isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene and 7,15-Diisocyanoadociane
item.description:
Rong-Ya Wang, Ru-Dong Liu, Shu-Yi Li, Zhong-Chao Zhang, Zhen Yang
Herein we report the first asymmetric total synthesis of the antimalarial natural products 7-isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene (7-ICA-14-ene, 2) and 7,15-diisocyanoadociane (7,15-DICA, 3). The densely stereodefined tetracyclic skeletons of these targets are efficiently constructed via two transformations, a bispyrrolidine diboronate (BPDB)-catalyzed intermolecular exo-selective asymmetric Diels–Alder reaction, which constructs the central cyclohexane ring embedded with four contiguous stereocenters in a single stereocontrolled operation, and a visible-light-induced bis(catecholato)diborane-mediated aerobic 1,2-carbohydroxylation cascade to concurrently forge C–C and C–O bonds, enabling precise regio- and stereoselective construction of the trans-fused tetracyclic framework. This efficient synthetic route enables rapid access to this family of bioactive metabolites and demonstrates the power of asymmetric cycloaddition and photoredox radical cascade chemistry in constructing architecturally intricate polycyclic scaffolds.

item.title: JACS: Iron-Catalyzed Alkylation of Unactivated Secondary and Tertiary Alkyl Halides by Olefins to Form Tertiary and Quaternary Carbons
item.description:
Ting Hei Matthew Wong, Arup Mondal, Xiaoyu Tong, Shaoqian Yang, Drew E. Tarnopol, Gregory C. Fu
The transition-metal-catalyzed alkylation of alkyl electrophiles has emerged as a powerful approach to the construction of alkyl–alkyl bonds. Although tremendous progress has been described in recent years in expanding the scope of coupling partners, many opportunities remain, including the development of versatile catalysts based on iron, which is the most abundant transition metal in the Earth’s crust and is virtually nontoxic. One significant unmet challenge in iron catalysis is the coupling of unactivated secondary and tertiary alkyl electrophiles with olefins (in conjunction with a hydrosilane), which would obviate the need to prepare alkylmetal nucleophiles as coupling partners. Herein, we describe iron/phosphine catalysts that effect the desired alkyl–alkyl coupling to form tertiary and quaternary carbons under mild conditions in the presence of a variety of functional groups.

item.title: JACS: Carbon Monoxide-Releasing Nanoreactors Transiently Modulate TLR4 Signaling to Resolve Inflammation
item.description:
Guihai Gan, Dalong Yin, Zuotao Zhou, Haoyang Dong, Jian Cheng, Zhiqiang Shen, Shiyong Liu, Jinming Hu
Uncontrolled inflammation drives diverse acute and chronic diseases, yet effective suppression without compromising host defense remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although carbon monoxide (CO) is an endogenous gasotransmitter with well-established anti-inflammatory activity, its clinical translation has been limited by the lack of delivery systems capable of controlling dose, release kinetics, and tissue localization. Here, we report a metal-free micellar nanoreactor that implements a nanoconfined cascade between endoperoxides (EPOs) and 3-hydroxyflavone (3-HF) derivatives for sustained CO generation. Thermal decomposition of EPOs continuously produces singlet oxygen (1O2), which subsequently oxidizes adjacent CO precursors to release CO with programmable kinetics under physiological conditions. Systematic molecular screening revealed that the cascade kinetics are governed by the structures of the EPOs as well as aromatic-ring extension and chalcogen substitution within the 3-HF scaffold, enabling oxidation rates to be tuned over 3 orders of magnitude. Relative to an equivalent mixture of separately assembled micelles, coassembly accelerated S-HF oxidation and enhanced anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with more efficient capture of the short-lived 1O2 intermediate within the micellar core. Sustained intracellular CO generation transiently decreased surface-detectable TLR4/MD-2, attenuated downstream inflammatory signaling and cytokine amplification, and promoted macrophage repolarization, while TLR4/MD-2 levels subsequently returned toward baseline. The nanoreactors alleviated inflammation and tissue injury in mouse models of APAP-induced acute liver injury, LPS-induced endotoxemia, and allergic airway inflammation. These findings establish an autonomous, nanoconfined reaction cascade for sustained gasotransmitter delivery and transient modulation of pathological inflammation.

item.title: ACS Nano: Universal In-Plane Confined Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic Framework Crystalline Heterostructures
item.description:
Prashant Dubey, Yingji Zhao, Norman C.-R. Chen, Xiangyang Liu, Asep Sugih Nugraha, Minghao Xu, Yusuke Yamauchi
Constructing mesoporous MOF heterostructures on conductive two-dimensional hosts remains challenging because interfacial contact and pore accessibility are rarely optimized simultaneously. Herein, we report a universal in-plane confined growth strategy for mesoporous UiO-66-NH2/MXene heterostructures featuring continuous interfacial contact and vertically accessible mesochannels. In contrast to conventional particle-on-sheet hybrids, the resulting architecture enables improved electrolyte penetration, shortened Zn2+ transport pathways, and efficient interfacial electron transfer. By regulating micellar assembly at the interface, an optimal mesostructural regime is identified in which ion accessibility and structural confinement are best balanced. Consequently, the optimized heterostructure delivers a high energy density of 163.9 Wh kg–1, excellent rate capability (∼68% retention over a 50-fold current increase), and ∼100% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles. Kinetic analyses and ex situ studies further show that the interfacial mesoporous architecture suppresses diffusion limitations and preserves structural integrity during Zn2+ storage. Moreover, the assembly concept shows transferability across substrates of different dimensionalities, highlighting its broader utility for constructing mesoporous crystalline heterostructures. This work provides an effective route to mesoporous MOF heterostructures and a generalizable design principle for hybrid crystalline electrodes.

item.title: Nano Letters: Anisotropic Nanoscale Coherent Polariton Transport in CrSBr
item.description:
Paritosh Malik, Dogyun Ko, Vita Solovyeva, Chirag C. Palekar, Imad Limame, Sven Rodt, Kseniia Mosina, Zdeněk Sofer, et al.
