In a combined experimental and theoretical study, we demonstrate anisotropic polariton transport on the nanoscale in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr. While effective cavity-polariton formation emerges via the self-hybridization of ultrahigh oscillator strength excitons with a thin slab photonic mode, the absence of external mirrors facilitates spectroscopic investigation of these polaritons via cathodoluminescence (CL) on length scales inaccessible to optical excitation. This direct access allows us to precisely chart the polariton landscape with nanometric resolution, and probe polariton interference phenomena. Our finding highlights that coherent polariton transport follows the C2v symmetry of CrSBr, highly directional transport along the a-axis, while no coherent features are found along the b-axis. By extending CL spectroscopy to strongly anisotropic cavity polaritons, our work establishes this technique as a powerful tool to probe highly directional expansion and relaxation phenomena on the nanoscale, paving the way for investigating complex polaritonic landscapes in asymmetric systems.

item.title: Nano Letters: Divalent Cations Induce Rigid and Compact Structures in Underwound DNA
item.description:
Aleksander Klimczyk, Dorothy Aboagye-Mensah, Graeme A. King
Negative supercoiling (underwinding) of DNA plays a vital role in regulating genome organization and gene expression. These processes often depend on the DNA structure, yet the influence of ionic strength on supercoiled DNA structure is still not well understood. Here, we develop an approach to extract detailed insight into the mechanical properties of underwound DNA from force–distance measurements. Using this approach, we demonstrate that low concentrations (2 mM) of divalent cations are sufficient to induce substantial increases in DNA persistence length at high superhelical densities. This is consistent with the formation of Z-DNA, a rigid, left-handed conformation, and suggests that Z-DNA-like structures can be more readily formed than is often assumed. We also show that divalent cations can induce extensive sawtooth-like behavior in force–extension curves of underwound DNA, revealing unexpectedly strong stabilization of secondary structures. Together, these findings demonstrate how divalent salt can sensitively modulate the stability of different underwound structures.

item.title: JACS: Porous Framework Assembly Creates Functional Tertiary Folds in Small Peptides
item.description:
Pragati Ganatra, Daniel F. Wang, Bidyut K. Kundu, Prithwiraj Jana, Dan McElheny, Savannah Nichols, Pamela J. Focia, Joseph S. Brunzelle, et al.
There is significant interest in recreating the protein tertiary structure in simpler systems, which can enable the precise and modular organization of multiple functional groups for enhancing molecular recognition and catalysis. Small peptides are minimalist analogs of proteins; however, their limited size highly disfavors folding into tertiary structures, especially those that also possess open binding sites needed for function. Here, we report that 3-dimensional self-assembly into a porous crystalline framework overcomes this limitation, producing modular tertiary structures in peptides shorter than 20 amino acids with tunable binding sites. As shown by X-ray crystallography, this framework-mediated folding tolerates many sequences with a broad range of functional groups, and it generates precise confined environments that are dynamic and mutationally robust. Thus, these pores can be programmed to selectively bind complex molecular guests such as nucleotides and perfluoroalkyl substances through the cooperative engagement of up to 10 distinct residues. These results demonstrate that a well-defined tertiary structure can exist in very short peptides and can impart tunable protein-like function to synthetic porous materials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Molecular Single-Photon Emitters across Chemical Space: Substrate Effects and Design Principles
item.description:
Haiyuan Wang, Mikael Kuisma, Tara Boland, Kristian Sommer Thygesen
Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are an emerging molecular platform for single-photon emitters, but predictive design strategies across chemical space have been lacking. Here we establish two general principles governing PAH/hBN emitters. The zero-phonon-line energy is molecule-controlled and robust to the substrate environment, whereas the Huang–Rhys (HR) factor is environment-governed and exhibits two distinct regimes. Pristine hBN modestly enhances HR through soft interfacial modes. In contrast, the NB antisite defect, introduced to immobilize the molecules, produces a molecule-specific HR response that cannot be predicted from gas-phase or pristine-hBN data alone. Strikingly, the defect can either partially restore the HR factor toward its intrinsic gas-phase value or amplify it by up to 3.7×, depending on the molecule. This positions defect engineering as a tunable design knob for vibronic coupling in molecule/hBN emitters. Combining high-throughput hybrid density functional theory (DFT) screening of 662 PAHs identifies 47 gas-phase candidates with low HR factors and high radiative rates spanning the near-infrared to ultraviolet. Among five representative candidates explicitly tested on NB@hBN, two retain HR factors below unity in gas-phase, pristine hBN, and defect-bound environments. However, no PAH simultaneously exhibits favorable single-photon-emitter properties and an excited-state singlet–triplet splitting below 0.5 eV, suggesting that PAH-based spin–photon interfaces will require further molecular design. All data are released through the open MolExDB platform.

item.title: Nano Letters: Streptavidin–Biotin Binding Is Intrinsically Noncooperative, but Experimental Artifacts Can Induce Apparent Positive Cooperativity
item.description:
Malavika Kayyil Veedu, Eléonore Martenne Duplan, Saurabh Rai, Prithu Roy, Jérôme Wenger
The biotin–streptavidin interaction is a key component of nanobiotechnology, yet the nature of its cooperativity remains a debated question. Here, we introduce a label-free spectroscopy approach based on confocal UV autofluorescence microscopy to probe the binding cooperativity of this high-affinity system. By leveraging the intrinsic autofluorescence of tryptophan residues, we avoid artifacts associated with extrinsic fluorescent labels, enabling precise measurements of fully biotin-saturated streptavidin across a wide range of molar ratios. Our experimental results, supported by Monte Carlo simulations, provide conclusive evidence for the absence of cooperativity. However, we show that false signs of apparent positive cooperativity can emerge from local concentration inhomogeneities occurring when rapid reaction kinetics outpace mixing. By establishing the noncooperative nature of biotin–streptavidin binding and identifying the key conditions to avoid cooperativity artifacts, these insights resolve a longstanding debate and offer critical implications for streptavidin-based biotechnological applications.

item.title: JACS: Anionic Phase-Transfer Catalysis for Constructing Chiral Sulfur Centers via Asymmetric Sulfinimidation
item.description:
Xin-Yang Lv, Julia A. Turner, Sven Roediger, Matthew M. Pompeo, Samantha Ly, Francis Gosselin, Abigail G. Doyle, Matthew S. Sigman, et al.
Chiral anion phase-transfer (CAPT) catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric catalysis, yet its stereocontrol modes remain largely limited to π-face differentiation or enantiotopic bond selection. The ability to exert stereocontrol through enantioselective recognition of heteroatom lone pairs remains underdeveloped, restricting catalytic access to configurationally stable heteroatom-centered stereocenters. Here, we report a CAPT platform that enables asymmetric sulfinimidation through enantioselective halogenation of prochiral sulfur(II) lone pairs, providing direct access to chiral aryl and alkyl sulfinimidate esters with high enantioselectivity. Mechanistic studies and computational investigations confirm that halogenation is the enantiodetermining step, forming a chiral, configurationally stable sulfinimidoyl fluoride intermediate. Enantioselective oxidation of prochiral sulfides indicates that this CAPT lone-pair recognition platform may be more generally applicable to heteroatom lone pairs. These findings establish lone-pair differentiation as a new mode of stereocontrol in CAPT and expand the conceptual scope of chiral anionic catalysis toward the asymmetric synthesis of chiral organosulfur compounds.

item.title: JACS: Hierarchical Engineering of Atomically Precise Gold Nanoclusters from Alloying to Cluster-Assembled Frameworks
item.description:
Kyoung Chul Park, Seong-Hyeon Park, Sarah S. Park
Atomically precise gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) provide molecular-level platforms for understanding how atomic structure influences catalytic, photophysical, chiral, and electronic properties. Although alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and nanocluster assembly have each emerged as powerful approaches for tailoring Au NC function, they are often considered as separate design strategies. In this perspective, we organize recent advances in Au NC design across three interconnected levels of structural control: core alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and cluster-assembled materials. We discuss how alloying modifies the intrinsic electronic structure of the NC core, how ligand and interface engineering regulate the expression of these properties through electronic and structural control, and how coordination-mediated assembly organizes individual NCs into aggregates, superstructures, and crystalline frameworks with collective photophysical and electronic properties. By connecting these design strategies, this perspective provides a hierarchical view of Au NC design that links molecular precision to materials-level functionality and highlights opportunities for catalysis, sensing, optoelectronics, and nanoelectronics.

item.title: JACS: Spin-Chirality-Driven Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in van der Waals Magnet CrSBr
item.description:
Dezhao Wu, Yong Xu, Meng Ye, Wenhui Duan
The bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) manifests with remarkable diversity in magnetic materials. Here, we establish vector spin chirality as a tunable knob for generating an unconventional time-reversal-even magnetic BPVE, comprising the chiral shift current (CSC) and chiral injection current (CIC). Using bilayer antiferromagnetic (AFM) CrSBr as a prototype, we theoretically demonstrate the emergence of CSC and CIC. Compared with conventional photovoltaic currents arising from noncentrosymmetric crystal structures or collinear magnetic orderings, CSC and CIC not only possess comparable magnitudes but also exhibit exceptional tunability. Specifically, they can be switched on and off by magnetic-field-induced spin canting, reversed in direction upon canting-direction reversal, and continuously modulated in intensity via canting-angle variation. Furthermore, we reveal an unusual optical transition channel governing both currents in CrSBr. Our work establishes an unconventional magnetic BPVE with remarkable controllability, offering opportunities for optoelectronic and magnetic-sensing applications in noncollinear magnets.

item.title: Nano Letters: (PEA)2(FA)Pb2I7/PVDF Composite Flexible Films Enable Self-Powered X-ray Detection with High Sensitivity and a Low Detection Limit
item.description:
Yuanxiang You, Yaping Gong, Qilin Wei, Huanxin Su, Haojie Xu, Zengshan Yue, Dan Huang, William W. Yu, et al.
Metal halide perovskites (MHPs) have attracted significant interest in the field of X-ray detection due to their unique semiconducting properties. However, the self-powered detection capabilities of almost all of these materials rely on their inherent ferroelectricity or heterojunction structures, yet the structure design and fabrication still pose significant challenges. By incorporating a polymer into a centrosymmetric MHP, we successfully prepared (PEA)2(FA)Pb2I7/PVDF composite flexible films (PEA = β-phenylethylamine, FA = formamidine, PVDF = poly(vinylidene fluoride)) and obtained self-powered X-ray responses in a nonpolar perovskite. Notably, the photodetector based on thin films exhibits excellent self-powered X-ray detection performance with a high sensitivity (559.11 μC Gyair–1 cm–2), a low detection limit (29.09 nGyair s–1), and excellent radiation stability. Our work offers a new strategy for self-driven devices without relying on ferroelectricity or heterojunctions, expanding halide perovskites in flexible film applications.

item.title: ACS Nano: Rapid-Mixing In Situ X-ray Diffraction Reveals Precursor-Reorganization Signatures in Additive-Free Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8 Nanoparticle Formation
item.description:
Shotaro Danjo, Shogo Kawaguchi, Shotaro Hiraide, Satoshi Watanabe
Controlling particle size and phase purity in solution-processed metal–organic frameworks requires understanding how disordered precursors evolve before they crystallize into the final framework. However, capturing this precursor-to-crystal conversion remains a key challenge. Here, we couple a central-collision-type microreactor with time-resolved in situ X-ray diffraction to track the additive-free formation of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) in water–methanol cosolvents, achieving 5 s temporal resolution after submillisecond micromixing. The setup directly captures crystal appearance, apparent crystallization kinetics, and subsequent lattice relaxation. Crystallization is fastest at 40–50 vol % methanol, where Bragg reflections appear earliest and grow most rapidly. Water-rich media approach a competing phase boundary between ZIF-8 and layered zeolitic imidazolate framework-L (ZIF-L) and yield a predominantly amorphous product at the water-rich extreme, whereas methanol-rich media form pure ZIF-8 more slowly. After crystallinity emerges, the apparent lattice constant contracts, indicating that the earliest Bragg-detectable domains undergo lattice relaxation as growth proceeds. Strikingly, raising the total reactant concentration at a fixed metal-to-linker ratio delays crystal appearance and yields larger particles, contrary to the behavior typically expected in a nucleation-dominated system. We propose that concentration-dependent precursor accumulation, coarsening, and interconnection, coupled to metal–ligand network reorganization, link these contrasting trends.

item.title: Nano Letters: Iron-Chelating Nanoparticles Enable Cytoprotection against Ferroptosis In Vitro and In Vivo
item.description:
Juyeon Kim, Jaewoo Lee, Gyusang Yu, Seh Ri Oh, Yunseo Jung, Shafinaz Abd Gani, Sungmin Nam, Nathaniel S. Hwang
Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial dysfunction, contributes to degenerative and ischemic diseases, yet strategies that simultaneously control labile iron and oxidative stress remain limited. Here, we developed mesoporous polydopamine nanoparticles (PDNs) with intrinsic antioxidant and iron-chelating properties. PDNs scavenged free radicals, reduced intracellular Fe2+ levels, preserved mitochondrial function, and rescued ferroptotic cell death in iron overload- and erastin-induced models. Untargeted metabolomics revealed that PDNs restored ferroptosis-associated metabolic profiles, including metabolites related to glutathione metabolism and energy production. In an erastin-induced muscle ferroptosis model, PDNs reduced lipid peroxidation and restored GPX4 expression. In a hindlimb ischemia model, PDNs enhanced blood perfusion and vascular recovery. Together, these findings establish PDNs as a multifunctional nanoplatform that suppresses ferroptosis through coordinated regulation of iron homeostasis, redox balance, mitochondrial function, and metabolism, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for ferroptosis-associated muscle degeneration and ischemic injury.

item.title: JACS: Metal-Free Synthesis of Unsymmetrical B–B Bond via Pyridyl-Directed m -Carborane Borylation
item.description:
Weilong Zheng, Jie Zhang, Wenqi Xu, Yizhen Liu, Zuowei Xie
Constructing B–B single bonds has long challenged boron chemists, as diboranes serve as crucial precursors for B–X bond formation. Traditional routes rely on strongly reducing metals for homocoupling, leaving unsymmetrical B–B bonds inaccessible. We report herein a metal-free strategy for regioselective B(2)–H borylation of m-carboranes with BBr3, forging unsymmetrical B–B bonds. Cooperative dual pyridyl moieties promote in situ generation of intramolecular Lewis pairs, driving B–H bond activation and borylation. The resulting B(2)–BBr2-m-carboranes are bench-stable and function as versatile intermediates, enabling synthesis of diverse B–BR2 derivatives (R = H, Me, Ph, OH, etc.).
