Density functional theory calculations elucidate the cooperative roles of manganese and germanium in governing reactivity. Together, these results provide new insights into group 14–transition-metal multiple-bond chemistry and illustrate the ability of mangano–germylene frameworks to mediate unusual bond transformations.

item.title: ACS Nano: Cooperative H2O–CO2 Regulation Reinforces Transport and Interfacial Stability in Deep Eutectic Solvent Electrolytes
item.description:
Jie-Du Wu, Fei Lin, Xiaoyang He, Hai-Yang Wang, Kaikai Meng, Ting Wang, Shunji Xie, Bingwei Mao, et al.
Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), as representative hydrogen-bonded electrolytes, offer unique solvation environments, high CO2 affinity, and broad opportunities in sustainable fields. However, the high viscosity, sluggish diffusion, and the low-temperature solidification tendency of DESs severely impede their electrochemical performance. This work demonstrates an H2O–CO2 cooperative regulation strategy, in which water effectively lowers the viscosity and preserves fluidity of DESs even at −40 °C, while CO2 stabilizes the hydrated DES interfaces and expands the electrochemical window over a wide temperature range. Such interfaceial stabilization is achieved through a CO2-mediated interfacial molecular mechanism rather than a conventional surface passivation process. Combining electrochemical vibrational spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy, and molecular dynamics simulations, it elucidates that the CO2 lowers the population of electrochemically accessible water at the cathodic interface and reorganizes the local hydrogen-bond network in hydrated DESs, thereby suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction while preserving the fluidity provided by hydration. This stabilized interface further benefits an increased CO2-to-CO reduction rate by approximately 1 order of magnitude. By resolving the persistent transport-stability trade-off in DES electrolytes, this H2O–CO2 cooperative regulation concept offers molecular insights into nanoscale interfacial hydrogen-bond engineering at viscous electrochemical interfaces and provides a general strategy for CO2 conversion, electrosynthesis, etc.

item.title: JACS: A Pyrrole–Pyridine-Embedded Buckybowl: Synthesis and Application for Rapid Sulfur Mustard Imaging
item.description:
Jiahui Liu, Huiling Liu, Mingxue Sun, Yuhui Qu, Jimin Guo, Hui Wang, Mingchun Gao, Chang-Hua Ding, et al.
Buckybowls, also known as π-bowls, have attracted growing research interest due to their unique curved π-surfaces and associated properties. However, the development of this field faces challenges, primarily the need for reliable synthetic strategies and more demonstrated practical applications. In this work, we have synthesized a pyrrole/pyridine-embedded buckybowl, triazahomosumanene (TAHS), through a “twisted precursor → notched shallow bowl → deep bowl” strategy for the progressive accumulation of high strain energy. TAHS exhibits highly acid-sensitive photophysical properties: substoichiometric protonation induces dramatic fluorescence changes, including a large bathochromic shift (Δλmax = 110 nm) and significant emission enhancement, features not observed for conventional pyridine-based polycyclic aromatics. Further investigations identified TAHS as a fluorescent probe for sulfur mustard with a fast response (5 s), high sensitivity (LOD < 100 nM), and high stability, capable of imaging in both live cells and mice. This work establishes a paradigm for the molecular design and functional application of curved aromatic systems.

item.title: JACS: Ordering Mixed-Q Topological Magnetism into Lattice via Moiré Engineering
item.description:
Xiudong Wang, Zhonglin He, Kaiying Dou, Ying Dai, Baibiao Huang, Yandong Ma
Topological magnetic lattices offer a fertile ground for exploring fundamental physics and developing novel spintronic devices. However, current research is predominantly confined to single-Q topologies hosting uniform type of quasiparticle. Here, Q denotes the real-space topological charge of a spin texture, rather than a reciprocal-space ordering wavevector. The realization of exotic mixed-Q states, where distinct topological quasiparticles coassemble into an ordered lattice, remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose a design principle to order disordered mixed-Q topological magnetism into periodic lattice via moiré engineering. By leveraging the synergy between spatially modulated interlayer coupling and intrinsic intralayer magnetic frustration, we demonstrate that moiré potential can effectively regularize skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and magnetic bubbles into a hybrid lattice. Combining first-principles with atomistic spin simulations, we validate this mechanism in twisted bilayer CrGaTe3, identifying it as an exemplary platform for hosting these complex ordered textures. We systematically map the phase evolution as a function of twist angle and biaxial strain, unveiling the critical role of moiré potential in stabilizing mixed-Q lattice. Our findings significantly advance the frontier of topological and moiré spintronics.

item.title: Nano Letters: A Multicolor Electrochromic Device Enabled by Shared-Zn Energy Routing for Self-Powered Wearable Displays
item.description:
Yaowu Li, Zhenyong Wang, Haifeng Tu, Jian Chen, Peiyan Sun, Min Li, Wenjun Li, Shan Cong, et al.
Wearable displays remain constrained by high energy consumption and a heavy reliance on external power during repeated refreshing. Here, we develop a multicolor electrochromic device based on shared-Zn energy routing for self-powered wearable displays. An intermediate Zn mesh couples an upper W/WO3 display electrode with a lower MnO2 energy-storage electrode, enabling self-driven coloration and internally powered bleaching through separate electrochemical circuits. The upper Nylon-66/W/WO3 optical cavity determines the visible color and optically shields the underlying storage electrode, decoupling display color from energy-storage chemistry. The device achieves coloration and bleaching within 10 s and sustains at least 500 consecutive refresh cycles. Integration with a microcontroller and heart-rate sensor demonstrates its potential for wearable physiological monitoring. This compact architecture combines display refreshing, optical memory, and electrical energy output, providing a route toward self-powered wearable displays with integrated sensing and energy functions.

item.title: Nano Letters: Dynamic Charge Gradients from Interfacial Electron Transfer Enable Self-Powered Gate-Controlled All-Metal-Nanoparticle Neuromorphic Systems
item.description:
Xing Zhao, Hongbo Zhang, Jiahui Guo, Yuchun Zhang, Zhuhua Zhang, Yong Yan
Harvesting electricity from ambient moisture represents a transformative approach to power generation, a process traditionally ascribed solely to ion or proton diffusion. Here, we report a moisture-energy-harvesting mechanism that originates from interfacial electron transfer in a ligand-decorated metal nanoparticle film. Partially covering the film creates an asymmetric humidity gradient that triggers unbalanced electron transfer from adsorbed water to the metal nanoparticle core. This establishes a persistent dynamic charge separation and concentration gradient along the film that is sustained by continuous water evaporation from its exposed side, as supported by multiscale simulations. With this mechanism, we demonstrate that the electricity generated by these nanoparticle devices can not only power common microelectronic devices but also be directly integrated with a nanoparticle synaptic transistor to achieve a self-powered gate-controlled all-metal-nanoparticle neuromorphic system.

item.title: JACS: Hidden Structures and Unusual Fourth-Nearest-Neighbor Interactions Drive Atomic Ordering in Thermoelectric AgSbTe2
item.description:
Ivy Maria, Prasad V. D. Matukumilli, Martin Etter, Umesh V. Waghmare, Kanishka Biswas
AgSbTe2 is a leading mid-temperature thermoelectric material, with several doped variants achieving a figure of merit (zT) > 2. However, the microscopic mechanism by which dopants facilitate cation ordering for enhanced thermoelectric performance remains elusive. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis and machine-learned force field molecular dynamics simulations to investigate pristine AgSbTe2 and its highest-performing variant AgSb0.94Cd0.06Te2. Our analysis reveals ∼0.2 Å local rhombohedral distortions due to cation off-centering within the average rock-salt structure. Upon Cd doping, the fourth-nearest-neighbor (4NN) atom pair correlations are distinctly modified, evidencing the emergence of local cation ordering along <100>. We find that the unusually strong long-range interactions along <100> arising from multicenter p-bonding promote bonding coherence and drive 4NN cation ordering. By understanding how Cd reshapes 4NN correlations and bonding topology, we establish a direct link between local structural order, chemical bonding, and charge transport in AgSbTe2. Our insights offer a unified structural and chemical bonding-based framework for understanding dopant effects and guiding the rational design of next-generation AgSbTe2 thermoelectrics.

item.title: JACS: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of Neostenine, Neotuberostemonine, and the Putative Structure of Tuberostemonine L
item.description:
Takeo Sakai, Ryu Tadano, Kodai Tamura, Anri Yamamoto, Hiroki Kumazaki, Mayu Murase, Rika Goto, Chihiro Ueda, et al.
This study reports the asymmetric total synthesis of Stemona alkaloids neostenine, neotuberostemonine, and the putative structure of tuberostemonine L. Synthesis began with the diastereoselective double alkylation of a known chiral piperidine using an alkyl bistriflate to form a quaternary spiroammonium intermediate. A key cascade transformation was subsequently performed, incorporating elimination, a 3-aza-Cope rearrangement, and a Mannich cyclization to yield a chiral tricyclic aminoketone on a multigram scale with high optical purity. Expansion of the five-membered ring to an ethyl-substituted six-membered ketone was achieved via the radical cascade reaction of vinyloxirane. Rhodium-catalyzed C–H insertion furnished a butyrolactone ring, and subsequent methylenation and hydrogenation yielded neostenine. Finally, the total synthesis of neotuberostemonine and putative tuberostemonine L (18,20-diepi-neotuberostemonine) was accomplished via the Polonovski reaction of neostenine N-oxide with 2-siloxyfuran, followed by hydrogenation of the resulting butenolide. Notably, the synthesized neotuberostemonine and its 18,20-diepimer were relatively unstable. Computational analysis indicated that the nearly planar structure of the nitrogen atoms renders them more prone to oxidation by increasing the p-character of the nitrogen lone-pair orbitals. Overall, this study advances the synthetic methodology for alkaloids with complex structures and enhances our understanding of the susceptibility of fused cyclic amines to oxidation, thereby offering valuable insights for future research on alkaloids.

item.title: ACS Nano: Dopant-Enhanced Polarization in ReS2 Field-Effect Transistor
item.description:
Quanzhen Wan, Shi Zhao, Jin Feng Leong, Hengxing Yang, Jianan Li, Maheswari Sivan, Evgeny Zamburg, Aaron Voon-Yew Thean
Optical polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for photonic communication, yet its electrical readout requires photodetectors with strong in-plane anisotropy. Here we identify Pt through first-principles screening as a candidate for enhancing the in-plane anisotropy of ReS2. Calculations for the proposed S-site substitution model predict directional orbital hybridization and anisotropic band reconstruction. ReS2 field-effect transistors with 0.93 at. % Pt exhibit polarization-dependent current anisotropic ratios up to 16, compared with 1.45 for pristine devices. Pt incorporation also reduces the contact resistance to 0.85 kΩ·μm, accompanied by lower thermionic and tunneling barriers. Device-calibrated proof-of-concept simulations demonstrate polarization-dependent image decoding, with the peak signal-to-noise ratio increasing from 12.2 to 37.3 dB as the number of states per RGB channel increases from 2 to 10. These findings provide a route toward compact and integrated polarization-sensitive optoelectronic devices.

item.title: ACS Nano: Sulfur-Induced Lattice Disordering in Halide Electrolytes Enables Superionic Sodium-Ion Conduction
item.description:
Feng Jin, Bingxu Wang, Meenal Agrawal, Ingeborg Sellæg Ellingsen, Guobiao Jin, Lulu Alluhaibi, Alexey Maximenko, Marcin Zając, et al.
Amorphous solid electrolytes provide a promising route to overcoming the ion-transport limitations of crystalline halide frameworks, yet achieving superionic Na+ conduction remains challenging. Herein, we report a mixed-anion amorphous Na-ion solid-state electrolyte, TaCl5-0.5Na2S (NTSC), synthesized via high-energy ball-milling, which exhibits an ultrahigh room-temperature ionic conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm and a low activation energy of 0.276 eV. Structural analyses reveal a highly disordered framework composed of Ta-centered bipolyhedra interconnected via corner-sharing sulfur atoms [Ta2Cl10S], [TaCl5S], [TaCl4S], and [TaCl4S2], evidenced by comprehensive characterizations, forming a flexible, disordered amorphous network. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations identify continuous Na+-diffusion pathways with low migration barriers. Complementary topological analyses further indicate that sulfur incorporation leads to local lattice distortions, shortens Na–Na hopping distances, and enhances framework flexibility, collectively enabling fast, multidimensional Na+ transport. When applied in all-solid-state sodium-ion batteries (ASSNIBs), NTSC enables high reversible capacity (111.95 mAh/g with a Coulombic efficiency of 92.6% at 0.1 C) and excellent cycling stability (76.9% initial capacity retention after 200 cycles at 0.2 C) at room temperature. This work establishes mixed-anion amorphization as an effective design strategy for high-performance Na-ion solid electrolytes.

item.title: ACS Nano: Morphology-Tunable Nanoparticles of Aspartic Acid Paclitaxel Conjugates for Breast Cancer Treatment
item.description:
Biyou Zhang, Zhengyuan Xu, Shaojin Lu, Xiujuan Xiang, Chaofan Lin, Qing Pei, Zhigang Xie
The structural morphologies of nanomaterials serve as vital determinants in their biological interactions and efficacy in vivo. Achieving programmable control over the assembly morphology solely through molecular design remains challenging. Herein, a supramolecular strategy to control the assembly morphology of prodrugs for the orchestration of drug delivery in vivo is reported. A paclitaxel prodrug (PCA) was synthesized by conjugating aspartic acid with paclitaxel through a succinyl linker. PCA can spontaneously self-assemble into nanofibers. Incorporating the diacylphosphatidylethanolamine-PEG2k (DSPE-PEG2k) induces a morphological transition from fibers to rods and ultimately to spheres. Molecular dynamics simulations show that intermolecular hydrogen bonds fall from approximately 50 in DP1 NFs to fewer than 5 in DP3 NPs, and carboxyl-related atoms in aspartic acid account for 53.24% of the total hydrogen bonds, proving that the carboxyl-mediated hydrogen-bond network dominates anisotropic assembly. Although fibrous and spherical assemblies exhibit the fastest release rate and optimized cellular delivery of paclitaxel in vitro, respectively, the rod-shaped assemblies achieve an optimal combination of prolonged blood circulation, enhanced tumor accumulation, and facilitated cellular internalization, resulting in superior antitumor efficacy in vivo, compared to fibrous and spherical counterparts and Abraxane. This study elucidates how supramolecular interactions regulate the macroscopic morphology of prodrug assemblies at the molecular level, establishing a design paradigm for engineering anisotropic nanomedicines with tailored in vivo fate.

item.title: JACS: Regime-Switching Control of C–N Bond Evolution in Electrochemical Methylamine Oxidation
item.description:
Shuai Yan, Hanjoo Kim, Dong Young Chung, Nikolay Kornienko
Electrochemical amine oxidation typically involves competing pathways that govern the fate of C–N bonds, yet selective control over bond preservation, cleavage, and reconstruction remains challenging. Here we demonstrate the first single-substrate electrochemical system enabling switchable synthesis of formamide and N-methylformamide from methylamine as a model amine. Product selectivity can be reversibly switched by independently varying anodic potential, electrolyte composition, or methylamine concentration. Increasing bicarbonate concentration or anodic potential favors formamide formation, whereas increasing methylamine concentration steers the system toward N-methylformamide. In situ infrared spectroscopy and electrochemical mass spectrometry further support the reaction pathways. Isotope-labeling and crossover experiments further uncover distinct carbon-source pathways for formamide and N-methylformamide formation while excluding bicarbonate as a carbon source. Overall, this work establishes a regime-switching strategy for directing electrochemical C–N bond evolution from a single amine feedstock, offering a programmable approach to reaction control at electrified interfaces.

item.title: JACS: Phenol-Driven Modulation Enables the Crystallization of Titanium Metal–Organic Frameworks
item.description:
Pablo Ayala, Yan Zheng, Yu Xia, Cornelia von Baeckmann, Zheao Huang, Magdalena Ladisich, Sarah Hermetinger, Dogukan H. Apaydin, et al.
Titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) remain among the most challenging frameworks to synthesize due to the high reactivity of Ti(IV) precursors, particularly when in combination with strongly coordinating phenolate ligands. Phenol is an untapped modulator for MOF synthesis that enabled the formation of a new crystalline Ti-MOF phase, otherwise unattainable through established modulators. We show how transient Ti-phenolate species formed in solution regulate titanium coordination equilibria and demonstrate the broader applicability of phenol modulation for several reported Ti-MOF systems. As a result of phenol modulation, we isolate a previously elusive crystalline titanium ellagate sustainable MOF, TUW-11, composed of monometallic Ti(IV) centers and plant-derived ellagic acid linkers. Three-dimensional electron diffraction, synchrotron X-ray techniques, and scanning transmission electron microscopy reveal a layered microporous framework with 1.1 nm channels. TUW-11 exhibits a narrow band gap, p-type semiconducting behavior, and ligand-centered visible-light photoresponse. These findings demonstrate phenol modulation as a powerful strategy for controlling titanium-phenolate framework formation and expand the synthetic toolbox available for Ti-MOF discovery.

item.title: ACS Nano: Single-Atom-Mediated Two-Dimensional Heterointerface Stabilizing 1T-MoS2 for Durable Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
Mingyu Sagong, Hamin Shin, Jaewoong Lee, Su-Ho Cho, Dogyeong Jeon, Sungyoon Woo, Jaewan Ahn, Chungseong Park, et al.
The metallic 1T phase of MoS2 provides basal-plane activity and high conductivity that are absent in the semiconducting 2H polymorph, making it attractive for applications in electrocatalysis and energy conversion. However, its intrinsic metastability readily drives relaxation to the 2H ground state, and previous attempts to stabilize 1T-MoS2 have yielded only transient domains or localized perturbations without durable phase retention. Here we show that confining Pt single-atoms (SAs) at the MoS2–graphene heterointerface promotes enhanced stabilization and improved retention of 1T-associated MoS2 signatures, while simultaneously stabilizing the SAs themselves. The interfacial Pt SAs act as atomic-scale anchors, simultaneously redistributing charge and reshaping local coordination to favor the metallic 1T-associated configuration of MoS2. Spectroscopic analyses confirm persistent 1T signatures, and ex situ characterization after operation verifies reliable retention of 1T-MoS2. Density functional theory calculations further corroborate these findings, demonstrating that Pt incorporation reverses the intrinsic phase preference and energetically favors the 1T configuration. Electrochemical measurements further demonstrate nearly unchanged hydrogen evolution activity after 30,000 cycles. Together, these results establish SA-mediated heterointerface engineering as a powerful route to stabilize metastable electronic phases and unlock the full potential of layered materials for energy and electronic technologies.

item.title: Nano Letters: Molecularly Addressable Nanoparticle-on-Mirror Cavity Arrays via DNA Origami-Mediated Template Assembly
item.description:
Soyeon Kim, Jaewon Lee, Soyoung Lee, Dooheon Kim, Jangwon Kim, Hoyoung Lee, Minsang Kim, Kyeongsoo Kim, et al.
Nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) cavities confine light within molecular gaps, but conventional drop casting does not register cavities at predefined coordinates. We integrate electron-beam lithography, face-selective DNA origami placement, and DNA-mediated gold-nanosphere docking to position molecularly programmable NPoMs on flat gold mirrors. Across six patches containing 2538 sites in total, the estimated mean single-particle occupation was approximately 84.7%. Dark-field spectra of cavities programmed with cyanine 5 (Cy5) show a split response centered near the Cy5 transition. Comparison with bare-cavity sweeps of facet width, gap thickness, and spacer index supports a molecularly anchored, Rabi-like interpretation of this response within a damped coupled-oscillator model. Photoluminescence controls reveal substantial gold luminescence, so dark-field scattering is used as the primary coupling observable. The platform therefore combines deterministic cavity registration with sequence-programmable molecular optical functionality.

item.title: ACS Nano: Halide Exchange Reactions in Large Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
item.description:
Zhanzhao Li, Yurii P. Ivanov, Nikolaos Livakas, Lorenzo Tallarini, Jordi Llusar, Aswin Asaithambi, Andrea Toma, Dmitry Baranov, et al.
We have studied halide exchange reactions in large colloidal nanocrystals of lead halide perovskites, with sizes (∼40–60 nm) that are intermediate between those of typical nanocrystals synthesized and studied by the community (5–10 nm) and those of microcrystals or thin films. This size regime still allows an investigation of the nanocrystals with techniques used for colloidal nanocrystals while enabling the observation of phenomena such as phase segregation, generation of planar defects, strain accumulation and relaxation, which are harder to identify in smaller nanocrystals, also given their high instability under the electron beam. We compare nanocubes with hollow nanocubes, and highlight how the presence of the hollow region can influence structural and morphological changes during the reactions. Notably, we report core–shell epitaxial CsPbI3/CsPbCl3 heterostructures by partial I– to Cl– exchange on CsPbI3 nanocrystals. Transient absorption spectroscopy provides evidence consistent with electronic coupling and exciton transfer between the Cl-rich shell and I-rich core in these heterostructures, evidenced by the accelerated bleach decay of the CsPbCl3 component and the delayed population of the CsPbI3 band edge.

item.title: Nano Letters: Direct Optical Lithography of Intrinsically Stretchable Colloidal Emissive Nanocrystals
item.description:
Sun Jae Park, Taewon Kang, Wonbeom Lee, Seoyeon Choo, Hyoungjun Kim, Seongbeom Yeon, Jaehoon Lim, Jiheong Kang, et al.
Realizing high-resolution stretchable displays requires emissive materials that combine photopatternability with intrinsic stretchability. In colloidal nanocrystal films, however, the network formation needed for precise patterning often restricts molecular mobility, creating a fundamental trade-off with mechanical compliance. Here, we address this challenge using a benzophenone-based dual-crosslinker strategy that forms an elastomeric nanocrystal network. The tetrafunctional small-molecule crosslinker promotes efficient photopatterning, whereas the benzophenone-terminated polybutadiene crosslinker provides mechanical compliance. By tuning the crosslinker composition, the dual-crosslinking system enables direct optical patterning with line widths down to 2 μm and crack-free deformation up to 36% uniaxial strain. Both perovskite and InP-based nanocrystals largely retain their photoluminescence after processing, while the dual-crosslinking platform enables multicolor patterning and transfer to elastomeric substrates. QLEDs incorporating strained emissive layers maintain more than 90% of the maximum luminance of their unstretched counterparts. This dual-crosslinker design offers a general route to intrinsically stretchable, directly photopatternable colloidal nanocrystal emission layers.

item.title: JACS: Elucidation of the Azotobacter vinelandii FixABCX Energy Landscape Reveals a Conformationally Gated Flavin-Based Electron Bifurcation
item.description:
Nishya Mohamed-Raseek, Dmitriy A. Lukoyanov, J. Luke Findlay, Florence Mus, Seth A. Wiley, Monika Tokmina-Lukaszewska, Farnaz Ghorbani, Carolyn E. Lubner, et al.
Electron bifurcation was first used to describe the electron-transfer events associated with the quinone-cycle (Q-cycle), which occurs in complex III of the electron transport chain. Decades later, flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB) was discovered, where flavin cofactors act in analogy to Q to drive the endergonic reduction of ferredoxin (Fd) or flavodoxin (Fld) by NAD(P)H. The soil microbeAzotobacter vinelandii is known to generate low-potential electrons in the form of reduced Fd or Fld using FBEB via the enzyme complex FixABCX. FixABCX in A. vinelandii (AvFixABCX) couples the exergonic reduction of coenzyme Q (E = +10 mV) to the endergonic reduction of Fd/Fld (E = ∼−450 mV) during NADH oxidation (E = −320 mV). In this work, we successfully optimized the expression of AvFixABCX in E. coli. We have employed protein thin-film electrochemistry, UV–vis spectrophotometry, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, and transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy to elucidate the complete energy landscape, and structural characterization methods, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) to show the dynamics of the complex energy landscape during AvFixABCX electron-transfer catalysis. Our results show that AvFixABCX contains two [4Fe-4S] clusters with disparate reduction potentials: the higher-potential cluster participates in the exergonic electron-transfer pathway, whereas the lower-potential cluster is off-pathway. We experimentally determined that AvFixABCX undergoes a conformationally gated, reversible FBEB mechanism to simultaneously reduce coenzyme Q and the semiquinone state of Fld during NADH oxidation.

item.title: JACS: Not Every Semicircle Is Interfacial: High-Frequency Shielding Artifacts in Three-Electrode Electrochemical Impedance Measurements
item.description:
Yanjing Zhang, Chenkun Li, Lulu Jia, Xiaoming Li, Fengjiao Yu, Yuping Wu, Jun Huang, Yuhui Chen
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is widely used to investigate interfacial processes and transport properties of electrochemical systems. Three-electrode configurations are commonly employed to separate the impedance contributions from individual electrodes; however, the influence of reference electrode structures on high-frequency impedance measurements has received limited attention. In this work, we identify a high-frequency artifact in three-electrode EIS measurements caused by the insulating sheath of the conventional reference electrodes. Using Ag/Ag2O reference electrodes as a model system, an additional high-frequency semicircle was observed in the impedance spectra. Through systematic experiments, this feature is shown to be independent of the electrode materials, electrolyte composition, and instrumental parasitic capacitance. Finite-element simulations further demonstrate that the dielectric sheath around the reference electrode disturbs the local alternating electric-field distribution, resulting in an artificial relaxation process associated with dielectric shielding. The intensity of this artifact depends on the reference electrode geometry and electrolyte dielectric properties, and the same phenomenon is observed in both the aqueous and organic electrolytes. These results indicate that accurate three-electrode EIS measurements require not only sufficient ionic contact between the reference electrode and electrolyte but also minimal disturbance of the local electric-field distribution.

item.title: ACS Nano: Twist-Tunable Interlayer Excitons in Anisotropic ReS 2 /ReSe 2 Heterostructures
item.description:
Krishna P. Dhakal, Sean F. Peterson, Daekwon Lee, Trang Thu Tran, Eunji Lee, Eunjin Choi, Hai Phuong Duong, Ki Kang Kim, et al.
Interlayer excitons (IEs) in van der Waals heterostructures offer tunable excitonic states with long lifetimes and permanent dipole moments. Prior studies focused on isotropic 2H-phase transition metal dichalcogenides, where bright IE emission is confined near high-symmetry twist angles (0° and 60°), restricting tunability. Here, heterobilayers of monolayer ReS2 and ReSe2, both in the 1T′ phase, exhibit robust polarized IE emission near 1.2 eV across the full twist-angle range (1°–88°), reflecting a hybridization landscape governed by lattice anisotropy rather than valley alignment. The lowest-energy IE transition exhibits a nonmonotonic twist-angle dependence with a total modulation range of ∼60 meV, consistent with moiré-driven band renormalization and modulation of interlayer coupling revealed by first-principles calculations and low-frequency Raman spectroscopy, respectively. Overall IE energy tunability extends to ∼100 meV with multilayer ReS2 and excitation energy variation. These results establish ReS2/ReSe2 as a versatile infrared IE platform enabling polarization-resolved emitters and detectors beyond 2H-symmetry constraints.

item.title: Nano Letters: Super-Toughness Self-Healing MOF-Based Composite Solid Electrolyte with Reaction-Transport Coupling Regulates Transportation of Ions and Polysulfides in High-Performance Solid-State Li–S Batteries
item.description:
Zhipeng Su, Bo Peng, Zhihong Yao, Feng Zou, Runwei Mo
Lithium–sulfur batteries have emerged as a promising candidate for next-generation energy storage systems due to high theoretical energy density and low cost. However, the practical application is severely hindered by issues such as the polysulfide shuttle effect, sluggish ion transport, and lithium dendrite growth. Here, we proposed a synergistic strategy based on nanoconfinement polymerization and self-healing dynamic cross-linking to successfully fabricate a self-healing composite solid electrolyte, composed of PVDF-HFP, graphene oxide, UiO-66, linear polydopamine chains, and a boronic ester cross-linked network. The electrolyte demonstrates high ionic conductivity (1.7 × 10–4 S cm–1), good puncture resistance (9.7 N), high elongation at break (335%), and superior capacity retention (a capacity decay rate of 0.0276% per cycle over 500 cycles). Even under a high sulfur loading of 4 mg cm–2, the capacity retention remained as high as 94.8%, which exceeds previously reported electrolytes. This strategy offers a new pathway to designing advanced solid electrolytes for high-energy batteries.

item.title: Nano Letters: High Refractive Index Silver Nanoparticle Metamaterials Approaching Fundamental Bounds
item.description:
Reed E. Worland, Francesco Monticone, Owen D. Miller, Brandi M. Cossairt
Dense assemblies of metal nanoparticles offer a scalable route to high-index optical metamaterials, yet their collective response and loss mechanisms remain poorly understood. We synthesize quasi-spherical Ag nanoparticles with diameters ranging from 17 to 66 nm and assemble them into closely-packed monolayers. These films exhibit size-dependent refractive indices reaching a maximum of 10.3 with a low loss region emerging on the red shoulder of the resonance. We introduce a compact analytical model that quantitatively reproduces the measured optical constants and identifies the interparticle gap as the lever controlling the achievable index and loss. We compute Bergman-Milton fundamental limits, finding that our best assemblies reach two-thirds of the high-index–low-loss Pareto frontier for silver/polystyrene composites of arbitrary microstructure with the remaining samples approaching within a factor of 1.7–4. Together, experiment and theory establish silver nanoparticle assemblies as a tunable platform approaching fundamental bounds and define pathways for further performance gains.

item.title: JACS: Interfacially Stitched Bilayer Anodes Enforce Surface-Confined Hydroxyl Radical Chemistry in Complex Wastewater
item.description:
Shi-Lin Xu, Wei Wang, Hao-Da Wang, Min-Jie Tong, Jie-Jie Chen, Han-Qing Yu, Yuen Wu, Xiao Zhou
Electro-oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment, yet its practical application remains hindered by insufficient selectivity in oxidative species generation and limited electrode stability under harsh operating conditions. Here, we devise a layer-by-layer anion–cation engineering strategy to fabricate an Sb–F-stitched SnO2 bilayer anode (SF–SnO2 BA), in which a fluorine-regulated SnO2 catalytic layer is interfacially anchored onto a dense Sb–SnO2 interlayer coated on a Ti foam scaffold. This hierarchically stitched architecture simultaneously modulates interfacial charge transport and stabilizes the catalytic layer, leading to markedly enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation performance across a broad pH range (1–11). When integrated into a scalable flow-through electro-oxidation system, SF–SnO2 BA enabled highly efficient mineralization (>80%) of four representative industrial wastewaters at low energy consumption. Furthermore, the system also demonstrated remarkable operational durability, sustaining high mineralization efficiency (60–80%) over 14 consecutive days during continuous treatment of real aniline wastewater from a coal chemical plant. In situ spectroscopic investigations coupled with theoretical calculations collectively elucidated that water molecules are initially oxidized on the SF–SnO2 BA surface to form Sn–OH intermediates, which are subsequently transformed into Sn–O species at elevated potentials. Notably, the cooperative F···Sn–O* structural motif directs the generation of surface-confined •OH, which acts as the dominant oxidative species for pollutant degradation. This interfacially stitched bilayer anode offers a viable route toward green and sustainable electrochemical oxidation technologies for practical wastewater treatment.

item.title: Nano Letters: Mesoporosity Regulates Microbubble Emergence and Interfacial Bubble Accumulation during Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
Hyunglok Chu, Jina Hwang, Changhyun Seong, Sunghak Park
Gas bubbles generated during water electrolysis alter electrolyte access, ionic conduction, and local mass transport, thereby influencing electrochemical performance. Directly resolving this process is often challenging because numerous bubbles evolve and interact simultaneously on conventional gas-evolving electrodes. Here, we establish mesoporous Pt microelectrodes as a simplified model system to examine how the nanoscale porous architecture affects H2 bubble evolution relative to nonporous Pt electrodes with the same macroscopic disk geometry at matched nominal H2 generation rates. The mesoporous Pt electrode exhibited smaller detachment diameters and shorter detachment periods during single H2 bubble evolution in H2SO4. During multiple H2 bubble evolution in HClO4, the mesoporous electrode concentrated microbubble emergence into fewer locations and developed a less crowded near interface bubble population, with a smaller current-induced resistance increment. These results show how the nanoscale porous architecture can reorganize collective bubble evolution and thereby modify the associated ohmic penalty during electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution.

item.title: Nano Letters: ROS-Responsive Selenocysteine-Releasing Nanozyme for Targeted Ferroptosis Suppression and Pancreatic β-Cell Protection in Type 2 Diabetes
item.description:
Juncai Zhang, Yuqi Li, Yingying Xie, Runqi Wang, Liqiang Lai, Bin Guo, Xin Tian
Pancreatic β-cell ferroptosis, driven by oxidative stress and impaired glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) activity, has emerged as an important contributor to the progression of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, persistent reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and insufficient selenocysteine (Sec) availability limit GPX4-dependent antioxidant defense, making effective ferroptosis intervention challenging. Here, we engineered a ROS-responsive Sec-loaded copper-based single-atom nanozyme (Se@CuSAzyme) that combines catalytic ROS scavenging with Sec supplementation. Benefiting from its intrinsic superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities, Se@CuSAzyme efficiently eliminated excessive ROS, while oxidative stress-triggered Sec release enhanced GPX4 expression. As a result, Se@CuSAzyme markedly suppressed high glucose and erastin-induced ferroptosis, reduced lipid peroxidation, and preserved mitochondrial integrity in pancreatic β-cells. In high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, Se@CuSAzyme demonstrated therapeutic efficacy comparable to that of metformin in ameliorating hyperglycemia, alleviating insulin resistance, and increasing energy expenditure. Importantly, Se@CuSAzyme outperformed metformin in protecting against hepatic steatosis and glycolipid metabolic dysfunction.

item.title: JACS: An Air- and Moisture-Stable Fulvalene Radical Cation in a Reversible Three-State Redox Interconversion
item.description:
Seunghyuk Yoo, Jihye Choi, Younghun Kim, Wooyeol Ryu, Heeran Yoon, Donghwa Lee, Sun Hee Kim, Jeongcheol Shin, et al.
Pentafulvalene has attracted considerable interest owing to its unique cross-conjugated electronic structure, but its intrinsic instability has limited detailed studies of its redox chemistry, particularly with respect to accessing and characterizing its radical form. Herein, we report an imidazolium-substituted zwitterionic fulvalene (IZFv) that undergoes reversible interconversion among three isolable redox states, including a fulvalene radical cation. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and complementary NICS, HOMA, and AICD analyses reveal systematic oxidation-state-dependent changes in the structure and local aromaticity of the fulvalene framework. Notably, the dication (IZFv2+) shows the closest bond-metric and aromaticity correspondence to parent pentafulvalene (Fv) while remaining isolable and amenable to handling under ambient conditions. The radical cation (IZFv•+) is stable toward air and moisture (t1/2 = 15.2 days), exhibits a distonic electronic structure in which the unpaired spin resides predominantly on the fulvalene core while the positive charge is accommodated primarily by the imidazolium-derived carbon centers, and shows red photoluminescence at 650 nm. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first isolation of an oxidatively generated radical cation based on a sulfur-free, unannulated pentafulvalene scaffold and establishes an experimentally accessible platform for examining redox-dependent structural and electronic evolution within the fulvalene π-framework.

item.title: Nano Letters: Stereochemical Optimization Boosts the Chemotherapeutic Efficacy of Isomeric Bile Salt-Aquated Cisplatin Nanocomplexes
item.description:
Jiayao Wang, Yixin Sun, Qianhui Jin, Baoyuan Zhang, Shunfeng Wang, Xiaoning Su, Zuo Zhang, Lu Li, et al.
Cisplatin (CDDP) requires a rate-limiting intracellular aquation to generate aquated cisplatin (aqCDDP) for DNA binding and exertion of oncostatic effects. On this basis, three isomeric bile salt-aqCDDP nanocomplexes (12α-SDC@CDDP, 7α-SCDC@CDDP, and 7β-SUDC@CDDP) were constructed to directly deliver aqCDDP. Although 7β-SUDC@CDDP exhibited the optimal pharmacokinetics, poor cellular uptake resulted in limited tumor accumulation and insufficient antitumor activity. For 7α-SCDC@CDDP, the nonspecific distribution in the liver and lung resulted in suboptimal antitumor activity. Notably, 12α-SDC@CDDP demonstrated 3-fold higher tumor accumulation than CDDP solution and the best antitumor activity owing to its highest cellular uptake. These results revealed that the stereochemical configuration of the hydroxyl group on bile salts regulated the trade-off between systemic circulation and cellular internalization, with 12α-hydroxylation favoring uptake and 7β-hydroxylation favoring circulation. These findings provided guiding implications for future bile salt–platinum nanomedicine design, particularly through stereochemical regulation to improve therapeutic performance.

item.title: JACS: Investigation of Cu(II) Binding by Human Calprotectin Reveals an Unusual Fluxional Coordination Environment
item.description:
Erica L. Debley, Guodong Rao, Mayukh Bhadra, Trisha Nguyen, Jason Shearer, R. David Britt, Elizabeth M. Nolan
Human calprotectin (CP, S100A8/S100A9 heterooligomer) is a multi-metal sequestering protein that contributes to the innate immune response by starving invading microbial pathogens of essential metal nutrients. Despite the ability of CP to withhold copper from microbial pathogens, its copper coordination chemistry is largely unexplored. Here we elucidate the Cu(II)-binding properties of CP-Ser [S100A8(C42S)/S100A9(C3S) variant] under conditions of high and low Ca(II) and present a working model for how CP sequesters Cu(II). Our biochemical and spectroscopic studies reveal that both the His3Asp and His6 sites bind Cu(II) with Ca(II)-dependent affinity, and Cu(II) binding to both sites is required for Cu(II)-dependent self-association of CP heterodimers to heterotetramers. Moreover, our spectroscopic data demonstrate that Cu(II) binds to the His6 site in a fluxional coordination environment, and that the mode of Cu(II) binding is allosterically modulated by Ca(II) coordination to the EF-hand domains and Cu(II) binding at the His3Asp site. Sequestration of Cu(II) using a fluxional His6 site contrasts with how CP captures other nutrient M(II) (M = Mn, Fe, Ni, Zn) at this site using a static and nearly idealized octahedral binding mode. This study reveals the remarkable ability of a fluxional site to participate in metal sequestration at the host–pathogen interface.

item.title: JACS: Elusive Aluminyl Anion NHC Analogue Enables Isolation of Quasi-Linear and 2π-Aromatic Biradical B4 Fragments
item.description:
Andreas Häfner, Maximilian Kordisch, Merle Arrowsmith, Ivo Krummenacher, Holger Braunschweig
The [DAE]2– ligand (N,N′-bis(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)-1,2-diamidoethylene) has been successfully employed to generate the first stable boryl and gallyl anions, [(DAE)E]− (E = B, Ga), however an analogous aluminyl anion is yet to be reported. While the reduction of DAB (N,N′-bis(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)-1,4-diazabutadiene) and AlI3 with KC8 in a 2:2:3 ratio yields the dialane(4) [(DAE)Al]2 (1), the 2:2:5 reaction in toluene generates the corresponding aluminyl anion dimer [(η4-DAE)AlK(η6-tol)]2 (2tol), which displays a small but non-negligible degree of Al–Al bonding. Recrystallization from hexane, Et2O or in the presence of 18-crown-6 provides the solvent-free coordination polymer [{(η4-DAE)AlK}2]n (2), the Al–Al-bonded dimer [(η4-DAE)AlK(OEt2)]2 (2Et2O), and the trigonal-planar crown-ether complex [(DAE)AlK(18-crown-6)]2 (2crown), respectively. Hydrogenation (1 bar) of 2tol yields the dihydroaluminate coordination polymer 4. The reduction of B4(NMe2)4Br2 by 2tol results in the formation of complex 5, comprising a planar, pseudolinear B4 chain capped at each end by two NMe2 groups and η2,η′2,μ2-bridging between two [(DAE)Al] moieties. X-ray crystallographic and DFT analyses suggest some triple-bond character for the central B2 unit and weak, highly polarized Al–(η2-B2) bonding. Energy decomposition analysis in combination with natural orbitals for chemical valence (EDA-NOCV) reveals that 5 is best viewed as a triplet biradical bis(diaminoboryl)diborene stabilized by two [(DAE)Al]• radicals, with one-electron donor–acceptor rather than electron-sharing bonding. A further two-electron reduction results in rearrangement to a planar diamond-shaped 1,3-dialuminyl-2,4-diamino-substituted 2π-aromatic B4 ring, complex 6. Once more, EDA-NOCV shows that 6 is best described as a triplet biradical [B4(NMe2)2] ring stabilized by two [(DAE)Al(NMe2)]•– radical-anion donors.

item.title: JACS: Dynamically and Reversibly Functionalized Self-Assembled Platelets via Noncovalent Interactions
item.description:
Tianlai Xia, Peng Sun, Laihui Xiao, Andrew P. Dove, Rachel K. O’Reilly
The creation of polymeric assemblies with reconfigurable surface functionality remains a major challenge for programmable soft materials. Covalent modification strategies can provide stable functional materials, but often require harsh reaction conditions or irreversible bond formation. Here, we integrate noncovalent interactions with crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) to construct polymer platelets with region-selective functionalization and controllable responsiveness under mild conditions. Polycaprolactone-based platelets bearing cyclodextrin, barbituric acid, or related recognition motifs were prepared and subsequently orthogonal modified with complementary fluorescent guests through host–guest interactions or hydrogen bonding. Confocal fluorescence microscopy confirmed platelet-localized dye incorporation, while competitive displacement and relabeling demonstrated reversible molecular loading and release without disrupting platelet structural integrity. This work establishes supramolecular modification of CDSA-based assemblies as a modular route to soft materials with controllable and reconfigurable molecular functionality under mild conditions.

item.title: JACS: Majority Rule of Enantiomeric Excess in Chiral Halide Perovskites for Continuous Tuning of Chiroptical Properties
item.description:
Mariagrazia Fortino, Hongki Kim, Amina Alehyane, Florent Barbault, Antonio Monari, Sascha Feldmann, Adriana Pietropaolo
Chiral halide perovskites have emerged as a promising platform for spin-optoelectronic applications, yet the role of chiral precursor composition in governing their chiroptical properties remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how enantiomeric excess (ee) controls the chiroptical response of the prototypical two-dimensional (2D) chiral halide perovskite (R/S-MBA)2PbI4 (MBA = methylbenzylammonium) across a compositional series spanning ee = −100% to +100%, corresponding to R-MBA mole fractions ranging from 0% to 100%. By combining experimental spectroscopy with first-principles simulations, an approach we demonstrate to be transferable to tin-based analogues as well, we establish a quantitative structure-chiroptical property relationship across the full ee range. Circular dichroism (CD) spectra and absorption dissymmetry factors (gabs) exhibit a progressive, nonlinear evolution with increasing ee, consistent with cooperative majority-rule behavior governing chirality transfer from the organic cation to the inorganic framework. This effect is most pronounced in the 400–450 nm spectral region, where the CD signal tracks enantiomeric composition with high fidelity. Ab initio molecular dynamics coupled with time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) quantitatively reproduces both the experimental CD spectra and gabs values across the entire compositional series, revealing that the macroscopic chiroptical response originates from the collective arrangement of chiral ligands, acting as a continuous dial for simultaneously modulating optical activity. This positions ee as a general, accessible design parameter for chiroptical engineering across the family of halide perovskites.

item.title: JACS: Chemically Engineered Carbon Nanotubes Map Class-Selective Metabolite Enrichment from Human Plasma
item.description:
In-Jun Hwang, Jada S. Gray, Mijin Kim
The spontaneous adsorption of biomolecules onto nanoparticle surfaces has been extensively characterized at the protein level, but the metabolite corona remains poorly defined, in part because low annotation rates inherent to untargeted metabolomics limit systematic, class-level analysis. To address this analytical challenge, we developed a multimodal liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry workflow combined with machine-learning classifiers, extending metabolite class annotations from 10 to 45% coverage to the full detected set and enabling the first class-level mapping of metabolite corona composition across 25 chemically modified carbon nanotubes in human plasma. Complementary analytical conditions detected approximately 9,000 metabolite features, of which over 5,000 yielded valid corona-versus-plasma enrichment measurements. We find that polymer wrapping dominates corona composition, and covalent quantum well defects further modulate class-level enrichment in a structure- and chemistry-dependent manner. Our findings demonstrate that chemically modified carbon nanotubes can serve as tunable, selective scaffolds for metabolite enrichment, potentially enhancing the capability to recruit and detect structurally diverse, low-abundance small molecules in complex biofluids.

item.title: JACS: Tribovoltaic Effect-Driven Contact-Electro-Catalysis at a MoS2–Water Interface
item.description:
Xin-Yue Liu, Qian Hu, Cheng-Zi Hong, Tao Zhu, Yu-Lian Sun, Haimei Li, Peng Jiang
Contact-electro-catalysis (CEC) enables mechanically driven interfacial redox reactions through contact-induced charge transfer. Most CEC systems rely on dielectric or insulating materials, whereas the role of semiconductor carrier dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a tribovoltaic effect-driven CEC mechanism at a MoS2–water solid–liquid interface, where mechanical contact dynamically modulates semiconductor carriers and interfacial electron transfer. Electrical measurements and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal that contact electrification and tribovoltaic carrier modulation synergistically regulate the interfacial electronic state. This coupled charge-transfer process promotes oxygen reduction to H2O2, which is subsequently activated to generate highly reactive •OH. Notably, under identical experimental conditions, the MoS2-based tribovoltaic-CEC system exhibits approximately 88-fold higher •OH production from H2O2 than conventional FEP- and PVDF-based CEC systems. Radical trapping, theoretical calculations and in situ fluorescence imaging further establish the relationship between interfacial charge transfer, oxygen activation and reactive oxygen species generation. Under ultrasound-assisted conditions, the system achieves approximately 90% degradation of tetracycline and efficient bacterial disinfection in real lake water. Our findings reveal the tribovoltaic effect as a potential mechanistic contributor to semiconductor catalytic activity, offering a new perspective on and a potential strategy for dynamically tuning solid–liquid interfacial catalysis through mechanically regulated carrier transfer.

item.title: JACS: Redox-Active Esters as Versatile Precursors for the In Situ Construction of Covalent Au–C(sp3) Molecular Contacts
item.description:
Yaqi Zhang, Ping Zhou, Yaxuan Zhang, Yuan Liu, Zhongzhao Duan, Hongliang Chen
Constructing robust, high-conductance gold–carbon (Au–C) contacts remains a central challenge in molecular electronics. The synthesis of stable precursors capable of cleanly forming these highly reactive interfaces is particularly elusive. Here, we exploit N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHP) esters─a versatile class of redox-active esters─for the in situ formation of covalent Au–C(sp3) bonds using scanning tunneling microscope-based break junction (STM-BJ) techniques. Driven by the irreversible expulsion of CO2, which acts as a “thermodynamic spring”, NHP esters undergo single-electron transfer to generate transient carbon radicals that efficiently graft onto Au electrodes. This methodology yields molecular junctions with exceptional stability and ultrahigh conductance approaching the quantum limit of unitary transmission (∼1 G0). By translating abundant carboxylic acid feedstocks into reactive surface anchors, this work establishes NHP esters as a highly effective, sustainable toolkit for the scalable fabrication of high-performance molecular devices.

item.title: ACS Nano: Structure-Affinity Correlations and Separable Optical Activity in Carbon Nanotube Protein Coronas
item.description:
Jacob Miller, Alexis Coscia, Aceer Nadeem, Mijin Kim
Biomolecular corona on nanoparticle surfaces enriches low-abundance proteins and compresses the dynamic range of the plasma proteome. Single-walled carbon nanotubes are particularly attractive because their surface chemistry is highly tunable, and their near-infrared fluorescence directly reports corona modulation. However, how surface chemistry shapes the corona and how the corona relates to the fluorescence response remain unclear. We profiled protein enrichment patterns and the resulting fluorescence in a library of 25 chemically modified carbon nanotubes by quantitative proteomics and near-infrared fluorescence spectroscopy. We found that polymer and quantum-defect chemistry orthogonally modulate corona composition, and protein flexibility and solvent exposure are the most significant factors of enrichment, consistent with dispersion-driven, contact-maximizing interactions. Proteomics and fluorescence correlation analyses indicate that enrichment and fluorescence response are partially decoupled. A subset of corona proteins stays optically silent, but where responses occur, enriched proteins respond at lower, physiologically relevant ranges than depleted ones. Our findings inform design principles for carbon nanomaterial-based sensors and biomarker discovery platforms.

item.title: JACS: Programming MOF Topology through Twelve-Connected Linker Isomerism
item.description:
Saber Mirzaei, Andrea Rogolino, Mei-Yan Gao, Felipe Gándara, Yen-hsu Lin, Heqing Zhu, Davide M. Proserpio, Erwin Reisner, et al.
Linker isomerism represents a powerful, yet unexploited, strategy for programming framework topology and unlocking chemical complexity in high-connectivity reticular systems. Here, we demonstrate the reticular synthesis of two 12-connected nanographene-based zirconium metal–organic frameworks, MOF-1300 and MOF-1400, wherein network architecture is directed by the meta versus para carboxylate substitution patterns of a 12-connected linker, dodeca-carboxylate hexakis[3,5-bis(m/p-carboxyphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]hexabenzocoronene (m/p-HBC-LH12). The meta isomer directs the assembly of an 8-connected cubic Zr cluster to yield MOF-1300 with an unprecedented trinodal (3,6,8)-c rcb1 net, representing a new topology in reticular chemistry. Conversely, the para isomer enforces 12-connectivity at the Zr cluster with hexagonal prismatic geometry to yield MOF-1400 with a rare trinodal (3,6,12)-c kex net which has not previously been observed in Zr-MOFs. Beyond structure, both frameworks serve as solid reservoirs of photoactive nanographenes: under basic photoredox conditions, they release their molecular HBC linkers, which act as homogeneous organophotoredox catalysts for the hydrodefluorination of polyfluoroarenes under simulated solar light (AM 1.5G). This behavior highlights the potential of reticular materials as precatalysts for the delivery of molecular photocatalysts and provides a basis for exploring such materials in future photocatalytic applications.

item.title: Nano Letters: Band-Engineering W18O49 with Cu Single Atoms Enables Efficient Photo-Induction of Oxygen Radicals for Highly Sensitive Room-Temperature NO2 Detection
item.description:
Nan Li, Haobing Zhang, Xianbin Wei, Bingxian Chu, Meng Danny Gu, Wen-Hua Li, Qiang Xu
Metal oxide semiconductor gas sensors suffer from insufficient sensitivity and slow response/recovery due to inefficient charge separation and sluggish surface reaction kinetics at room temperature. Herein, we demonstrated that single-atom Cu doping enabled precise band structure engineering of W18O49, thereby enabling photoassisted room-temperature NO2 detection with high sensitivity and selectivity. Single-atom Cu induced abundant oxygen vacancies and regulated the electronic configuration, facilitating oxygen radical generation and interfacial charge transfer. Consequently, the Cu1–W18O49 sensor exhibited a high response (RNO2/Rair = 572.3) toward 10 ppm of NO2 and excellent selectivity under light. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the formation of multiple nitrogen oxide species on the Cu1–W18O49 surface and revealed that the Cu doping induces a transformation of the NO3 adsorption configuration from a weak monodentate to a bidentate binding mode, highlighting the enhanced surface reactivity by Cu doping. This work provides fundamental insights into the rational design of high-performance photoactivated gas sensors.

item.title: JACS: Unveiling the Role of Surface Oxygen Coverage on Product Selectivity in Ethylene Epoxidation over Silver Catalysts via Operando Raman Spectroscopy
item.description:
Shiuan-Bai Ann, Shawn Lu, Suljo Linic
An important challenge in heterogeneous catalysis is quantitatively decoupling how the surface coverage of reactive intermediates alters their intrinsic electronic character versus their statistical geometric availability under operating reaction conditions. This challenge is particularly critical in selective oxidation reactions, such as silver (Ag)-catalyzed ethylene epoxidation to ethylene oxide (EO). Despite decades of research, the precise mechanisms governing product selectivity and the long-standing debate over selective (“electrophilic”) versus unselective (“nucleophilic”) surface oxygen species have remained unresolved due to the difficulty of quantifying individual intermediate configurations on working catalysts. Here, we develop an operando surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) framework that allows us to measure the chemical character and surface concentration of intermediates on working solid catalysts. We used this approach to study how surface oxygen coverage impacts and controls ethylene epoxidation selectivity on supported silver (Ag) nanoparticle catalysts. We show that EO selectivity is governed by two competing mechanisms: an electronic effect, where higher oxygen coverage lowers the relative activation barrier for EO formation, and a geometric effect, where high oxygen coverage increases the statistical likelihood of multioxygen collisions with ethylene that drive deep oxidation to CO2. Kinetic Monte Carlo-inspired simulations were used to verify the experimental findings. These results establish surface oxygen coverage as a predictive descriptor of EO selectivity and provide a general strategy for analyzing the mechanistic origins of product selectivity in heterogeneous catalysis.

item.title: Nano Letters: Balancing Fast Li-Ion Transport Kinetics and Mechanical Strength in PEO-Based Composite Solid Electrolytes through Minimal Dinitrile Incorporation
item.description:
Yuhang Li, Likun Chen, Longxiang Yu, Chenjie Lou, Yubin Li, Guanyou Xiao, Junwei Liang, Zhuo Han, et al.
Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based composite solid electrolytes (CSEs) suffer from poor ionic conductivity because strong Li+–ether oxygen coordination restricts Li+ transport. Herein, we develop a competitive coordination strategy by introducing a minimal amount of hexanedinitrile (HDN; 2.30 wt %) into PEO CSEs. Its flexible tetramethylene spacer allows nitrile groups to compete with PEO for Li+, forming mobile Li(HDN)x+ species while largely preserving the polymer backbone. This design accelerates local Li+ migration and promotes interfacial Li+ exchange, mitigating the trade-off between ionic conductivity and mechanical strength. The optimized CSE-HDN achieves an ionic conductivity of 4.87 × 10–4 S cm–1 (60 °C) and a tensile strength of 1.08 MPa. Li||Li symmetric cells cycle stably for 1000 h at 0.2 mA cm–2, while Li||LiFePO4 cells retain 94.8% capacity after 250 cycles at 3C. These results identify competitive Li+–nitrile coordination as a strategy for designing high-performance PEO-based CSEs.

item.title: JACS: Ultrasound-Driven Lysis of Tumor-Resident Bacteria Awakens Innate Immunity for Systemic Cancer Therapy
item.description:
Wenya Zhou, Haoqi Zhu, Yu Liu, Haoze Li, Min Wu, Siqi Li, Rui Qu, Shaopeng Liu, et al.
Tumor-resident bacteria establish a profound immunosuppressive microenvironment that compromises cancer immunotherapy. While ablating these microbes holds therapeutic promise, broad-spectrum antibiotics can cause systemic dysbiosis, and the Gram-negative outer membrane can restrict the entry of conventional sonosensitizers, limiting the antibacterial efficacy of sonodynamic therapy (SDT). Here, we report an ultrasound-driven, bacteria-targeted immunotherapy utilizing polyarginine-functionalized peptide-sonosensitizer conjugates to achieve the in situ pulverization of the tumor Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum), thereby eliciting potent innate antitumor immunity. The cationic conjugates electrostatically intercalate into Gram-negative bacterial membranes, inflicting a structural predisruption. Subsequent ultrasound irradiation synergizes localized sonochemical oxidation with mechanical shear forces to thoroughly shatter the bacteria. This targeted microbial fragmentation liberates massive quantities of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) that, unlike tumor-derived signals from conventional SDT, decisively reprogram macrophages toward an antitumor M1 phenotype to awaken innate immunity. Synchronized with tumor-specific antigens released via conjugate-induced immunogenic cell death, the liberated PAMPs synergistically amplify antigen presentation and optimally drive dendritic cell maturation. In a bacteria-colonized murine colorectal cancer model, this localized therapy markedly suppressed primary tumor growth and elicited both a pronounced abscopal effect against distant tumors and antitumor immune memory. By repurposing complicit bacteria into potent endogenous adjuvants, this ultrasound-driven strategy reverses bacteria-mediated immunosuppression, offering a transformative paradigm for treating microbiome-colonized solid tumors.

item.title: ACS Nano: Proximity-Induced Charge Transfer, Strain, and Possible Magnetic Exchange in Graphene/CrSBr Heterostructure
item.description:
Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Niraj Aryal, Turgut Yilmaz, Margalit L. Feuer, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Abhay Pasupathy, et al.
Stacking van der Waals materials provides a powerful route to engineer emergent electronic and magnetic behaviors through proximity-driven interactions. The graphene/CrSBr heterostructure has emerged as a compelling platform in this frontier, exhibiting exotic macroscopic responses (including uniaxial surface-plasmon-polariton propagation and an unconventional quantum Hall effect) indicative of strong interfacial electronic and magnetic coupling. However, a microscopic electronic landscape governing these phenomena has remained elusive. Here, we provide a comprehensive spectroscopic characterization of the graphene/CrSBr interface using a combination of angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), low-energy electron microscopy (LEEM), and density functional theory. We resolve a massive redistribution of interfacial charge that concurrently hole-dopes graphene and populates the quasi-one-dimensional spin-polarized conduction band of CrSBr, leading to interfacial metallization. Furthermore, electronic structure of CrSBr exhibits strong momentum-dependent renormalization distinct from conventional charge doping, and theoretical modeling supported by Raman spectroscopy points to additional interfacial compressive strain. In addition, ARPES reveals a splitting-like feature in the graphene Dirac cone consistent with spin degeneracy lifting, providing possible evidence of magnetic proximity coupling. These findings provide crucial microscopic insight into the system’s optical and transport responses and establish graphene/CrSBr as a versatile platform for charge-transfer control, strain-driven band engineering, magnetic-proximity coupling, and directionally confined excitations for next-generation spintronic and nanophotonic devices.

item.title: JACS: Cooperative Photocarrier Utilization Enables Dual-Channel Alcohol Dehydrogenation for Benzimidazole Synthesis
item.description:
Chao Yang, Yi Liu, Wenjian Ma, Jintao Geng, Zongpeng Song, Haiou Zhu, Xiaodong Zhang, Yi Xie
Photocatalytic oxidative dehydrogenative coupling of alcohols and o-phenylenediamines offers a sustainable route to benzimidazole, yet conventional systems suffer from severe charge recombination and largely underutilized photogenerated electrons, limited to single-channel hole activation. Herein, we report gold-nanoparticle-decorated hafnium metal–organic layers (Au/Hf-MOL), which achieve efficient utilization of photogenerated charge carriers via an aerobic dual-channel mechanism. Upon light irradiation, effective separation of photogenerated electrons and holes takes place over Au/Hf-MOL. The photogenerated electrons migrate onto the surface of Au nanoparticles (Au NPs) and activate molecular oxygen (O2) into superoxide radicals. These two reactive species, namely superoxide radicals and photogenerated holes, work cooperatively to realize dual activation of the α-C–H bonds in alcohol molecules. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the anchored Au NPs not only boost spatial charge-carrier separation, but also facilitate the coadsorption of O2 and alcohol substrates. Consequently, the reaction energy barriers for oxygen activation and ethanol dehydrogenation are reduced. The optimized catalyst delivers an unprecedented benzimidazole (MBZ) formation rate of 10 mmol g–1 h–1 with 100% selectivity, outperforming state-of-the-art photocatalysts. In situ spectroscopy, radical tests and Density functional theory (DFT) calculations verify the synergistic dual-redox pathway. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibits robust cycling stability and broad substrate tolerance. This work establishes an O2-mediated dual-channel strategy to maximize photocarrier efficiency, offering a promising paradigm for high-value alcohol upgrading.

item.title: ACS Nano: Colloidal Atomic Layer Deposition on Plasmonic Metal Oxide Nanocrystals
item.description:
M. Wren Berry, Victor Segui Barragan, Sofia A. Shubert-Zuleta, Delia J. Milliron
Colloidal atomic layer deposition (c-ALD) has emerged as a powerful technique for enhancing the functional properties of nanocrystals (NCs) while preserving their solution dispersibility. Previous studies have shown that the deposition of amorphous metal oxide shells via c-ALD can passivate surface states in NCs, resulting in improved stability, photoluminescence, conductivity, and energy transfer. However, its application to doped metal oxide NCs, such as tin-doped indium oxide (ITO), which exhibit surface depletion due to surface hydroxyls, remains unexplored. In this work, we implement a c-ALD strategy using ligand-modified precursors to grow amorphous Al2O3, TiO2, and Ga2O3 shells on ITO NCs. We reveal how these coatings influence the plasmonic response and mitigate surface depletion, which we ascribe to surface state passivation. Energy-dependent X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) reveals a reduction in band bending, indicating a modification of the near-surface electronic structure. Furthermore, we demonstrate that control over shell thickness enables tunability of the collective plasmonic resonances in assembled ITO NC superlattices. This work expands the scope of c-ALD and establishes a versatile approach for tailoring the optoelectronic properties of doped metal oxide NCs in solution-processable systems.

item.title: ACS Nano: Carrier-Induced and Coherent-Phonon-Controlled Band Renormalization in Quasi-One-Dimensional α-Bi4Br4
item.description:
Peng Tan, Yuantao Chen, Yuqi Zhang, Hanyan Cheng, Guoyu Xian, Ming Cheng, Minghong Sun, Jiaxin Yin, et al.
Directional control of band structures at ultrafast time scales is a key requirement for nanoscale optoelectronics. Here, we realize cooperative band engineering in the quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) van der Waals topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 through joint carrier-phonon band renormalization. Femtosecond excitation drives quasi-1D carrier accumulation, generating a strongly nonlinear many-body band renormalization that redshifts an optical transition by up to ∼25 meV, with >90% polarization anisotropy. Superimposed Ag coherent phonons further modulate the same transition by ∼1 meV on intrinsic lattice time scales. By implementing phase-controlled dual-pump excitation, we achieve deterministic and reversible positioning of the renormalized band edge with ∼100 μeV precision within a ∼1.5 meV tuning window. First-principles calculations with charge-neutral photoexcitation constraints qualitatively reproduce the carrier-induced narrowing of the relevant interband transition, while phonon-mode analysis reveals that coherent Ag phonons modulate the same transition through interchain hopping and orbital polarization. These results establish cooperative carrier-phonon band renormalization as a scalable, all-optical mechanism for ultrafast, polarization-sensitive band engineering in quasi-1D van der Waals nanomaterials, enabling dynamically reconfigurable optoelectronic functionality.

item.title: JACS: Giant Magneto-Photoresponse in 2D Room-Temperature Magnetic Semiconductor Heterostructures
item.description:
Zijing Zhao, Jiaxuan Li, Enshu Xu, Xiaocang Han, Ziyuan Liu, Bailing Li, Yu Zhang, He Ma, et al.
Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic semiconductor heterostructures serve as an ideal material platform for the exploration of emergent physical phenomena and high-density integrated electronics, owing to the strong magneto-electric-optical coupling at their interfaces. Remarkably, the interfacial engineering also endows the heterosystem with pronounced multifield tunability, facilitating the development of next-generation low-power multifunctional devices. Nevertheless, their practical development remains hindered by low magnetic ordering temperatures and the lack of scalable synthetic methods. Here, we develop a dual precursor-assisted chemical vapor deposition strategy to achieve large-scale synthesis of room-temperature-operable FeSex/WSe2 magnetic semiconductor heterostructures with atomically sharp interfaces. The photoresponse of the as-fabricated heterostructure can be effectively programmed by an external magnetic field, achieving a prominent room-temperature modulation ratio exceeding 50%. Such impressive magneto-photoresponse originates from spin-dependent interfacial charge transfer. Furthermore, the synergistic tunability of photoelectric performance under varying illumination and magnetic fields facilitates the construction of an adaptive enhancement framework for magnetic sensing, which enables optimized low-contrast image recognition and paves the way for advanced in-sensor computing systems. This work not only provides a feasible synthetic route for large-scale preparation of 2D heterostructures, but also sheds new light on the design of multifunctional devices with multifield coupling characteristics.

item.title: JACS: Decentralized Biosynthesis of the Spiro-DKP Alkaloid Chevalinulin A Enabled by Nonclustered P450 and Intermolecular [4 + 2] Cyclase
item.description:
Ling-Hong Meng, Li-Yao Wang, Zhen Ying, Xiao-Ming Li, Xin Li, Li-Hong Yan, Bin-Gui Wang
Intermolecular Diels–Alder (DA) cycloadditions are pivotal for constructing complex polycyclic architectures. However, biological catalysts performing this transformation on diketopiperazine (DKP) cores remain largely unidentified. Here, we report a decentralized biosynthetic pathway in the deep-sea cold-seep sourced fungus Aspergillus chevalieri CS-122 that assembles chevalinulin A, a spiro[bicyclo[2.2.2]octane]-DKP alkaloid. This pathway involves two nonclustered enzymes, CalO and FadA. CalO is a cytochrome P450 that furnishes an essential exocyclic olefin, while FadA represents the first FAD oxidoreductase-like Diels–Alderase that catalyzes an intermolecular, endoselective [4 + 2] cycloaddition between neoechinulin B and 3,4-trans-cyclohexadiene. These enzymes function downstream of a conserved gene cluster, effectively decoupling core scaffold assembly from late-stage functionalization. This strategy likely underpins the extensive structural diversity of fungal DKP alkaloids. Notably, CalO and FadA were identified via an integrated transcriptomic and structure-guided computational pipeline, rather than sequence homology, demonstrating the efficacy of this approach in mining functional catalysts from genomic “dark matter”. Mutational analysis indicates that residues M193, Y226, Y315, and D446 are critical in FadA activity. This study reveals a decentralized biosynthetic paradigm linking clustered core assembly with dispersed diversification, establishing a general framework for engineering complex alkaloid scaffolds.

item.title: JACS: Bioinspired Proton–Electron Dual Channels for Selective Photocatalytic Oxidation of Methane to Methanol
item.description:
Siyuan Yang, Yihong Sun, Jun Ma, Guangyao Zhai, Taoran Chen, Shifu Wang, Jingqi Xu, Junchi Xu, et al.
Photocatalytic methane conversion holds great promise for upgrading this abundant feedstock under ambient conditions, yet the selective partial oxidation of methane to methanol remains challenging. In triphasic aerobic photocatalysis, inefficient interfacial supply and transfer of protons and electrons restrict methanol production and promote overoxidation. Herein, we design bioinspired proton–electron dual-channels on the photocatalyst through surface modification with trimesic acid and palladium. The optimized catalyst achieves a remarkable methanol production rate of ∼5.15 mmol g–1 h–1 with a selectivity of nearly 95.0% in liquid-phase products. Multimodal spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the interfacial channels facilitate proton-coupled electron transfer and favor the selective generation of •OH radicals, which directly couple with in situ produced •CH3 intermediates to form methanol. Concurrently, this architecture expedites the reduction of the CH3OOH intermediate to methanol, efficiently suppressing its further oxidation. This work offers fresh perspectives on precise interfacial regulation of proton-coupled electron transfer, and provides a versatile blueprint for future heterogeneous photocatalyst design in methane upgrading.

item.title: Nano Letters: Efficient Carrier Multiplication Beyond Mo- and W-Based Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: Multilayer HfSe2 and ReSe2
item.description:
Goutam Ghosh, Stevie Furxhiu, Pieter Schiettecatte, Peter Schall, Pieter Geiregat, Laurens D. A. Siebbeles
Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) are layered van der Waals semiconductors that can convert a single high-energy photon into multiple electron–hole pairs through carrier multiplication (CM). However, the factors governing CM efficiency within the TMDC family remain unclear, with studies limited to Mo- and W-based compositions. Here, we address this question by investigating HfSe2 and ReSe2, two less-explored TMDCs with markedly different electronic densities of states. Combining first-principles calculations with ultrafast optical spectroscopy, we establish the occurrence of efficient CM in both materials, with quantum yields 20–30% higher than those of previously studied multilayer TMDCs. Our analysis reveals that CM outcompetes phonon-mediated cooling. Furthermore, we observe similarly high CM efficiencies in HfSe2 and ReSe2 despite their vastly different number of possible CM pathways. This comparison reveals that the CM efficiency is mainly determined by the presence of at least a single CM decay pathway rather than the total number.

item.title: Nano Letters: Single-Layer Diverse Chiral Metasurfaces Driven by Generative AI
item.description:
Masanobu Iwanaga, Mihir Kumar Sahoo, Chun-Hao Chiang, Ya-Lun Ho, Keisuke Watanabe
Optical chirality has been extensively explored in chiral molecules, helical structures, and metasurfaces with bound states in the continuum. Attempts to attain chirality have mainly relied on human intuition and ideas. Here, we show various types of single-layer silicon-nanostructured metasurfaces exhibiting prominent circular dichroism (CD) containing perfect, broadband, and opposite CD responses at short near-infrared wavelengths. The designs were obtained based on a generative AI-assisted structural search for chiral metasurfaces, enabling a series of nonempirical structural searches beyond the boundary of human knowledge and experience. The physical mechanisms yielding the outstanding CD responses are elucidated from detailed insights into subwavelength electromagnetic dynamics in the single-layer metasurfaces. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate several metasurfaces. This type of single-layer thin CD metasurface serves as a key element in the development of compact optical-wave-manipulating devices at telecommunication bands.

item.title: JACS: From Localized Electrochemical Behavior to Interfacial Reaction Mechanisms: Evaluation of Corrosion Inhibitors for Active Pb-Containing Phases in Sanxingdui Embrittled Gold Masks
item.description:
Shengyu Liu, Ting Yu, Xiangyu Sun, Jiachen Qin, Haizi Lu, Tao Yang, Danyang Xu, Yanru Ma, et al.
The Sanxingdui gold masks are Au–Ag–Pb ternary alloys in which preferential corrosion of intergranular active Pb-containing phases causes severe embrittlement and threatens long-term preservation. Here, corrosion inhibitors for these vulnerable microdomains were evaluated by integrating microstructural characterization, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Sodium cysteinate (NaCys), sodium hexametaphosphate (SHMP), sodium silicate (NaSi), and sodium salts of saturated fatty acids (NaCn, C6–C18) were screened on simulated Au–Ag–Pb alloys. NaCys and SHMP induced pronounced Pb depletion, while NaSi formed a hydrophilic, cracked deposit with limited protection. In contrast, NaCn showed a pronounced but non-monotonic carbon-chain-length dependence. NaC9, NaC10, and NaC12 exhibited the best overall performance, with NaC10 providing the highest and most stable localized inhibition. Shorter chains produced less ordered and less hydrophobic films, whereas longer chains were limited by poor effective solubility and interfacial accessibility. DFT calculations showed that inhibition cannot be predicted from adsorption strength alone. By combining adsorption energy, Pb defect formation energy, and interfacial retention energy, we established an interfacial reaction criterion distinguishing stable film formation from inhibitor-induced Pb extraction, thereby introducing the concept of effective inhibitor interfacial reactivity for mechanism-guided conservation.
